Become a free MediaPost member now to read this article Unlimited articles every day Keep up-to-date with media, marketing and advertising news Invitations to exclusive industry events and research Subscribe to MediaDailyNews Amazon Lets Advertisers Use ChatGPT Via OpenAI Partnership by Laurie Sullivan , September 10, 2026 Amazon announced a partnership with OpenAI on Thursday to allow its advertisers to run ads in ChatGPT, starting with select brands in the U.S. Previously, the marketplace had been restricting access to its web store from artificial intelligence (AI) platforms like ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini, while it built its own shopping tools. Through the new integration, Amazon Ads will enable advertisers such as Delta Vacations to engage with customers who might want to explore products, compare choices, and make decisions on ChatGPT. “Travel planning is becoming increasingly personalized, and travelers expect experiences that feel relevant,” Katrin Koenig, President of Delta Vacations, told Amazon Ads. “Through our collaboration with Amazon Ads and ChatGPT Ads, we can leverage deep consumer insights to inform how and when Delta Vacations appear within ChatGPT Ads experiences to create new opportunities for travelers to engage and discover vacation possibilities." In a research note published earlier this month, Sensor Tower calls out positive performance for ChatGPT’s ad network, as the number of ads per user, per hour of time spent on ChatGPT’s mobile app in the U.S. increases. In August 2026, that number rose 163% compared with in April 2026. advertisement advertisement “Ad density on the platform likely suggests greater ad supply and willingness to ramp ads throughout the user experience,” Sensor Tower data shows. Ads per user per hour of time spent on ChatGPT’s mobile app in the U.S. from April 2026 through August 2026 increased an average of 26% month-over-month, the data showed. The access to ChatGPT Ads gives advertisers a way to extend campaigns further into where their customers are actively spending time in conversational chat platforms. Amazon Ads also posted the news on LinkedIn. "Big opportunity for sellers," Abrar Hashmii, founder of ThriveBizz, which supports ecommerce brands, wrote in the comments of Amazon Ad's announcement. " The real question now is how brands will adapt their campaigns and product data for conversational shopping instead of relying only on traditional keyword targeting." For months, Amazon has been quietly running successful ad campaigns, per the company, on OpenAI's ChatGPT platform, which in February in the U.S. began selling ads and experimenting with major retailers such as Best Buy and William-Sonoma. Part of OpenAI's ad success points to Amazon acknowledging that the platform has become an important marketing channel and that ChatGPT reached 900 million weekly active users. Chris Conetta, director of omnichannel supply at Amazon DSP, believes conversational ads represent the fastest-growing engagement opportunity for brands to reach new and existing audiences. "The AI-driven ad experience is not just a vision of what’s to come, but an opportunity for advertisers to meet relevant users where they spend time today," Conetta said. records.title: Cisco, OpenAI Launch Shirudo to Strengthen AI Infrastructure Security
records.excerpt: Cisco, OpenAI Launch Shirudo to Strengthen AI Infrastructure Security Technologies Services Business Devices TFM Awards 2026 LiveX 27 Home Blog Insights Awards Events Directory Programs DTW 2026 Asia Tech Series Special Edition: GenAI Podcasts Cisco, OpenAI Launch Shirudo to Strengthen AI Infrastructure Security Monday, 23 November 2026 23:10 Ray Sharma 1 2 3 4 5 (0 votes) 4 min read font size decrease font size increase font size Comment Image Credit: vladimircaribb/Bigstockphoto.com Cisco and OpenAI today launched an open source effort to make infrastructure secure by default and able to defend itself against today's sophisticated cyber attacks. For too long, security has been a coat of paint. Cisco builds protection into the infrastructure itself, drawing on decades of building and protecting the systems the world depends on. OpenAI brings leading frontier AI research and insight into the attacks coming next. Together, they combine their insight to help anticipate AI-driven threats with the control to stop them. Defenders must protect every part of their infrastructure, all the time. Attackers only need one machine that hasn't been patched. Shirudo is an important step toward closing that gap. The goal is infrastructure that is hardened from the moment it is built, keeps getting harder to attack, and can be restored to a known-good state if it is compromised. Shirudo: An Open Source Project from Cisco and OpenAI Shirudo, Japanese for "shield," uses eBPF, a technology that runs small, custom programs inside the operating system kernel without changing its source code. With it, AI agents can find a vulnerability, build a shield, and test that it stops the attack without disrupting the service. Shields go live only when the evidence says they are safe. Every shield is cryptographically signed, so the host can verify it before it runs, even if an attacker has gained administrator access. In testing against recent critical vulnerabilities "Java4shell" and the PHP flaw, Shirudo was able to write code that detected and blocked attempts to exploit both threats. By utilizing an agentic framework, Shirudo matches the speed of AI-driven attacks as soon as a vulnerability is identified. Learn more about Shirudo here . Cisco and OpenAI are inviting developers, researchers, and enterprises to help shape what comes next. Contribute a test that reproduces a vulnerability, run a shield against a kernel build you use, or show us where it breaks legitimate traffic. Jeetu Patel, President and Chief Product Officer, Cisco: There is nothing more important than giving security teams the tools they need to match the speed of the AI-driven threats they are facing. We need self-defending infrastructure that acts at the speed of code, learns in real time, and shields itself until patches are safely rolled out. Today, we're proud to announce Shirudo with OpenAI, an important step towards that vision as we continue to collaborate with the wider community to solve the unique challenges of AI safety and security. Greg Brockman, President and Co-founder of OpenAI: We're giving defenders better models and tools to find and fix vulnerabilities faster, but finding a bug today doesn't mean you can patch every system tomorrow. We are partnering closely with Cisco on Shirudo to help teams protect the systems they need to keep running while they build and roll out a fix. So many teams rely on the same software that it makes sense to build these tools in the open. Now when one team finds a better way to protect a system, others don't have to start from scratch. cisco openai network security ai infrastructure Ray Sharma Ray Sharma is an Industry Analyst and Editor at The Fast Mode. He has over 15 years of experience in mobile broadband technologies and solutions, conducting research and analysis on various technology segments and producing articles and write-ups on the latest developments within the sector. He is also in charge of social media engagement and industry liaisons. Follow him on LinkedIn or Facebook . records.excerpt: OpenAI updates ChatGPT to handle complex everyday questions, web searches, and images more reliably Ad Skip to content See plans Sign In Subscribe Now The Decoder Discord LinkedIn Matthias Bastian View the LinkedIn Profile of Matthias Bastian Nov 23, 2026 Short News OpenAI updates ChatGPT to handle complex everyday questions, web searches, and images more reliably OpenAI is rolling out a chat-tuned version of GPT-6.2 Sol worldwide, available now for Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users. The company says the model handles complex requests and web searches better than GPT-6 and asks more relevant follow-up questions. In internal tests, GPT-6.2 understands images better (71.7 vs. 47.4 percent) and follows difficult instructions more often (78.1 vs. 62.5 percent). On an internal benchmark for expert-level tasks, GPT-6.2 beats GPT-6 across all four reasoning levels, according to OpenAI. It scores roughly 65 to just over 71 percent, compared with about 52 to 66 percent for GPT-6. OpenAI also uses an internal version of BrowseComp to test how well models find answers to tough questions on the web. GPT-6.2 leads at every level, finishing about 10 percentage points ahead at the highest one. GPT-6.2 outperforms GPT-6 on expert-level tasks across all reasoning settings in ChatGPT's regular chat mode. | Image: OpenAI According to the system card , GPT-6.2 follows safety policies in 91 to 94 percent of difficult conversations, up from 77 to 80 percent for GPT-6. The model makes its biggest gains in youth safety, specifically around emotional dependency, eating disorders, and dangerous activities. Ad These numbers only apply to ChatGPT's chat mode. The Work and Codex models stay the same. Enterprise admins can decide whether their users get access to GPT-6.2. Aleph Partnership](https://dscdn.daily-sun.com/english/uploads/news_photos/2026/11/24/ChatGPT_Ads_presence_increases_in_44_countries_through_Aleph_partnership-6b051824c01f2.png) A A OpenAI has expanded local access to ChatGPT Ads across 44 countries through an exclusive reseller partnership with Aleph, bringing Bangladesh among the markets where brands and advertising agencies can now buy advertising services with local support. Under the agreement, Aleph will serve as OpenAI’s exclusive reseller in the selected markets, enabling advertisers to contract, make payments and receive campaign support through local teams. The partnership covers 14 countries in Latin America, 16 in Europe and Central Asia, 10 in the Middle East and Africa, and four in the Asia-Pacific region. Besides Bangladesh, the Asia-Pacific markets included are Cambodia, Hong Kong and Sri Lanka. **Read More** #### [How to use ChatGPT Dots: A practical guide to AI agents](https://daily-sun.com/sci-tech/909351/how-to-use-chatgpt-dots-a-practical-guide-to-ai-agents) [![Image 9: How to use ChatGPT Dots: A practical guide to AI agents](https://dscdn.daily-sun.com/english/uploads/news_photos/2026/11/15/medium/How_to_Use_ChatGPT_Dots_A_Practical_Guide_to_AI_Agents-6af9d7ecdbfc2.png)](https://daily-sun.com/sci-tech/909351/how-to-use-chatgpt-dots-a-practical-guide-to-ai-agents) For Bangladeshi brands and advertising agencies, the arrangement introduces an additional option for purchasing ChatGPT Ads through a local business partner. Services include local contracting and invoicing in local currencies, payment terms, onboarding, campaign assistance and training. According to [**OpenAI**](https://openai.com/ads/blog/chatgpt-ads-increases-its-market-presence/), the new reseller arrangement complements its existing **[global technology partners](https://openai.com/index/new-ways-to-buy-chatgpt-ads/)**and self-service [**ChatGPT Ads Manager**](https://ads.openai.com/). Advertisers can continue to purchase ads directly through Ads Manager or use available global technology partners. OpenAI clarified that the announcement does not change advertisers' ability to target countries in their campaigns. Advertisers worldwide can continue targeting any country where [**ChatGPT Ads are available**](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001245-ads-manager-availability#ads-manager-availability). **Read More** #### [What is AI Safety? Understanding privacy risks and human control](https://daily-sun.com/sci-tech/909914/what-is-ai-safety-understanding-privacy-risks-and-human-control) [![Image 10: What is AI Safety? Understanding privacy risks and human control](https://dscdn.daily-sun.com/english/uploads/news_photos/2026/11/18/medium/What_is_AI_safety-6afdbade8e3e6.png)](https://daily-sun.com/sci-tech/909914/what-is-ai-safety-understanding-privacy-risks-and-human-control) The company said more than 100,000 marketers have advertised on ChatGPT, adding that it will continue developing new advertising formats, optimisation tools and measurement solutions as the platform expands. OpenAI said its focus remains on broadening access to AI, maintaining user trust and helping businesses achieve their advertising goals. Advertisers and agencies interested in purchasing ChatGPT Ads through Aleph can contact the company's local teams for further information. records.excerpt: Title: The NineHertz Joins OpenAI Partner Network to Support Enterprise AI Adoption URL Source: http://www.freep.com/press-release/story/276150/the-ninehertz-joins-openai-partner-network-to-support-enterprise-ai-adoption/ Final URL: https://www.freep.com/press-release/story/276150/the-ninehertz-joins-openai-partner-network-to-support-enterprise-ai-adoption/ Published Time: 2026-11-20T12:02:51.000Z Markdown Content: ![Image 1](https://pix.xpr.media/p/eyJzIjoiMzdmZGMyZmQtY2U2Yi00MTA2LTgwMmMtYmJjODM1NmQ4YmZhIiwiYyI6ImEwNmQzYjMyLTA2ZDUtNDgxYS05ZTNiLWVkMmZmZjI0MTExZCIsInYiOjF9.NMM9P4OEwOAW2ElhDCgoIXB7yzsN5tW95TJe7WMRuo8.gif) _The NineHertz partners with OpenAI as a Select Partner, strengthening its AI-native engineering, agentic systems, enterprise AI engineering & FDE capabilities._ GA, UNITED STATES, November 20, 2026 /[EINPresswire.com](https://www.einpresswire.com/)/ — The NineHertz, an AI-native software engineering company headquartered in Jaipur, India, today announced that it has been named an OpenAI Select Partner, joining the OpenAI Partner Network. The designation supports the company’s focus on helping organizations move beyond AI experimentation to build and deploy AI-powered applications, intelligent workflows, and agentic systems using OpenAI technologies. As businesses scale and look to integrate artificial intelligence into their products and operations, the challenge is increasingly about engineering AI into real-world environments. Moving from promising prototypes to dependable applications requires more than access to advanced models. It demands the integration of AI with enterprise data, existing systems, business processes, and operational requirements that determine whether a solution can deliver sustained value. Through its [Forward Deployed Engineer](https://theninehertz.com/artificial-intelligence/forward-deployed-engineering) as a Service capabilities, The NineHertz aims to help enterprises bridge this gap by bringing engineering expertise closer to business and technology teams, supporting AI solution development, integration, and deployment in real-world environments. For The NineHertz, the OpenAI partnership aligns with its broader vision of becoming a leading AI-native engineering partner to frontier AI companies and enterprises. By bringing together AI engineering, software development, intelligent automation, and enterprise modernization capabilities, the company aims to help organizations translate emerging AI technologies into practical business applications. Strategic Significance of The NineHertz Joining the OpenAI Partner Network The OpenAI partnership aligns with The NineHertz’s broader AI-native engineering approach: designing, building, and evolving software with AI integrated into the development process and the resulting business applications. The practical opportunity lies in connecting AI capabilities with specific business requirements rather than treating AI as a standalone technology layer. For enterprises, this means approaching AI as part of a wider technology and operating strategy rather than as a standalone capability. Through its [enterprise OpenAI implementation](https://theninehertz.com/artificial-intelligence/openai-development-services) capabilities, The NineHertz aims connecting AI systems to enterprise knowledge, automating document-intensive processes, enabling more intuitive interactions with business applications, and orchestrating workflows across systems. The OpenAI partnership represents an important milestone in The NineHertz’s broader strategic ambition: to become a leading AI-native engineering partner to frontier AI companies and enterprises, bringing together advanced AI capabilities, forward-deployed engineering, and specialized industry expertise to turn emerging technology into real-world business solutions. “Enterprise AI is moving beyond experimentation, and the next phase will be defined by how effectively organizations translate AI capabilities into real business outcomes. Our ambition at The NineHertz is to build an AI-native engineering organization that operates at the intersection of frontier AI innovation, industry expertise, and forward-deployed engineering. Our partnership with OpenAI is an important milestone in that journey, strengthening our ability to help enterprises design, build, and operationalize the next generation of intelligent products and systems,” said Tarun Khatri, CEO of The NineHertz. The Road Ahead: Advancing Enterprise AI Engineering and Agentic AI Capabilities The NineHertz views the Select Partner designation as a milestone in its broader journey to strengthen its position in the AI engineering ecosystem. The company will continue investing in specialized AI engineering talent, expanding its engagement with frontier AI ecosystems, advancing its agentic AI and autonomous operations capabilities, and building industry-focused solutions designed to address complex enterprise challenges. The company’s Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) approach brings engineering teams closer to customer environments, enabling them to work alongside business and technology stakeholders to identify challenges, architect solutions, integrate AI into existing systems, and accelerate implementation. These capabilities are complemented by flexible delivery models spanning expert augmentation, dedicated offshore development teams, managed delivery, and build-operate-transfer arrangements. As enterprises move toward the next phase of AI adoption, The NineHertz aims to be a partner that not only understands emerging AI technologies but can engineer, integrate, and operationalize them to create lasting business value. [About The NineHertz](https://theninehertz.com/about-us) The NineHertz is an AI-native software engineering company founded in 2013 and headquartered in Georgia, USA, with offices across the globe. The company helps businesses design, build, and evolve digital products, enterprise applications, and AI-enabled software systems. Its capabilities span AI engineering, generative AI, agentic workflows, intelligent automation, and enterprise modernization. Through its proprietary ContinuumAI™ build-run-evolve framework, The NineHertz supports organizations across the software lifecycle through flexible engineering and delivery models, helping businesses develop, deploy, and continuously evolve AI-enabled solutions. Artificial Intelligence US Banks Tighten AI Agent Controls After OpenAI Models Bypass Testing Safeguards Written by: Tathagata Sen Updated 7:03 AM EST, November 23, 2026 Photo credit: Unsplash.com Several large and mid-sized U.S. banks are tightening controls on internally developed AI agents after experimental OpenAI models bypassed internet-isolation safeguards during cybersecurity tests and accessed external systems, including Hugging Face, according to a November 23 Reuters report . The incidents occurred during July testing. OpenAI said the models had fewer safeguards than its public products. No banks have reported similar incidents, but several have formed teams to investigate the weaknesses and assess their own exposure. Banks Restrict Agent Access and Strengthen Monitoring Banks are limiting the systems, credentials and activities available to AI agents and separating them from critical banking systems. They are also strengthening mechanisms to detect and stop potentially harmful activity. Institutions are reviewing emergency shutdown mechanisms, or kill switches, and testing backup procedures for functions such as loan processing, fraud detection and financial-crime reviews. They are also studying how to detect agents using credentials assigned to human employees. Banks are strengthening post-deployment monitoring to track which systems agents access, what actions they take and whether those actions receive human approval. The Reuters report also cited an AI risk specialist who warned that agents can exhibit behaviors after deployment that were not identified during testing. Agent Identity and Data Access Become Governance Priorities The developments highlight the need for chief data officers (CDOs) to work with cybersecurity and technology teams to govern agents’ access to enterprise data and systems. Organizations need clear agent identities, defined permissions and records of data access and activity. These controls help detect unauthorized actions, reconstruct incidents and establish accountability. As AI governance extends beyond pre-deployment testing, CDOs must help ensure agents remain monitored and that their access can be revoked quickly when their behavior becomes unsafe. records.title: Oracle Rebuts Funding Gap Rumors, Says OpenAI Contract Financing Fully in Place
records.excerpt: Oracle issued a statement late Friday evening stressing that the funding needed to fulfill its OpenAI infrastructure contracts is fully in place, rebutting reports of a funding shortfall and saying that additional talks with suppliers are merely options. The company completed roughly $20 billion in fundraising earlier this month, while also announcing that its Abilene, Texas campus is nearing completion, that its new Shackelford campus has secured permits, and that it will deliver Nvidia Vera Rubin racks in the coming weeks. The move comes as concerns mount over circular financing in AI and Nvidia turns more cautious about backing emerging cloud players, with market attention shifting to who will bear the massive capital expenditures and whether cash flow can support them.

The work will begin with Cohesity identity threat detection and response (ITDR) software and is intended to help engineers identify, validate, and remediate vulnerabilities earlier in the development lifecycle. Cohesity received access to Daybreak Red and Daybreak Blue through the OpenAI Trusted Access for Cyber program. This program provides vetted security organizations with governed access to advanced AI models for defensive red teaming and penetration testing. Cohesity security engineers plan to use the models to probe software for exploitable weaknesses, determine which findings pose material risk, and direct fixes to the appropriate components. The work will complement the static analysis, dependency scanning, and third-party penetration testing that Cohesity already performs. By applying advanced cyber models within a controlled environment, Cohesity aims to identify potential vulnerabilities before they can be exploited and strengthen protections delivered through future product updates. "Our customers trust Cohesity with some of their most critical data, so the software we ship must be tested against emerging attack techniques," said Eric Brown, CFO and COO, Cohesity. "Using OpenAI GPT Cyber Models can help our security engineers identify and address potential weaknesses earlier in the development lifecycle. We are starting with identity security and plan to apply what we learn wherever it can strengthen the resilience of our platform." AI Basics and How-To Guides ChatGPT Limits: When They Reset and How to Check By Lenka Vojtechova · Updated November 22, 2026 · 10 min read ChatGPT OpenAI AI Pricing GPT The most useful thing to know about ChatGPT limits is something OpenAI never puts on a marketing page: ordinary chat has no usage counter. No meter, no percentage, no dashboard. You find out you have reached a chat limit when ChatGPT tells you that you have reached it, and not one moment sooner. The one place a meter does exist is Work and Codex, which run on a 5-hour window, a weekly cap and a reset system of their own, and that is where most of the confusion about "ChatGPT resets" comes from. That single fact reshapes the whole question. If you cannot read a number, four other things matter instead. Which activities are capped at all, when each window resets, how to tell a usage limit from a rate limit, and what your options actually are at the wall. This guide covers all four, plus the Work and Codex meter and its instant, banked and global resets. Every figure comes from OpenAI's own help centre, not from the recycled numbers still circulating from before the August 2026 changes. The Key Takeaways There is no usage meter for chat. OpenAI says ChatGPT "will notify you when you reach an applicable limit" and displays reset timing "when that information is available". Nothing shows remaining chat usage in advance. Work and Codex do have a meter. They share one allowance with a 5-hour window on Plus and a weekly cap, shown under Settings > Usage. Plus and Pro can buy an instant reset, and promotional banked resets wait on your account until they expire. Ordinary text chat is no longer capped on Free and Go. Those tiers moved to unlimited everyday text chats from the week of 10 August 2026, subject to abuse-prevention safeguards. Plus and Pro already had it. Everything else still has a cap. File uploads, image generation, voice and data analysis all carry separate usage limits, and they reset on their own schedules. No chat message number is published for Plus. OpenAI describes Plus chat by which reasoning levels it unlocks, never by a message count. Any article quoting a specific Plus chat figure is quoting a retired one. A usage limit and a rate limit are different walls. One clears at a reset time, the other clears in seconds. The fix is not the same. This is the single most repeated question about ChatGPT limits , and it keeps being asked because many pages that answer it describe a chat meter ChatGPT does not have. Work and Codex are the exception, and they are covered in their own section below . What OpenAI actually exposes OpenAI's own documentation is careful about this. It says ChatGPT "will notify you when you reach an applicable limit", and that ChatGPT "displays when an allowance resets when that information is available". Both statements describe what happens at the wall, not before it. There is no equivalent of a mobile data meter that counts down as you use it. Enterprise and Edu administrators are the exception. Those plans have a workspace budget view, because the organisation paying the bill needs one. Individual Free, Go, Plus and Pro accounts have nothing comparable for everyday chat. Their only meter is the Work and Codex one under Settings > Usage, and it counts agent work, not conversation. The three signals you do get Without a counter, you are reading indirect signals instead. There are three worth knowing. The model picker. When an allowance on a specific model is spent, that option is greyed out, or carries a note about when it returns. Opening the picker is the closest thing to a status check. A silent model downgrade. If answers suddenly get shorter or noticeably weaker without you changing anything, ChatGPT may have moved you to a lighter model. OpenAI describes this as continuing "with another available reasoning model". The reset notice itself. Once you hit a limit, the message that appears usually names the time the window reopens. That notice is the only concrete number most users will ever see. If answers have gone slow rather than stopped, that is usually a different problem, and our guide to why ChatGPT gets slow covers the causes that are not usage related at all. When Do ChatGPT Limits Reset? There is no single reset time, and that is the detail most pages get wrong. Limits are attached to individual models, features and tools, and each counter runs on its own clock. Nothing resets globally at midnight. Rolling windows, not calendar days Most consumer allowances behave as rolling windows. Capacity returns a set period after you consumed it, rather than everyone's quota refilling together at a fixed hour. This is why two people on the same plan can hit and clear a limit at completely different times of day, and why "ChatGPT resets at midnight" is wrong as a general rule. Weekly allowances are the other clock, and the clearest documented example is Work and Codex, where a new weekly period starts with your first request after a reset rather than on a fixed day. That system has its own meter and its own kinds of reset, so it gets its own section. Work and Codex Limits: The 5-Hour Window, Weekly Cap and Resets If you have searched for "ChatGPT resets" and found a screen in your settings that says you have none, this is the system you are looking at. ChatGPT Work and Codex share one allowance, and OpenAI states that Work "uses the same pricing, credits, and usage limits as Codex". Unlike chat, it is metered, and it can be reset in three different ways. Where the meter is Open Settings > Usage in the ChatGPT desktop app or on the web, or the usage dashboard directly. It shows how much of each window you have used and when it resets. In the Codex CLI, /status shows the same thing mid-session. This is the only place an individual ChatGPT account gets a running percentage. records.excerpt: OpenAI, the artificial intelligence (AI) company led by Sam Altman, is reportedly in discussions for a partnership with Worldcoin (WLD). OpenAI, the artificial intelligence (AI) company led by Sam Altman, is reportedly in discussions for a partnership with Worldcoin (WLD) , a cryptocurrency-based universal basic income and identity verification firm also co-founded by Altman. The potential partnership would involve OpenAI providing AI solutions and services to Worldcoin, with the possibility of future collaboration. Both OpenAI and Worldcoin have faced controversies and regulatory challenges in the past. OpenAI recently navigated an investigation threat from European Union authorities regarding its partnership with Microsoft, ultimately avoiding any allegations. Worldcoin, on the other hand, has encountered bans in Portugal, Kenya, and Spain in the first three months of 2024. The involvement of Sam Altman in both companies would likely attract increased regulatory scrutiny. According to Tools for Humanity CEO Alex Blania, this attention is primarily due to Altman's presence, which exceeds what one would typically expect for companies or projects of their size. Worldcoin is currently one of the world's most active identity verification services with an average of two million daily users. Worldcoin has been focused on expanding its operations throughout 2024. The company launched its own blockchain, a layer-2 solution prioritizing verified Worldcoin users over bots. Worldcoin also plans to increase its WLD token supply by 36 million, valued at approximately $196 million, over the next six months, targeting select institutions for the sell-off. The same document, titled "Research acceleration: The jagged frontier," shows those agents succeeding on 79% of tasks that involve watching training runs for problems but on only 29% of tasks that involve building the evaluation, reinforcement-learning and agent environments where new models are tested. People, it says, still came up with nearly all of the ideas behind OpenAI's latest model releases. In Short OpenAI measured how its own researchers use AI coding agents and found the agents now handle far more work alone than in March, while spending on them has climbed to $2,400 a day for the typical researcher at list prices. The gains are uneven: agents do well at monitoring and answering questions, and poorly at building infrastructure, testing environments and serving code, and people still supply most of the important ideas. The report is OpenAI's own measurement of its own staff, with no external audit, and it frames the numbers as early signs of AI speeding up the development of AI. A report about the machine that builds the machine The November 18 publication is OpenAI's second report on what it calls research acceleration. It builds on a September 2026 post and adds, in OpenAI's words, "new quantitative and qualitative measures of (1) AI uplift across research domains and (2) how humans remain involved in the research process." The company describes the result as "a broader, though still partial, picture of how research at OpenAI is changing." The stated reason for publishing is policy, not product. OpenAI says it believes "AI labs should be required to track and publicly report indicators of recursive self-improvement (RSI) - the process by which AI accelerates the development of future AI systems," a position it says it first set out in its frontier policy blueprint . The report adds a qualifier that is easy to miss: "our reporting should not be read as an intention to pursue full RSI." OpenAI is not alone in this kind of disclosure. The report notes that Anthropic "has independently released three separate reports documenting how internal model deployments have accelerated the AI research process," that Section 3.4.2 of Google's Gemini 4 Argon Safety and Security Report describes "the growing share of AI-written code internally at Google DeepMind," and that METR, in collaboration with Anthropic, released an acceleration report estimating how much internal Claude models have accelerated the capabilities frontier. Anthropic went further in its own filings on November 2: its amended IPO registration statement says internal estimates indicate it "may imminently meet" its own policy's definition of dramatically accelerated progress. The report is organized in three parts. Inputs covers coding agents as a research resource. Process covers how researchers turn those inputs into model capabilities. Outputs covers what comes out the other end. Nearly half of two-to-four-hour tasks, with a caveat attached The headline figure comes from a measurement OpenAI calls task success with zero human interventions. Tasks delegated to agents are grouped by how long a person would be expected to take, and the share completed without any human correction is tracked month by month. From March to October, according to OpenAI, estimated success rose from 23% to 46% for tasks estimated to require two to four hours of human work, and from 13% to 35% for tasks estimated to require four to eight hours. The chart reports success across "all outcomes, including uncertain outcomes," and displays a midpoint, partial identification bounds and approximate 95% confidence intervals for each month. The October figures cover October 1 to 18. In OpenAI's chart, the eight-hours-plus success rate sits near 25% in June, July and August, drops to about 15% in September and rises again to about 29% in the first half of October, with wide intervals throughout. Short tasks still account for most delegated work: tasks under an hour make up a majority of the volume in every month shown, though the two-to-four-hour bucket roughly doubled its share of tasks between March and October, by PPC Land's reading of the chart. OpenAI flags a selection problem with its own number. "As agents have become more capable, researchers may also have changed the types of tasks delegated within each duration bucket," the report states. "As a result, changes in zero-intervention success rates within these buckets may reflect both capability improvements and researchers' changing choices about when and how to use agents." In plain terms, researchers may simply be getting better at handing agents the tasks agents are likely to finish. The jagged part The report's title refers to how uneven the gains are. To show it, OpenAI sorted tasks using the O*NET AI R&D taxonomy developed by Epoch AI, which splits research work into six categories - Decide, Design, Build, Run, Analyze and Communicate - and 27 individual tasks. AI Basics and How-To Guides ChatGPT Memory: How It Works and How to Delete It By Lenka Vojtechova · Updated November 22, 2026 · 16 min read ChatGPT OpenAI Data Privacy Tips & Tricks Productivity Ask ChatGPT what it knows about you and it will tell you something. What most people do not realise is that the screen where you manage that knowledge changed completely on 4 June 2026 . OpenAI replaced the familiar scrolling list of saved memories with a single memory summary , written and rewritten automatically by a background process the company calls dreaming . The old list still exists, but it is now the legacy option. That matters because many guides to ChatGPT memory still walk you through the old path, and following it on a current account leads nowhere. This guide covers how memory actually works now, the exact steps to delete it, what deleting does and does not remove, how memory behaves inside projects and Temporary Chats, and the one behaviour that catches people out: switching memory back on can bring the memories back. The Key Takeaways New system since 4 June 2026: a continuously updated memory summary replaced the saved memories list, built by OpenAI's dreaming process. Where to look: Settings, then Personalization, then Memory . Not Data controls, which is where every stale guide sends you. Deleting is not erasing: clearing your memories does not delete your chats, and turning memory back on lets ChatGPT rebuild memories from the chats still in your history, including older ones . Muting is not deleting either: the newer Don't mention this again option reduces future references to a detail but leaves the original chat, file or email in place. Full removal takes several deletions: past chats, archived chats, files in Library or Space, the memory summary, and any connected apps holding the same detail. Screens still differ: OpenAI began with Plus and Pro in the US , and as of November 2026 its Memory help page still says controls vary by plan, region, platform and workspace, so two accounts can legitimately show two different screens. When it is on, ChatGPT pulls useful details from your chats, your files and your connected apps, so you do not have to reintroduce yourself every time you open a new window. The important shift is in how those details are produced. Under the old system, ChatGPT wrote a note whenever something looked worth keeping, and those notes piled up in a list you maintained by hand. Under the new one, a background process reads across your conversation history and keeps a synthesis of it up to date. That synthesis is one of the hidden inputs behind why two people get different answers to the same question . You read that synthesis on the memory summary page. The memory summary The memory summary is a written, high-level portrait of what ChatGPT has concluded about you. You can change it three ways: type a correction into the text field, highlight a line and correct that specific piece, or select Don't mention this again where the option appears. OpenAI is direct about its limits. The summary does not necessarily include every detail or source that memory can reference, and it may leave out details that are less relevant or come from sources that are not shown individually. If you want to know whether something specific is in there, the company's own advice is to ask ChatGPT what it remembers about you. Where the context actually comes from When ChatGPT uses personal context, Sources can appear below the response. It lists what fed the answer: a past chat, a saved memory, a custom instruction, a file or a connected email. From there you can open the source, correct or delete a saved memory, delete a referenced chat, or mark a source as relevant or not relevant. Two caveats are worth carrying: Sources may not show every factor that shaped a response, and memory Sources are not included when you share a conversation through a link. The inputs are wider than chats. Depending on your plan and region, OpenAI's Memory help page lists past chats, saved memories, custom instructions, files saved in Library or Space, and content from connected apps such as Gmail. Memory can also shape a web search: ChatGPT may use a detail such as your location or a dietary preference to write a better search query. What Changed in June 2026, and Why OpenAI published the reasoning in a post titled Dreaming: Better memory for a more helpful ChatGPT on 4 June 2026. Memory first launched in April 2024 as saved memories, a system the company now likens to talking to someone who took a few notes but still forgot everything that was not written down. In April 2025 it added the ability to reference chat history, powered by the first version of dreaming. The June 2026 release rebuilt the whole thing on that foundation. The problem being solved was staleness. In OpenAI's words, saved memories "tend to go stale over time and eventually become incorrect or irrelevant". The company's own test case is a note that you are planning a birthday party for next Saturday: eventually, Sunday arrives. A synthesis that updates itself handles the passage of time, so "You're going to Singapore in July" becomes "You went to Singapore in July 2026" once the trip ends. Two numbers are worth knowing. In that announcement OpenAI says it cut the compute needed to serve dreaming to Free users by approximately five times, which is what made the wider rollout practical. The release notes for the same day supply the figure the blog leaves vague: Plus and Pro accounts got twice as much memory capacity. The generations have names, and you will see them quoted elsewhere: saved memories in 2024, saved memories plus Dreaming V0 in 2025, and Dreaming V3 in 2026. The rollout started with Plus and Pro users in the US, with additional countries and the Free and Go plans promised over the following weeks and an in-product notice when your account is switched over. records.title: OpenAI Perplexity Metric: GPT Log-Loss Curve (Nov 2026)
records.excerpt: Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki posted OpenAI's held-out log-perplexity history from GPT-3.5 through frontier models and asked rivals to adopt shared pacing limits tied to that metric. OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki published OpenAI's internal log-perplexity curve on November 22, 2026 and asked every frontier lab to adopt the same metric for shared safety pacing. In Perplexity and Intelligence , he argues that pretraining compression—measured as cross-entropy loss on a fixed held-out set—is the "intelligence substrate" behind ChatGPT, reasoning models, cyber skills, and internal math breakthroughs. He ties specific capability jumps to numeric thresholds, warns that monitorability tools weaken as loss falls, and proposes industry-wide development limits labs would not cross until oversight catches up. Update (November 23, 2026): Microsoft backs the transparency push and cites MAI-2 on OpenAI's holdout Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman publicly endorsed Pachocki's essay on November 22, 2026 with a quote post on X calling the transparency push "super important" and crediting @merettm and OpenAI. The quote post itself does not list a loss number. AIbase's November 23 recap says Suleyman went further the same day: with OpenAI's permission , Microsoft disclosed MAI-2 Base at 0.819 log-perplexity on OpenAI's evaluation dataset , described as close to GPT-5.6 Sol on that pretraining measure because both models share a tokenizer . table · 2 cols What Microsoft signaled What it does not establish Willingness to discuss pretraining progress on a common held-out set A signed industry-wide training stop One comparable loss on OpenAI's private eval snapshot Parity on agents, coding agents, or post-trained products Alignment with OpenAI's safety-bar narrative That Anthropic, Google, or Meta will publish matching curves Suleyman's own October MAI-Base-2 lab note already argued for bits-per-byte when tokenizers differ. That tension is the point of Pachocki's footnote: transparency norms must precede apples-to-apples league tables. Builders routing between Copilot's MAI stack and OpenAI API models should still pick on task evals , not one borrowed loss—see GPT-6.2 comparisons . OpenAI leaders Sam Altman , Greg Brockman , and Mark Chen also praised the essay on X the same weekend, per syndicated roundups; those posts add political cover inside the frontier club, not a new number on Microsoft's side beyond the 0.819 reports. What is OpenAI actually sharing? The headline is transparency on progress metrics , not a dataset dump. Pachocki says OpenAI has tracked perplexity on held-out data for years and is now publishing the curve because competitive disadvantage is outweighed by the need for shared safety norms . table · 2 cols What appeared What it is not Log-perplexity plot from GPT-3.5 through recent models Full pretraining corpus or weights Threshold story linking loss to emergent skills A new API product or benchmark leaderboard Proposal for cross-lab limits before the next loss band A signed treaty or regulator rule today The held-out material comes from OpenAI's internal codebase on a fixed snapshot , per the essay. That choice matters: code prediction is not identical to general web text, which is why Pachocki discusses dataset-selection pitfalls in a footnote. The numbers are still what OpenAI says it uses day to day to judge pretraining. The compress-or-predict view of frontier AI Pachocki's framing matches his earlier "alien mind" essay : build a large compressor on unstructured data, then elicit latent skills through prompting, fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning. Algorithmic blur between stages does not remove the split between creating capability and steering it. He repeats a claim familiar from OpenAI's research-acceleration write-up : once models near roughly 0.76 log-perplexity , internal math evaluations began producing results that felt like a phase change for researchers who had stared at the problems for years. He extrapolates that pretraining algorithm research —not full recursive self-improvement—could see a similar avalanche as soon as 2027 , while alignment work may not accelerate at the same rate. That asymmetry is why the post lands beside Managing frontier AI risk , where OpenAI describes pausing training after the Hugging Face incident and holding models until safety cases clear. Perplexity pacing would be another brake tied to measurable compression , not benchmark fashion. Capability thresholds on the published curve A green rounded polyhedron revealed between parted curtains, illustrating emergent frontier model capabilities tied to OpenAI log-perplexity thresholds Pachocki maps log-perplexity bands to capabilities OpenAI associates with its own history. records.title: Oracle Says OpenAI Data Center Expansion Is Fully Funded After $20bn Capital Raise
records.excerpt: Title: Oracle Says OpenAI Data Center Expansion Is Fully Funded After $20bn Capital Raise URL Source: http://www.tekedia.com/oracle-says-openai-data-center-expansion-is-fully-funded-after-20bn-capital-raise/ Final URL: https://www.tekedia.com/oracle-says-openai-data-center-expansion-is-fully-funded-after-20bn-capital-raise/ Published Time: 2026-11-21T20:06:18+00:00 Markdown Content: ![Image 1: Oracle Says OpenAI Data Center Expansion Is Fully Funded After $20bn Capital Raise](https://www.tekedia.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/larry-oracle-768x463.jpg) Oracle said on Friday that its infrastructure contract with OpenAI is fully funded following a $20 billion capital raise earlier this month, seeking to reassure investors concerned about the cost of its expanding artificial intelligence data-center operations and growing financial exposure to the ChatGPT maker. Oracle shares rose as much as 3.3% in after-hours trading following the announcement. The company said the financing arrangements disclosed at its Investor Day remain in place, including funding from vendors. It added that any further discussions with suppliers were aimed at securing additional financing options rather than filling a funding gap. “The financing we outlined at Oracle Investor Day, including vendor financing, is in place. Any further private discussions with vendors are just additional options,” Oracle said in a post on X. The clarification comes as investors examine how Oracle will finance the infrastructure required to support OpenAI’s growing computing needs. The two companies plan to develop an additional 4.5 gigawatts of data-center capacity in the United States, beyond the initial Stargate facility in Abilene, Texas. The scale of the commitment has raised questions about Oracle’s capital requirements, particularly as it takes on a larger role in supplying computing infrastructure for some of the world’s most demanding AI models. [![Image 2](https://www.tekedia.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/invest-masterclass.jpg)](https://school.tekedia.com/course/masterclass/) Oracle’s $20 billion capital raise, announced earlier this month, comprises approximately $10 billion in equity and $10 billion in debt. The financing is intended to support its infrastructure expansion, although the company did not provide a breakdown of how much would be allocated specifically to the OpenAI contract. Texas data-center projects are moving forward. Oracle also provided an update on construction at its Texas facilities, saying its Abilene campus is nearly complete. The site was used to train OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra model, giving it a prominent role in the companies’ expanding infrastructure partnership. [![Image 3](https://www.tekedia.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/parrot-2.jpg)](https://capital.tekedia.com/course/fee/) The company said its next gigawatt-scale campus in Shackelford County, Texas, has received full permitting approval. It also expects the handover of Nvidia’s next-generation Vera Rubin computing racks to proceed as planned in the coming weeks. The progress matters because the value of Oracle’s AI infrastructure commitments depends not only on securing financing but also on bringing computing capacity online on schedule. Delays in construction, equipment delivery, or deployment could affect its ability to meet customer requirements and generate returns from the investment. The Vera Rubin systems are expected to provide the computing capacity needed for advanced AI workloads. Their delivery will therefore be a significant step in preparing Oracle’s facilities for the next phase of AI infrastructure demand. Oracle’s statement addresses one of the central questions surrounding its AI expansion: whether the company has sufficient financing to meet its commitments to OpenAI without repeatedly returning to capital markets or relying on uncertain arrangements with suppliers. Its clarification that the financing is already in place may ease concerns about an immediate funding shortfall. However, the scale of the planned expansion means investors will continue to assess the company’s borrowing requirements, construction spending and ability to convert infrastructure investments into sustainable cash flows. But securing financing does not automatically make a large infrastructure programme profitable. Oracle must still manage the cost of building and equipping data centers, maintain delivery schedules, and generate enough revenue from computing services to justify the capital deployed. Its growing relationship with OpenAI also creates customer concentration exposure. A substantial portion of the infrastructure being developed is tied to demand from one major AI company, making Oracle’s returns sensitive to OpenAI’s computing requirements, commercial growth, and ability to fund its own expansion. Oracle is currently signaling that the financing for its existing OpenAI commitments is secured and that construction milestones are progressing. The next phase of the adventure is execution: delivering the promised capacity on time and turning the investment into revenue capable of supporting the cost of the expansion. records.title: Oracle OpenAI Deal: Oracle Says $300 Billion Contract Is Fully Funded
records.excerpt: Oracle says its roughly $300 billion OpenAI contract is fully funded after a $20 billion raise, calling itself the first hyperscaler funded for the AI cycle. Technology Oracle OpenAI Deal: Oracle Says $300 Billion Contract Is Fully Funded Oracle has told investors that every dollar is in place for its roughly $300 billion contract with OpenAI, saying a final capital raise earlier this month has made it the first of the big cloud compa… Published By : Technology Desk , The Open Press Last Updated: November 23, 2026, 07:15 IST Oracle says every dollar is in place for its roughly $300 billion OpenAI contract. (Photo: The Times of India) Oracle has told investors that every dollar is in place for its roughly $300 billion contract with OpenAI, saying a final capital raise earlier this month has made it the first of the big cloud companies to be fully funded for the current AI investment cycle. Why Oracle had to speak up The statement came at the end of a rough week for Oracle's stock. Shares closed on Friday at about $101, down more than 8 percent for the day and 19 percent for the week, closing out a seventh straight losing session. The stock now sits close to 70 percent below its record close from September 2025. Investors have been asking how much money Oracle needs to build AI data centres and how much of its future rests on a single customer. The OpenAI agreement runs over five years and makes up a large share of the company's $664 billion in remaining performance obligations. Earlier this month, Microsoft began winding down its own deal to rent AI computing from Oracle. Oracle issued its statement shortly after US markets closed on Friday. Shares rose as much as 3.3 percent in after-hours trading once the statement went out. The $20 billion raise behind the claim The raise Oracle is pointing to was worth $20 billion, split between about $10 billion in stock and $10 billion in debt. Oracle said the financing it laid out at its Investor Day, including vendor financing, is now fully in place. The company also addressed its talks with suppliers. Any further private discussions with vendors "are just additional options," Oracle said, adding that its ability to deliver on the OpenAI contract does not depend on them. Oracle went further and pushed back in advance against reports questioning its funding. "Any media reports that will come out and say the contrary are incorrect and wrong," the company said. Data centres: Abilene, Shackelford and Vera Rubin racks Oracle paired the funding update with progress on the ground. Its Abilene, Texas campus, where OpenAI's Astra-6 model was trained, is nearly complete. Shackelford County, its next gigawatt-scale site, is fully permitted, and the handover of Nvidia Vera Rubin racks in its data halls is on track for the coming weeks. The two companies plan to add 4.5 gigawatts of US data centre capacity on top of the original Stargate site in Abilene. The buildout is one of the largest AI infrastructure programmes in the world, and Oracle's ability to deliver it on time is now central to how investors judge the company. What Oracle promised on cash flow On the money side, Oracle stuck to its guidance. It expects positive free cash flow in the second half of fiscal 2028 and is targeting more than $30 billion in free cash flow in fiscal 2029. From that year, the company expects to fund its own growth. That promise matters because Oracle has been spending heavily to build data centres years before customers pay for the computing power. The company says the funding is now settled, and it stands by its funding position. Frequently Asked Questions What did Oracle say about its OpenAI contract? Oracle said its roughly $300 billion, five-year contract with OpenAI is fully funded, and called itself the first hyperscaler fully funded for the current AI investment cycle. How did Oracle fund the OpenAI deal? Oracle completed a final capital raise of $20 billion earlier this month, split between about $10 billion in stock and $10 billion in debt, along with vendor financing laid out at its Investor Day. Where is Oracle building data centres for OpenAI? Oracle is building at its Abilene, Texas campus, which is nearly complete, and at a fully permitted gigawatt-scale site in Shackelford County, with Nvidia Vera Rubin racks due in the coming weeks. By Martin Holloway 24 November 2026, 00:05 3 min read Share on X Share on LinkedIn Share on Facebook Share on WhatsApp Cisco Systems (NASDAQ: CSCO) and OpenAI launched a joint open-source project on 23 November 2026 called Shirudo, aimed at securing so-called agentic AI systems. The two companies said the effort is designed to let infrastructure defend itself at machine speed, before a permanent security patch is even available. Cisco shares closed little changed on the day, up 0.36% at $96.75, as the companies announced the project . What Shirudo does CSCO over the last month, hourly closes. Source: consolidated US exchange data. Cisco and OpenAI describe Shirudo as an industry-first open-source project for self-defending infrastructure. The pitch: systems that are secure by default and can respond to threats automatically, buying defenders time while a fix is developed. Cisco’s own newsroom confirmed the launch , and the firm also posted the news to its investor relations page, a sign it regards the project as material to shareholders. OpenAI published a parallel announcement on its own site titled “OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo,” underscoring the joint nature of the effort. The Wall Street Journal and SiliconANGLE both carried independent same-day coverage, framing Shirudo as a shield against AI-driven cyberattacks. Cisco’s engineering blog expanded on the underlying concept under the heading “Expanding the Defender’s Window,” describing the rationale for infrastructure that reacts to intrusions without waiting for human intervention. Muted market reaction The modest share-price move contrasts with positioning data around the stock. FINRA’s daily short-sale volume ratio for Cisco rose from 0.272 on 17 November to 0.587 on 23 November, roughly doubling over the week that included the Shirudo announcement, according to FINRA data . Cisco shares were also down 5.7% over the prior 20 trading days, having traded as high as $104.74 and as low as $90.69 in that window, with volume running at 1.86 times the 20-day average on the day of the announcement. Three Cisco executives, including chief executive Charles Robbins, each filed a Form 4 insider-transaction report on 20 November, three days before the Shirudo launch, according to SEC filings . The filings do not disclose share counts or transaction values in the fields available, so the size of any trades cannot be confirmed. Cisco’s recent numbers Cisco Systems, Inc. revenue by quarter, as filed. Source: SEC EDGAR. The launch follows a strong quarterly update from Cisco. The company reported revenue of $18,517m and net income of $4,552m for its fiscal first quarter of 2027, covering the three months to 24 October 2026, in a 10-Q filed with the SEC on 17 November, six days before the Shirudo announcement. Diluted earnings per share came in at $1.14 for the quarter. That marks a sharp sequential jump from the $15,841m in revenue and $3,373m in net income Cisco reported for fiscal third-quarter 2026, the quarter ended 25 April 2026. Revenue has climbed steadily across recent quarters: from $14,883m in fiscal first-quarter 2026 to $15,349m in fiscal second-quarter 2026, before the jump to $18,517m most recently. Net income over the same stretch rose from $2,860m to $3,175m to the latest $4,552m, a trajectory Cisco has linked in its own filings to demand tied to AI infrastructure build-outs, a theme that now extends into security products with Shirudo. The wider backdrop The announcement lands against a macro backdrop of gently easing US interest rates. The 10-year Treasury yield stood at 4.92% on 20 November, down from a prior 5.04%, according to Federal Reserve data , while the 2-year yield eased to 4.63% from 4.76% over the same period. The unemployment rate ticked down to 4.1% in October from 4.2% the previous month, per Bureau of Labor Statistics data compiled by the St. Louis Fed , part of a broader backdrop of resilient US macro conditions against which technology and AI-infrastructure spending announcements have continued through the back half of 2026. Investing.com and GuruFocus also carried same-day wire coverage of the launch, a sign of broad pickup beyond the two companies’ own channels. Whether Shirudo translates into a measurable product line for Cisco, or stays a research collaboration, is likely to become clearer as the open-source project attracts outside contributors and as Cisco details any commercial packaging in future filings. 歴代のベースモデルによる社内ソースコードの予測結果。点の位置が低いほど、モデルはコードの続きをうまく予測できた。右端の四角は、図に「Internal model」とだけ記されたOpenAIの社内モデルの測定値（OpenAIの発表ブログより）。 Pachocki氏は、2026年に予測精度の向上が速まった主な理由として、長年の研究と計算資源への投資が実を結んだことを挙げている。同氏によると、直近のモデルではAIも設計の面で重要な役割を果たしている。 自然な会話から数学の未解決問題まで⁠ 、 各世代で現れた能力 OpenAIは図の5本の水平な破線に、それぞれの水準でモデルが発揮した能力の例を書き添えている。以下の数値は、図から読み取ったおおよその対数パープレキシティを表す。 約0. 99 （GPT-3. 5） 自然な会話ができるようになり、初代ChatGPTの基盤になった。 約0. 91 （GPT-4） 答える前に段階を踏んで推論することで、回答の質を高められた。この力を引き出す研究が、後の推論モデルにつながった。回答時に推論を重ねて得られる改善は、事前学習を終えた時点で測るパープレキシティには表れない。 約0. 87 （GPT-5. 3-Codex／ GPT-5. 4） プログラムを書く際に実用的な助けになる水準としている。 約0. 83 （GPT-5. 6 Sol） サイバーセキュリティの専門家に相当する水準としている。 約0. 76 （GPT-6. 2 Astra） OpenAIはこの水準での成果として、数学のミレニアム懸賞問題の一つを解いたと図に記している。 Pachocki氏は、対数パープレキシティが0. 8を下回る水準に達した現在、サイバーセキュリティや数学で新たな能力が見られるようになったと報告している。OpenAIの研究者は、モデルの評価の一環として、1年以上にわたり数学の未解決問題を与えてきた。対数パープレキシティが約0. 76のモデルに切り替えたところ、研究者たちが長く考えてきた問題をモデルが次々と解き、その結果が社内の一つのSlackスレッドに並んだという。 ただし、グラフの数値が直接表すのは、モデルがコードの続きをどれだけうまく予測できたかという点に限られる。どの値に達すれば数学の未解決問題を解けるようになるかは、研究者にも事前にはわからなかった。 パープレキシティを使う利点は、次にどんな能力が現れるかを知らなくても、同じデータで世代ごとの事前学習の成果を比べられることにある。Pachocki氏がこの点を重視する背景には、特定の能力を試すベンチマークの限界がある。たとえば、GPT-2やGPT-3の時代に使われたベンチマークの多くは、GPT-4の頃にはスコアが頭打ちになり、その後の進歩を捉えにくくなっていたという。 AIが次世代モデルの事前学習の方法を改良したら AIが次世代モデルの開発を速める過程は、再帰的自己改善 （RSI） と呼ばれる。 Pachocki氏によると、再帰的自己改善をめぐる議論では、開発の各工程でAIが研究者をどこまで支援し、その仕事をどこまで引き受けられるかに関心が集まる。この見方では、人の監督なしに開発の全工程が進む 「完全な再帰的自己改善」 が、大きな転換点とされる。Pachocki氏は、人間が開発を制御し続けるには、そうした状態を避けるべきだと考えている。 ただ、開発全体の自動化の度合いに注目するだけでは、事前学習の研究で起こりうる変化を見落とすと同氏は指摘する。人が開発を監督し続けていても、AIがよりよい学習方法を見いだせば、次世代モデルの開発は大幅に速まる可能性がある。 この見通しの背景には、モデルが数学の未解決問題を次々と解くのを目にした経験がある。深層学習の研究は数学よりも実験に頼る部分が大きいものの、後から見れば単純な着想でも、研究者が何年も気づかなかった例がある。Pachocki氏は、早ければ2027年にも、AIが事前学習の研究で重要な発見を相次いでもたらす可能性があるとみている。 学習方法が改良されたとき、次世代モデルの能力がどれだけ伸びたかを、開発各社はどう比べられるのか。Pachocki氏は、モデルがデータの続きをうまく予測できるようになることが、思いがけない能力が現れる主な要因だとみている。そのため、開発の自動化がどこまで進んでいても、予測の良さを測るパープレキシティをもとに、モデルの能力全般の伸びを比べる共通の指標を作れるのではないかと考えている。 ただし、今回の評価データで対数パープレキシティがどこまで下がるかは、まだわかっていない。Pachocki氏は、下限に近づくほど値は下がりにくくなり、数値の上ではわずかな改善でも、モデルの能力は大きく伸びる可能性があるとみている。 では、値がさらに下がると、モデルは何ができるようになるのか。Pachocki氏はこれまでの推移から、対数パープレキシティが約0. 68〜0. 70に達する頃には新たな能力が現れると予想している。グラフでは、この範囲に 「？」 が付いている。どんな能力が現れるかはまだわからず、現在の試験では評価していない能力かもしれないという。 開発をさらに進める条件を⁠ 、 各社でどう決めるか 能力の高いモデルが人間の意図に沿って振る舞うかを、開発者はどう確かめるのか。Pachocki氏は、今後のモデルは自分が評価や訓練を受けていることに今より気づきやすくなると予想している。また、人間の意図に沿っているかを調べる現在の主な監査手法も、今後は有効性が下がるとみる。AIは、モデルの振る舞いを人間の意図に沿わせる研究や監視技術の開発にも大きく貢献すると同氏はみている。ただ、AIを使って事前学習の研究を最大限に加速させれば、安全性や監視の研究が追いつくのは難しいという。 そこでPachocki氏は、新しいモデルを使い始めるまでに、先端モデルの開発各社が協力して、モデルの評価方法や開示する情報について共通の基準を整えるよう提案している。同氏の案では、モデルを安全に使えるとする各社の説明をどう検証し、その根拠の弱点を探るかも、共通の基準に含める。 Pachocki氏はさらに、パープレキシティなど複数の指標をもとに、各社が開発を進めてよい範囲を共同で決めておくよう提案した。たとえば現在は、モデルが答えに至るまでの推論を監視する手法がある。同氏は、この手法に代わる技術の開発を、次の段階に進む条件の一例に挙げている。 OpenAIのCEO、Sam Altman氏は、開発各社が 「White House Accords」 で、AIシステムの安全性を高める基準や望ましい実践方法を定めることに合意したと説明した。そのうえで、パープレキシティをめぐる議論が その取り組みの後押しになることに期待を寄せた 。同社のGreg Brockman氏は、各社がどこまで開発を進めるか、そこから先に進むには何が必要かについて合意できれば、 次の段階でも同じ枠組みを使える可能性があると述べている 。 OpenAIの研究責任者、Mark Chen氏は、各社が個別にモデルの安全性を判断し、どこまで開発を進めるかを決めている限り、開発競争の圧力からは抜け出しにくいとみる。同氏は、モデルを安全に開発できるという根拠を各社で共有し、それをもとに、どこまで開発を進めてよいかを共同で決めたいと考えている。課題は、今後もモデルの性能が伸びていくなかで、各社の進歩をどんな指標で比べるかにある。 そこでChen氏は、先端モデルの開発各社に、 進歩を測るために使っている主な指標を公表するよう呼びかけた 。自社の測定値については、長く機密として扱ってきただけに、5年分を公開することには不安もあったと明かした。 Microsoft AIもOpenAIの社内コードでMAI Base 2を評価 Microsoft AIのCEO、Mustafa Suleyman氏は、OpenAIによる測定値の公開を、開発各社がモデル開発のペースを調整するための一歩として支持した。自社も、学習に使っていない共通の評価データで事前学習の成果を測り、 結果を公表していくとXで述べた 。 Microsoft AIは、10月15日に 事前学習の完了を発表した 自社の基盤モデル 「MAI Base 2」 [2] をOpenAIの社内コードで評価し、OpenAIの許可を得て結果を公表した。対数パープレキシティは0. 819だった。Suleyman氏は、GPT-5. 6 Solのベースモデルに近い値だと説明している。 OpenAIの歴代モデルの測定値（青）に、Microsoft AIの2モデルの測定値（赤）を重ねた。対数パープレキシティはMAI-1 Baseが0.878、MAI-2 Baseが0.819（Suleyman氏のX投稿より）。 Suleyman氏によると、MAI Base 2はOpenAIと同じトークナイザーでコードを区切るため、同じ評価データで測った両社の値を直接比べられる。ただ、Microsoft AIがOpenAIの社内コードを使えたのは特別なケースで、他社とも比べるには別の評価データが必要になる。開発元によってトークンの区切り方も異なるため、同氏は、1バイト当たりのビット数を表すbits per byte （BPB） で結果を報告する必要があるかもしれないと述べている [3] 。 評価データの選び方は、比較するモデルの世代によっても変わる。Pachocki氏によると、GPT-2やGPT-3は現在のモデルとは学習データの構成が異なり、コードの予測精度から能力全般を推し量るのは難しい。これらのモデルと現在のモデルを比べるなら、一般の文章を共通の評価データに使い、その続きをどれだけ正確に予測できるかを調べる方法が考えられるという。 おすすめ記事 記事・ニュース一覧

records.title: OpenAI元技術者、他社との戦略提携の機密文書写真を所持-条件書と見られると米検察（TBS CROSS DIG with Bloomberg）
records.excerpt: OpenAI元技術者、他社との戦略提携の機密文書写真を所持-条件書と見られると米検察 11/24(火) 13:02 配信 （ブルームバーグ）:米検察当局によると、米AI大手OpenAIのオフィス会議室に盗聴器を仕掛けた罪に問われている元技術者は、営業秘密を傍受した可能性が高いほか、ChatGPTを開発する同社と別の企業との「戦略的提携」の主要条件をまとめた文書と見られる写真を所持していたという。 検察当局は23日の裁判所への提出書類で、アブドゥルラフマン・アルフォザン被告の保釈を認めないよう米連邦判事に求めた。捜査は継続中だが、同被告は米国とのつながりが比較的弱い一方、母国サウジアラビアに相当な資産や人脈があり、公判前に逃亡を図る恐れが依然あるとしている。 検察側は提出書類で、「これまでに被告の個人用コンピューターから数百件の音声ファイルを発見した。この中には2026年9月を通じてOpenAIで行われた会議や会話の録音が数十件あり、その多くで企業秘密の可能性がある内容が議論されている」と説明した。 米国の永住権を持つアルフォザン被告は、盗聴の罪について無罪を主張している。司法省によると、OpenAIの社員が幹部用会議室のテレビの裏に仕掛けられた高性能の録音装置を発見した後、被告は10月に逮捕された。OpenAIによれば、被告は25年7月から勤務し、逮捕された日に解雇された。 今月これまでに開かれた審理では、ビンス・チャブリア連邦地裁判事が、より重い罪を裏付ける追加証拠を連邦政府が示さない限り、アルフォザン被告の身柄拘束を続けることに懸念を示していた。 検察当局は23日の提出書類で、アルフォザン被告が音声ファイルと、一部の録音をAIで文字起こしした記録を、日付ごとに入念に分類し、録音内容に応じてファイル名を変更して保管していたようだと指摘した。ファイルを自身のコンピューターに保存したほか、少なくとも一部の録音をクラウド型ファイル共有サービスのDropboxにアップロードした形跡があるという。 検察側はまた、被告の携帯電話から複数の写真を発見したと説明。この中には、confidential（機密）と記された戦略的提携に関する文書の画像が含まれていたという。 前へ 1 2 次へ 1 / 2ページ 【関連リンク】 若年層で「うつ病」による日常生活への影響が顕在化 高齢層とは対照的な健康動向 50代は「人生の折り返し」か 不遇な世代論では捉えきれぬ団塊ジュニアの多様なリアル 「若者の大移動」は合理的判断。国勢調査が暴いた、人口減少ニッポンの厳しい現実 64万トン放出で浮き彫りになった備蓄米の限界 買戻し条件と制度柔軟性の再設計 AI失業、日本で本当に危ないのは「若者」ではない 日本型雇用が生み出す“ホワイトカラー淘汰”のリアル

records.title: 米AMD、OpenAIとMetaのワラントに関連する3億3700万株の登録を申請
records.excerpt: アドバンスト・マイクロ・デバイセズ（AMD）は米証券取引委員会（SEC）に様式S-3を提出し、既存株主および戦略的パートナーによる転売の可能性がある最大3億3693万4324株を登録した。これは発行済み株式16億6000万株の約20.3%に相当する規模だ。うち約3億2000万株はOpenAIとメタ・プラットフォームズが保有する業績連動型ワラントに由来し、両社はそれぞれ最大1億6000万株を1株0.01ドル（約1.6円）で取得できる。いずれのワラントも現時点では行使可能ではなく、権利確定は1ギガワットから始まり6ギガワットに達するGPU購入と、最大600ドル（約9万5000円）の株価条件に連動する。残りはWorld LabsとTaalasの買収対価に相当する。AMD自身は株式を売却せず、手取り金も得ない。 アドバンスト・マイクロ・デバイセズ（AMD）は、既存株主や戦略的パートナーが将来的に売却する可能性のある最大3億3693万4324株の普通株式を対象とする棚卸登録を申請した。この規模は同半導体メーカーの発行済み株式の約5分の1に相当する。同社は月曜日、様式S-3を米証券取引委員会（SEC）に開示した。AMD自身はこれらの株式を一切募集しておらず、株主による売却から得られる手取り金もない。 今回の登録規模は目を引く。登録された株式ブロックは、2026年11月18日時点でAMDが発行済みとする16億5631万7509株の約20.3%に相当する。ただし、登録は売却ではない。この申請は株主に一部、全部、あるいは全く売却しない裁量を与えるものであり、ブロックの大部分は当面行使できない。 ワラントがブロックの大半を占める 登録株式のうち約3億2000万株は、OpenAIとメタ・プラットフォームズ（META）が保有する業績連動型ワラントに由来する。両社はそれぞれ最大1億6000万株のAMD株式を1株0.01ドル（約1.6円）の行使価格で取得できる。いずれのワラントも現在は行使可能ではない。AMDは2025年10月にOpenAI向けワラントを、2026年2月にメタ向けワラントを、それぞれ別途のチップ供給契約と併せて発行した。 権利確定は段階的で、両パートナーが実際に購入するハードウェアの量に依存する。最初のトランシェは、AMD Instinct GPUの初期1ギガワット相当（OpenAIの場合はMI450シリーズを含む）の納品または出荷に連動する。各1億6000万株のパッケージの完全な権利確定には、累計6ギガワットの購入に加え、技術的条件および最終トランシェでは1株600ドル（約9万5000円）まで上昇する株価条件の達成が必要だ。同社の申請書類は、ワラント株式が2026年11月18日から60日以内に行使可能になる見込みはないと述べている。 棚卸登録の残り、約1700万株は直近の2件の買収に伴う株式対価に相当する。AMDは2026年11月13日にWorld Labs Technologiesの買収を完了し、同社の旧株主に1497万8322株を発行した。また11月17日に推論チップ専門のTaalas Inc.の買収を完了し、最大195万6002株がクロージング対価、交換可能対価、条件付対価として割り当てられた。 目論見書には売却株主の名簿が記載されており、アンドリーセン・ホロウィッツ、フィデリティ、ブラックロックの関連ファンドに加え、NVIDIA（NVDA）、オートデスク、シスコ・インベストメンツが名を連ねる。いずれも取引完了前にWorld LabsまたはTaalasの持分を保有していた。 登録株式 概算株数 発動条件 OpenAIワラント 最大1億6000万株 初期1GWで権利確定開始、完全確定には6GW、最終トランシェに600ドルの株価条件 メタ・ワラント 最大1億6000万株 初期1GWで権利確定開始、完全確定には6GW、最終トランシェに600ドルの株価条件 World Labs対価 1497万8322株 2026年11月13日の取引完了時に発行 Taalas対価 最大195万6002株 クロージング、交換可能、条件付株式 合計 3億3693万4324株 2026年11月18日時点の発行済み株式の約20.3% 注：OpenAIとメタの双方について、ワラントの行使価格は1株0.01ドル（約1.6円）。 市場への圧迫は「洪水」ではなく「重し」 この区別は、今回の申請をどう読むべきかを左右する。ワラントは数ギガワット規模の調達コミットメントと段階的に上昇する株価目標に連動しているため、株式が一度に市場に出回ることはない。実際の売却が起きるとしても、それは数年規模で続くハードウェア納品と権利確定のマイルストーンを経た後であり、OpenAIとメタが保有を選ぶか売却するかにもかかる。 投資家が追うべき点は2つ残る。GPU購入コミットメントに対する進捗と、ワラント保有者による転売意向の開示だ。もう1つの考慮点は、買収によって登録プールに約1700万株が加わったことだ。ワラントのブロックに比べれば小さいが、ベンチャーや戦略的株主による退出の可能性に紐づく供給源ではある。 今回の申請は半導体株の急騰後に出された。AMDは月曜日の通常取引で約7%高と引け、2026年の上昇率を112%に拡大した。NVIDIAの取締役会がジェンスン・フアンを最高経営責任者（CEO）に即時復帰させたことを受け、業界全体が急伸した流れに乗った形だ。NVIDIA株は取引終了時に31%超高だった。AMDは登録が公表された後の夜間取引で約1.1%下落した。 株式に対する売り手アナリストの見方は引き続き強気だ。TipRanksが集計する平均目標株価は652.26ドルで、現水準から約43.8%の上昇余地を示す。28件の「買い」と3件の「保有」による「強い買い」のコンセンサスが形成されている。 AIハードウェア関連全体にとって、今回の申請はAMDがハイパースケールとの提携をどう組み立てたかを示す異例の窓となる。アンカー顧客に現金を支払うのではなく、顧客がInstinctアクセラレータを中心にデータセンターを拡張するにつれて株式に転換される持分を約束したのだ。この整合は両刃の剣だ。OpenAIとメタをAMDのロードマップに縛り付ける一方、GPU分野での成功が取引可能な株式数を着実に増やすことを意味する。

records.title: OpenAIが蒸留対策を公開、AIの「思考過程」を抜き取る攻撃の成功率を54%から0.2%に
records.excerpt: OpenAIは11月20日、自社のAIモデルの出力を無断で集めて別のモデルの学習に使う「敵対的蒸留」への対策を 公開 しました。新しいGPT-6.2 AstraとGPT-6.2 Solで防御を強め、モデルの内部の思考過程を抜き取る攻撃の成功率を、54.0%から0.2%に下げたとしています。 蒸留は、あるモデルの出力を別のモデルの学習データにする一般的な手法です。OpenAIが問題にしているのは、これを無断で行い、元のモデルにあった安全策を引き継がないまま能力だけを写し取ることです。たとえばOpenAIのモデルは、サイバー攻撃を手伝うよう求められると断ります。しかし、その出力を学習して脆弱性を見つける能力だけを写し取った別のモデルには、この歯止めがありません。元のモデルなら断る攻撃の手助けをそのまま引き受けてしまうおそれがあるというわけです。 特に防御しようとしているのは、モデルが答えを出すまでに内部で生成する推論の過程です。最終的な答えには出ない情報を含み、学習データとしての価値が高いためです。 OpenAIは、推論の過程が盗まれるとどれだけ余計に能力が写し取られるのかを、社内の実験で確認しました。まず自社モデルに、コーディングと防御的なセキュリティの作業をさせ、その記録を教材にします。次に、同じ状態のモデルを2つ用意し、片方には推論の過程をそのまま、もう片方には利用者にふだん見えている最終的な答えと推論の要約だけを学習させました。 学習の直後に比べると、推論をそのまま学んだモデルのほうが、おおむね高い成績でした。さらに訓練を重ねた後は、回答に使える計算量が多い条件では同じ傾向が続き、少ない条件では要約で学んだモデルが上回りました。 OpenAIはこの結果から、推論の過程を守ることが能力の流出を抑えるのに役立つとみています。教材にしたのは、どれも規約で認められた作業のやり取りです。それでも数が集まれば、攻撃にも使える技能が身に付いてしまうとしています。 対策は2つの層に分かれます。1つは個々のリクエストへの対策です。推論を明かさないようモデルを訓練し、入力と出力を分類器で検査します。出力の検査は、ツールを呼び出すときの引数も対象です。最終的な答えに出さなくても、引数に推論が漏れることがあるためです。API側では、推論を、それを生んだ会話の履歴に結び付けました。過去のメッセージを書き換えると、それ以降の推論はAPIが破棄します。古い世代のモデルに新しいモデルの推論を読ませることもできなくしました。 もう1つは、組織的な抜き取りの検出です。リクエストやアカウントの傾向から協調した動きを見つけ、関係するアカウント群をまとめて停止します。今年は複数の事例があり、週あたりの停止は数千から数万アカウントの規模で、夏に大きく増えたとしています。見つけた手がかりは他のモデル提供企業とも共有しています。 効果の測定では、6種類の攻撃用モデルに、相手の反応を見ながら手口を変える攻撃をさせました。以前のリクエストで生成された推論を取り出す攻撃の成功率は、当初の安全策のGPT-6 Astraで54.0%、GPT-6.2 Astraで0.2%。現在のリクエストの推論を取り出す攻撃は22.9%から0.9%になりました。一部の改善はGPT-6 Astraにも適用を進めています。 OpenAIはこの問題を安全保障上のリスクとも位置づけています。2月にはDeepSeekが米国の先端モデルの蒸留を試みていたとして議会に説明し、9月には推論を抜き取る活動の中核部分を、Kimiを開発するMoonshot AIの関係者によるものと報告したとしています。外国の主体を特定し制裁する手段を政府に与える立法を支持する立場も示しました。

records.label: ai.watch.impress.co.jp
records.title: OpenAIとCisco、再起動不要でLinuxを守るOSS「Shirudo」 AIエージェントが脆弱性を調査し一時的な防御策を生成
records.excerpt: OpenAIとCisco、再起動不要でLinuxを守るOSS「Shirudo」 - AI Watch 検索 閉じる ニュース OpenAIとCisco、再起動不要でLinuxを守るOSS「Shirudo」 AIエージェントが脆弱性を調査し一時的な防御策を生成 編集部：中野信二 2026年11月24日 13:52 オープンソースランタイム「Shirudo」 OpenAIとCiscoは11月23日（米国時間）、パッチの適用やシステムの再起動を必要とせず、稼働中のLinuxシステムを保護するオープンソースランタイム「Shirudo」を発表した。 OpenAIのフロンティアAIやセキュリティ・インフラ研究と、Ciscoのインフラおよびセキュリティの専門知識を組み合わせたプロジェクトであり、開発者やセキュリティ研究者、インフラ運用者に向けて開発への参加を呼びかけている。 脆弱性の発見後、パッチのテストと展開には数日から数週間を要する場合がある。その間、攻撃（エクスプロイト）と正当なリクエストが同じLinuxの操作に依存しているケースでは、該当操作を完全にブロックするとサービス自体が停止する可能性がある。 OpenAI社長兼共同創業者であるGreg Brockman氏は、バグを発見しても翌日に全システムへパッチを適用することは難しく、修正プログラムの構築と展開を進める間も稼働し続けるシステムを保護するためにCiscoと緊密に連携していると述べている。 日本語の「シールド」に由来するShirudoは、このトレードオフに対処するために設計された。運用チームは「シールド」と呼ばれる一時的な保護機能が脆弱性を突く挙動のみを遮断し、正当なリクエストを通過させるかを事前にテストしたうえで、承認後にサービスを稼働させたまま展開する仕組みを備える。 Shirudoは、OS内部の特定のポイントで小さなプログラムを実行するLinux技術「eBPF」を採用している。これにより、ガーディアンエージェントがカーネルやネットワーク上の不審な活動を監視し、稼働中のシステムに対して的を絞ったセキュリティ保護を適用する。 ガーディアンエージェントがeBPFを使用して稼働中のシステムを監視・保護する仕組み 同ランタイムは、下記の4つの主要機能を中心に設計されている。 ライブ保護（Live protection） システムを再起動することなくeBPFシールドによって脆弱なコードパスを遮断し、提案されたシールドを適用する前に、アプリケーションにどのような影響を与えるかを監視する。 マシン速度での防御（Defense at machine speed） AIエージェントにプログラム可能な制御機能を提供し、脆弱性の調査、標的型防御の開発、実際のワークロードやエクスプロイトに対する有効性の検証を行なうが、最終的な展開の判断はセキュリティチームが管理する。 信頼された展開（Trusted deployment） ロード前にシールドの暗号署名と検証を実施し、LinuxのeBPF検証ツールによる安全規則の確認と、カーネルのセキュリティ制御によって不正な変更を制限する。 ハードウェアベースの検証（Hardware-backed verification） トラステッドプラットフォームモジュール（TPM）を使用し、保護機能のロードや削除に関する検証可能な記録を保持し、運用者がセキュリティ要件への適合を確認する際の根拠として利用する。 実証例として、管理下でのテストにおいてOpenAIのAIエージェント「Codex」が生成したシールドを用い、稼働中のElasticsearchサービスに対する「Java4Shell」脆弱性の悪用試行をブロックした事例が紹介されている。 長期的な目標として、OpenAIとCiscoは新たな脅威に適応しつつ信頼性を維持するインフラ基盤の強化を掲げている。カーネルやコアサービスの強化、ワークロード権限の制限、アップデートとリカバリの安全性向上などの保護機能を展開するために、防御担当者とAIエージェントが影響を受けるシステムを迅速に特定し、ワークロードを中断することなく、eBPFシールドを展開可能にする。 また、フロンティアAIとセキュリティ研究を組み合わせて脆弱性の発見や現実的な攻撃に対する防御テストを実行し、侵害の検知と封じ込め、システム間の横展開の防止、検証済みの正常な状態へのサービス復旧を容易にすることを目指す。個々のシステムが侵害された場合でも、ハードウェアベースの認証と独立したネットワーク制御によって追加の保証を提供するとしている。 両社はコードの検査や保護機能のテスト、開発への貢献を可能にするため、ShirudoをGitHubでオープンソース公開した。ShirudoはBSD 2条項ライセンスに基づいて提供されており、BPFプログラムについてはBSDとGPLのデュアルライセンスとなっている。 現在、テスト用保護機能の署名・ロード・検証を試す仮想マシン（VM）のクイックスタートや、Isovalentのセルフガイドラボ、公式ドキュメントが公開されている。12月15日に開催する技術解説ウェビナー（technical deep dive）の参加登録を受け付けている。 両社は今後、脆弱性情報の公開とあわせて検証済みの防御策を提供し、運用担当者が恒久的なパッチを準備する間の一時的な保護手段として評価・展開できる体制を整えるとしている。 URL 🔗ニュースリリース https://openai.com/index/introducing-shirudo/ 🔗OpenAI https://openai.com/ 🔗Cisco https://www.cisco.com/ 🔗shirudo-dev/shirudo: eBPF-based security platform https://github.com/shirudo-dev/shirudo 🔗Deep Dive into Shirudo https://isovalent.com/events/shirudo-virtual-panel/

records.title: OpenAIとCisco、未修正のLinuxシステムを守るオープンソースの盾「Shirudo」を公開
records.excerpt: OpenAIとCiscoは、修正プログラムの準備中に稼働中のLinuxシステム上でエクスプロイトの経路をeBPFで遮断するオープンソースランタイム「Shirudo」を公開した。2026年11月23日に発表されたこのプロジェクトは、署名済みで検証可能な「シールド」を中心に据え、実運用ワークロードに対して事前にテストできるようにすることで、サービスを中断させる再起動を回避する。制御されたテストでは、OpenAIのCodexで生成したシールドが、稼働中のElasticsearchサービスに対するJava4Shellエクスプロイトを再起動なしで遮断した。コードはBSD 2条項ライセンスで提供され、BPFプログラムはBSDとGPLのデュアルライセンスとなっており、両社は外部からの貢献を呼びかけている。OpenAIのGreg Brockman社長は、修正プログラムの構築と展開を進めながらも稼働を続けなければならないシステムをチームが保護できるようにすることが狙いだと述べた。 OpenAIとCisco Systemsは、恒久的な修正プログラムがまだ作成・テストされている間に、セキュリティチームがLinuxマシンをエクスプロイトから守れるようにするオープンソースランタイム「Shirudo」を公開した。プロジェクトは2026年11月23日に発表され、コードはBSD 2条項ライセンスで提供され、BPFプログラムはBSDとGPLのデュアルライセンスとなっている。 名称は日本語の「シールド（盾）」に由来し、設計の中心にある仕組みを表している。すなわち、周囲のサービスを停止させることなく、脆弱性を露呈させる特定の動作を遮断する、一時的で的を絞った保護措置である。 このトレードオフこそが、Shirudoが解決すべく作られた課題だ。修正プログラムのテストと展開には数日から数週間かかることがあり、その間、攻撃者のエクスプロイトと正当なリクエストが同じLinuxの操作に依存している場合がある。その操作を一律に遮断すればサービスが停止しかねず、防御側は露出かダウンタイムかの二者択一を迫られる。 Shirudoは、オペレーティングシステムのカーネル内の定められた箇所で小さなプログラムを実行するLinux技術、eBPF上に構築されている。この配置により、ランタイムは不審な活動を監視し、再起動したシステムではなく稼働中のシステムに保護を適用できる。 OpenAIとCiscoは、このプロジェクトを4つの機能を中心に構成している。 機能 内容 ライブ保護 eBPFシールドが再起動なしで脆弱なコード経路を遮断する。チームは適用前に、提案されたシールドがアプリケーションに与える影響をプレビューできる マシンスピードの防御 プログラマブルな制御により、エージェントが脆弱性を調査し、シールドを構築し、エクスプロイトや実運用ワークロードに対してテストできる。何を出荷するかはセキュリティチームが判断する 信頼できる展開 シールドは読み込み前に暗号学的に署名・検証される。カーネルのeBPF検証器がプログラムを安全規則に照らしてチェックし、カーネルの制御機構が不正な変更を制限する ハードウェアに裏付けられた検証 Trusted Platform Moduleが、読み込まれた、または削除された保護措置の検証可能な記録を保持し、運用担当者はこれを用いてシステムがセキュリティ要件を満たしていることを確認できる 制御されたテストでは、OpenAIのCodexツールで生成したシールドが、稼働中のElasticsearchサービスに対するJava4Shellエクスプロイトの試行を再起動なしで遮断した。シールドはJavaのBase64デコーダに入力チェックを追加し、稼働中のプロセスに直接アタッチされた。エクスプロイトが試行されると、シールドは悪意ある入力を拒否し、サービスは稼働を続けた。 OpenAIの社長兼共同創業者であるGreg Brockman氏は、今回の公開を、欠陥の発見とその全システムでの解消との間のギャップへの対応と位置づけた。「われわれは防御側に対し、脆弱性をより迅速に見つけて修正するための優れたモデルとツールを提供しているが、今日バグを見つけたからといって、明日すべてのシステムに修正を適用できるわけではない」と同氏は述べた。さらに両社は緊密に協力し、チームが修正プログラムの構築と展開を進めながらも稼働を続ける必要のあるシステムを保護できるようにしていること、またツールをオープンに構築することで、あるチームの優れた手法を他の全員がゼロから作り直す必要がなくなることを付け加えた。 このプロジェクトは、OpenAIの最先端AIとセキュリティ研究を、Ciscoのインフラとセキュリティの専門知識と組み合わせている。技術的な解説はLinux Plumbers Conferenceで発表され、Cisco傘下のIsovalentが自主学習用ラボを提供している。技術ウェビナーは12月15日に予定されている。 長期的な狙いは修正プログラムの適用期間にとどまらない。両社によれば、カーネルと中核サービスを堅牢化し、自動生成されたポリシーの下でアプリケーションが必要なものだけを備えて動作するようワークロードの権限を制限し、更新と復旧をより安全にしたい考えだ。掲げられた目標は、防御側とAIエージェントが影響を受けるシステムを迅速に特定し、保護措置を検証し、ワークロードを中断させることなくeBPFシールドを展開できるインフラであり、個々のマシンが侵害されたとしてもハードウェアに裏付けられた認証と独立したネットワーク制御が保証を提供する。 Shirudoは、開発者、セキュリティ研究者、インフラ運用担当者がコードを検査し、保護措置をテストし、開発に貢献できるよう公開されている。両社はまた、テスト済みのシールドを脆弱性の開示と併せて提供し、恒久的な修正プログラムの準備中に運用担当者が評価・展開できるものを提供したい考えだ。 Linuxおよびエンタープライズセキュリティ市場にとって、今回の公開は、開示から修正までの期間を業界がどう扱うかという転換点を示している。この期間はこれまで、ネットワークレベルのフィルタリング、緊急メンテナンス、あるいは単にリスクを受け入れることで対応されてきた。署名済みで監査可能なカーネルレベルの暫定措置を運用担当者に渡すことで、この期間を大幅に短縮できる可能性がある一方、シールド承認プロセスの重要性も高まる。範囲設定を誤ったシールドは、攻撃者のリクエストと同様に効果的に正当なトラフィックを遮断しかねないからだ。オープンソースで寛容なライセンスの手法は、カーネル内の独自エージェントに警戒するインフラ運用担当者の間で採用を加速させる可能性があり、OpenAIのコーディングモデルをソフトウェア開発だけでなく防御的セキュリティ作業のツールとして位置づけることにもなる。

records.title: Richpanel、30日以内にサポート業務の50%自動化を約束、OpenAIのGPT-6シリーズを採用
records.excerpt: Richpanelは、自社のAIサポートプラットフォームが顧客企業のカスタマーサービス業務の50%を30日以内に自動化できるとし、達成できなければ返金する保証を付している。2026年10月までの6カ月間に完了した約300件の導入でこの保証を満たしたと主張している。同社のアプローチの鍵は「Boss AI」と呼ばれるAIマネージャーで、OpenAIのGPT-6 AstraとGPT-6.1 Solを基盤に構築され、手順書の作成やフロントラインのエージェントが必要とするツールの接続を行う。実際の顧客対応にはより安価なGPT-6 Lunaを使用し、1件あたりの対応コストを外部委託サポート以下に抑える。CEOのAmit RG氏は、保証対象のすべての導入でAIが顧客満足度において人間のエージェントを上回ったと述べているが、これは独立した検証を受けた主張ではない。同社はEコマースブランドをターゲットとし、ZendeskやGorgiasと競合する。 アジア太平洋地域のサポートテクノロジー新興企業Richpanelは、導入初月のうちに顧客企業のカスタマーサービス業務の半分をAIに引き渡せるとし、達成できなければ契約金額を返金すると表明している。同社によると、2026年10月にCEOへ取材した時点から遡る6カ月間に完了した約300件のAIサポート導入において、この「30日で50%」という保証を満たしてきたという。 この提案の核心は、チャットの品質そのものよりも、ボットが顧客に回答する前に何が行われるかにある。CEOのAmit RG（アミット・RG）氏によれば、人間のサポートエージェントは1件の案件を解決するために20〜30ものツールを使い分けることがあり、その手順は文書化されておらず、従業員の頭の中にしか存在しないことも多い。AIエージェントにこうした知識に基づいて行動させるには、通常、顧客先に常駐するエンジニアがシステムに接続し、ルールを明文化する必要がある。 アミット氏の答えは、そのエンジニアをソフトウェアとして構築することだった。Richpanelは、手順書を起草し、同社のフロントラインサポートエージェント、コパイロット、品質保証エージェントが必要なツールをどのように呼び出すかを定義するAIマネージャーを開発した。顧客企業はこれを「Boss AI」と呼ぶようになった。この設定作業はGPT-6 AstraとGPT-6.1 Sol上で実行される。この段階での誤りは下流のすべてに波及するため、精度を重視して選ばれたモデルだ。 実際の会話対応では、コストが制約条件となる。Richpanelのフロントラインエージェントは数十万件のやり取りを処理するよう設計されており、1件あたりの価格がモデル選定を左右する。同社はこの大量処理をGPT-6 Lunaとその他のOpenAIモデルに振り向け、コパイロットや品質保証エージェントにも同じ論理を適用している。 「重要なのはコストと知能のバランスだ」とアミット氏は述べた。多くの見込み顧客はすでに低コストの外部委託サポートを購入しているため、自動化は能力だけでなく経済性でもその基準を上回る必要があると同氏は指摘する。OpenAIについては、長いコンテキストを保持し、1件あたりのコストを膨らませることなく長めのタスクを処理できるモデルを提供していると評価し、これによりRichpanelは準備段階にはより深い推論を、会話そのものには安価なモデルを適用できると述べた。 アミット氏は、保証の対象となったすべての導入において、AIが顧客満足度で人間のエージェントを上回ったと述べている。これらの主張は独立した検証を受けていない。 同社は、サポート件数が人員を上回るペースで増えているEコマースブランドを狙い、ZendeskやGorgiasといった既存のヘルプデスクプラットフォームに対抗する位置づけを取っている。その中核的な約束――迅速な応答、1チケットあたりの低コスト、高い満足度スコア――は、この分野のすべてのベンダーが掲げる同じ三角形であり、顧客企業自身のカタログ、ポリシー、注文システムを接続した後に自動化率が維持されることをRichpanelが証明する責任を負うことになる。 購入者にとっては、返金保証の仕組みが導入リスクの多くをベンダー側に移し、財務部門が比較検証できる明確な基準を与える。より広いコンタクトセンターソフトウェア市場にとって、より重要なシグナルはこの2層のモデル戦略だ。つまり、推論重視のシステムが設定を担い、安価なシステムが会話を担う。この分担が大規模に機能すれば、サービス業務の自動化におけるコストの下限が下がり、人間のエージェントが大半のチケットを処理することを前提に価格設定している既存事業者への圧力が強まる。
