records.excerpt: 移動の喜びと安全を両立する運転支援機能を──二輪領域の新たな技術をHondaから | Me and Honda, Career | Hondaの人＝原動力を伝える HONDA The Power of Dreams HONDA The Power of Dreams 新卒採用 中途採用 Menu SHARE ON Sustainable impacts 2026/11/24 移動の喜びと安全を両立する運転支援機能を──二輪領域の新たな技術をHondaから 新卒入社 研究開発（IT・通信・AI） コネクテッド 最先端技術 キャリアチェンジ スキルアップ・成長環境 SHARE 四輪領域でデータサイエンティストとしてキャリアを歩んだ後、二輪の運転支援機能開発へ──社内公募で新たな挑戦を始めた熊谷。二輪ならではのハードウェアの制約や開発環境の違いに戸惑いながらも、ものづくりの手応えを感じています。移動の喜びと安全を両立させた機能開発に挑むやりがいを聞きました。 熊谷 優惟子 Yuiko Kumagai 二輪・パワープロダクツ事業本部 二輪・パワープロダクツ開発生産統括部 商品技術開発部 安全技術開発課 学生時代は脳波解析などの生体信号処理を専攻。2018年Hondaに新卒入社。四輪のコネクテッド領域にてデータの分析や利活用業務に従事し、二輪向け連携アプリなどの開発にも携わる。2025年秋に社内公募で二輪領域へ異動。現在は運転支援機能における画像認識技術開発を担当している。 画像認識技術の性能・評価検討から実車検証まで。二輪特有の制約のなかで安全をつくる 熊谷が所属するのは、二輪における運転支援機能の開発を行う部署。特定の車種にとどまらず、横断的に展開できる技術を生み出す役割を担います。 そのなかで熊谷が担当するのは、画像認識技術の開発。画像認識技術はさまざまな機能に関わります。そのため、求められる性能や評価の考え方を検討するだけでなく、画像認識やAIの観点から、運転支援機能の仕様についても関係者と議論しながら開発を進めます。さらに、実車での検証から得られたデータを分析しながら、AI機能としての品質をつくり込んでいます。 そこには、二輪ならではの難しさがあると熊谷は言います。 「二輪にはさまざまな制約があります。まず、車体が小さいため、必要な機器を搭載する場所が制限されます。また、1台あたりにかけられるコストを抑えるため、四輪に比べると処理能力が限られた半導体チップでシステムを成り立たせる必要があるのです。 さらに、走行時には車体が左右に傾斜したり上下に揺れたりします。そのなかで求められる性能をどのように定め、品質を担保するか。とても難しい挑戦です」 二輪特有の制約はありながらも、お客様の求める機能を実現したい──そのために、迷った際に立ち返るのは「お客様視点」だと話します。 「技術的な検討を進める際にも、お客様が求めている価値や困りごとを起点に、どのような機能が必要なのかを考えるようにしています。 また、実際の走行データなどに基づくことも大切です。必要なデータの収集・分析と、お客様視点から考えることの両輪で進めることが重要だと感じています」 人の生活に役立つ技術をつくりたい。新たな価値創造に挑戦するため二輪領域へ 学生時代は、脳波や眼電図といった微弱な信号を解析する生体信号処理分野の研究室に所属し、AIや機械学習を活用した研究をしていた熊谷。将来は、AIを使って人の生活に役立つ技術を開発したいと考えていました。 「AI領域の研究をするなかで、人工知能が人間を置き去りにして勝手に進歩していくのではないかという懸念を抱いていました。そうではなく、『人と協調して、人の生活に役立つための技術』をつくりたい。 そう思っていた時に興味を持ったのが、『Honda CI（Cooperative Intelligence）』です。周囲の環境を認識しながら人とコミュニケーションをとり、自ら判断する協調人工知能というコンセプトに惹かれたことが、Hondaに入社を決めた理由です」 2018年に入社後、最初に配属されたのは四輪のコネクテッド領域を担う部署。データサイエンティストとして車両データを用いた停車時間予測技術の研究で学会発表を行ったり、PL（プロジェクトリーダー）として車両向け音楽アプリの企画・開発を行ったりと、実績を積んでいきます。 今につながる転機となったのは、バイクとスマートフォンをつなげて、バイクの運転中でもナビや音楽機能を操作できるようにするアプリ「 Honda RoadSync 」の開発に携わったことでした。 「じつは、内定式に参加した時に、会場に展示されていた『 Monkey 』という小さなバイクに一目ぼれして、入社後に普通二輪免許を取得したんです。実際に乗ってみると、クラッチ操作など自分で機械を操っている実感を得られるバイクの運転がとても楽しくて。 そんななか、たまたま『Honda RoadSync』のプロジェクトに関わることになりました。収集したアプリのログデータを分析し、UXを改善していく仕事をしながら、自分もバイクに乗るからこそ得られる気づきがたくさんあって、二輪領域でのものづくりがとてもおもしろかったんです。AIや運転支援機能という領域にも興味があったので、社内公募に挑戦し、2025年の秋に現在の部署に異動しました」 AIを活用した運転支援機能のなかでも、あえて二輪領域に挑戦したのは、「バイクが好き」という想いに加えて、新しい技術や価値を生み出していくおもしろさもあったと話します。 「二輪の運転支援機能には、まださまざまな可能性が広がっています。正解がひとつではない難しい課題に向き合い、自分たちで考えながら新しい技術を形にしていけることに魅力を感じました。また、グローバルに展開しているHondaだからこそリードしていける分野だと感じたことも大きな理由です」 分野の壁と技術の壁。チームで開発する難しさと、その先にあるものづくりの手応え 四輪のデータ分析から二輪の運転支援機能開発へ。環境が大きく変化したことに戸惑いもあったと言います。 「二輪の開発現場に来てはじめに驚いたのは、担当範囲の広さと、ハードウェア開発チームとの距離の近さです。 四輪領域で仕事をしていた時は、機能開発ではなく開発後のデータを扱うことが中心でしたが、今はハードウェアの設計者や社内外の関係者らと密に連携しながら仕事を進めています。運転支援機能開発でもデータ分析は重要ですが、皆の専門領域は異なります。そのため、データ分析の専門用語を使う際には、概念や言葉の定義を丁寧に確認しながら進めることを心がけています」 加えて、それぞれが担当する機能ごとに求める性能が変わる点も、リードする上での難しさを増していると話します。 「走行環境や機能によって、画像認識に求められる性能や重視すべき評価軸は異なります。複数の条件を踏まえ、製品全体として適切な評価方法を組み立てることが難しさのひとつですね」 そんな高い壁を乗り越える原動力となっているのが、自ら手掛けた技術が実車として形になっていく「ものづくり」の喜びです。 「データ分析では、分析結果から改善点を提案することが主な仕事でしたが、今は仕様検討から実車のテストまで直接関わることができます。 事故データの分析結果などを参考に、『こういうシーンで作動する機能がいいのではないか』と皆で議論しながら具体的な機能を考え、実車に取り付けて目の前で動く姿を確認できます。自分たちで手掛けたものをお客様に届けるという、メーカーならではの仕事に挑戦できている手応えがあります」 自らの手で進められるやりがいを胸に、二輪の運転支援機能をHondaがリードしたい 難しい課題に向き合いながらも、「違う環境に飛び込むことが好きなんです」と笑う熊谷。自ら社内公募に手を挙げ、新たなフィールドに足を踏み入れたように、やりたいことに挑戦できる環境がHondaの魅力だと語ります。 「意思を持って発信することで、誰でも挑戦の機会を得られる環境だと感じています。主体的に進め方を考えて組み立てていく場面では難しさを感じることもありますが、見方を変えれば、自ら提案して進めていけるおもしろさがあるということ。 自分なりの想いを持ち、新しいことに挑戦したい方は、Hondaの環境を楽しめるのではないでしょうか」 Hondaは、「2050年に全世界で、Hondaの二輪車・四輪車が関与する交通事故死者ゼロ」をめざしています。その実現に向けて、二輪領域における運転支援機能の進歩は重要なテーマです。 「バイクは風を感じながら走る楽しさがある反面、事故が起きてしまった際には四輪に比べて人的被害が大きくなりやすい乗り物です。だからといって運転支援機能を詰め込みすぎると、快適なライディングを阻害する機能になってしまうかもしれません。 バイクに乗る楽しさを邪魔することなくライダーの運転を支援することで、移動の喜びと安全を両立させ、ライダーから『この機能があるから安心して走れる』と信頼してもらえる技術をつくりたいのです。二輪の運転支援機能は開発途上の段階です。だからこそHondaが率先して取り組んでいくべき技術だと思っています。 まずは、今取り組んでいる運転支援機能を製品としてお客様に届けることを目標に、その先には、AIを使って人の生活が豊かになる技術を開発していきたいですね」 移動の喜びと安全をかなえる技術で、バイクに乗る楽しさをさらに大きなものへ──壁にぶつかる難しさをやりがいに変えながら、未知なる領域への挑戦を楽しみます。 ※ 記載内容は2026年9月時点のものです records.title: F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix results changed as FIA announce post-race penalties
records.excerpt: One of the most unusual races in recent years took place but there was no unusual winner as Max Verstappen showed supreme class to take victory at the Las Vegas Grand Prix. Photo: © IMAGO Change your timezone: Las Vegas Grand Prix F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix results changed as FIA announce post-race penalties The final results from the Nevada Strip Dan Ripley Global Editor Professional F1 journalist and analyst Sunday 22 November 2026 15:57 Make us your Google favorite One of the most unusual races in recent years took place but there was no unusual winner as Max Verstappen showed supreme class to take victory at the Las Vegas Grand Prix. In a race that never settled down into any particular race order, the likes of Lando Norris , Oscar Piastri, Kimi Antonelli, George Russell , Isack Hadjar and even Alpine's Pierre Gasly all spent time in the top three before ultimately it was the McLaren drivers led by the 2025 world champion following Verstappen onto the podium. Antonelli and Gasly took fourth and fifth, with the latter's team-mate Franco Colapinto taking sixth to score big points for Alpine. Article continues under video Lewis Hamilton battled back from a 10-second penalty to finish seventh, with Carlos Sainz pipping Russell on the line to finish eighth. Having finished seventh on the road, a 10-second penalty for a clumsy tap on his team-mate Hamilton meant Charles Leclerc was demoted to the final points paying position in 10th. There was also a late penalty handed out to Hadjar, who was penalised for driving too slowly under the safety car , although this had no major impact on his result dropping him one place below Liam Lawson's Racing Bull to finish 15th. Here are the final classified results from the Las Vegas Grand Prix. F1 HEADLINES: Hamilton vs Leclerc boils over AGAIN as Ferrari collision causes bizarre crash F1 Results: Las Vegas Grand Prix Las Vegas Grand Prix Race Results Pos Driver Team Gap 1 Max Verstappen Red Bull 1:27:39.624 2 Lando Norris McLaren +0.639s 3 Oscar Piastri McLaren +1.529s 4 Kimi Antonelli Mercedes +2.574s 5 Pierre Gasly Alpine +2.927s 6 Franco Colapinto Alpine +7.955s 7 Lewis Hamilton Ferrari +12.795s 8 Carlos Sainz Williams +12.938s 9 George Russell Mercedes +13.192s 10 * Charles Leclerc Ferrari +17.554s 11 Nico Hulkenberg Audi +22.720s 12 Gabriel Bortoleto Audi +28.602s 13 Ollie Bearman Haas +28.843s 14 Liam Lawson Racing Bulls +36.588s 15 *Isack Hadjar Red Bull +46.488s 16 Rafael Camara Haas +47.814s 17 Lance Stroll Aston Martin +68.353s 18 Valtteri Bottas Cadillac +71.673s 19 Fernando Alonso Aston Martin DNF NC Arvid Lindblad Racing Bulls DNF NC Sergio Perez Cadillac DNF NC Alex Albon Williams DNS * Charles Leclerc penalised 10 seconds for causing a collision * Isack Hadjar penalised 10 seconds for driving unnecessarily slowly When is the next F1 race? There are only two more F1 races left in the 2026 season and they are coming at you fast! One week after the Vegas action F1 heads to the Qatar Grand Prix for the penultimate round on November 29. It's a race where if Ferrari's drivers don't keep crashing into each other, they will clinch second in the constructors' championship . In a similar vane, despite not being in the title battle for the entire season, Verstappen can also secure runner-up in the championship for the second season running. records.title: Lewis Hamilton reignites Charles Leclerc criticism after Las Vegas clash
records.excerpt: Lewis Hamilton reignites Charles Leclerc criticism after Las Vegas clash Taylor Powling 24 Nov 2026 6:01 AM Lewis Hamilton took aim at Charles Leclerc's mentality after their Las Vegas clash Lewis Hamilton appears to have called into question teammate Charles Leclerc’s mentality once more after the two Ferrari drivers collided in the Las Vegas Grand Prix. Following a controversial incident in Mexico, the scrutiny on the Ferrari pairing has intensified again in the wake of Hamilton and Leclerc’s second clash in three races. Lewis Hamilton takes aim at Charles Leclerc again after latest run-in The tension between the two was already running high at the Las Vegas Strip Circuit before their coming together on Lap 38 amid Hamilton’s indignation at Leclerc’s role in him copping a 10-second penalty for leaving the track and gaining a lasting advantage. Hamilton was battling McLaren’s Lando Norris on Lap 12 when Leclerc made it three-wide heading into Turn 7, leading his teammate to go deep and cut across the chicane. Hamilton maintained the position over Norris, prompting the stewards to take action. The Briton disagreed with the decision, highlighting that he was avoiding a collision, while he also voiced his frustration at Leclerc as the duo continued to exchange places. “Charles is just… can you tell him to back the f*** off?! I’m trying to catch these guys ahead,” Hamilton exclaimed on team radio. Leclerc certainly didn’t adhere to his teammate’s wish, though, as later on he spied a gap down Hamilton’s inside at the same corner where they had already had a close call. But Hamilton, on the outside again, didn’t bail out on this occasion and the Ferraris made contact, pitching the seven-time champion into a spin that dropped him to 10th. Having claimed that Leclerc has a long-standing “do or die” attitude towards racing the sister Ferrari, Hamilton, who recovered to seventh place, seemed to condemn his teammate’s mindset again as he suggested that he had not prioritised the team result. “I’ve been there many, many times, and I think just in that point, I mean, just I knew I was quicker,” Hamilton recounted. “[I had] just come back from a 10-second penalty, and I’m literally only thinking about beating McLaren. We have to beat McLaren. “It’s not about us battling behind, and every time we battle, we just lose ground, so let’s just work together and stay in the tow. Let’s keep pushing and catch those guys up ahead. We weren’t on the same frame of mind, I guess, in that. “It ultimately cost us a lot of points today, which is a shame. So, I think the team deserve better, for sure.” More from the Ferrari clash in Las Vegas Ferrari boss signals doubt over ‘unmanageable’ Lewis Hamilton-Leclerc line-up Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari ‘deserve better’ after latest Charles Leclerc clash The stewards laid the blame at Leclerc’s door, handing him a 10-second penalty, but that was little consolation to Hamilton, who believes a podium was within reach given that he had been battling the McLaren duo, who went on to finish second and third. “We knew that we were faced with a massive challenge this weekend,” Hamilton told Sky Sports F1. “We didn’t realise that there’d be such a limitation on these straights. “Qualifying was obviously difficult, but in the race I felt great and I was really progressing well. I really ultimately wanted to try and make sure we finish ahead of the McLarens, because that’s who we’re really fighting in the Constructors. “Then avoiding a collision with one of the McLarens got me a 10-second penalty which was, I think, really harsh and which was frustrating. But I just got my head back down and kept chasing and managed to get back in the fight and then again got knocked back again. But I never gave up and I was just trying to get the best result. I really think we could have had a podium today with the pace we had.” Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur has not ruled out more stringent measures being put in place to avoid the team’s drivers running into each other on track, having seen his reminder to the pair during clear-the-air talks in Brazil fall on deaf ears in Las Vegas. Hamilton has intimated that he is hopeful that the latest incident involving him and Leclerc will be the catalyst for the Italian marque to introduce rules of engagement. “That’s for Ferrari to decide, obviously,” he said. “I’ve done all I can and I’ve said everything and more. It’s been difficult. All I can do is just show up and give it everything I can and hopefully in the background they eventually figure it out.” Read next: Haas makes new announcement ahead of Qatar Grand Prix Ferrari Charles Leclerc Lewis Hamilton

records.title: FIA announce Lewis Hamilton penalty verdict at Las Vegas Grand Prix
records.excerpt: A furious Lewis Hamilton was handed a 10-second time penalty after an incident early in the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Saturday night. Photo: © IMAGO Change your timezone: Las Vegas Grand Prix FIA announce Lewis Hamilton penalty verdict at Las Vegas Grand Prix Disaster for Hamilton on the Strip Graham Shaw Consultant Editor Digital sports specialist running global brands for 30 years Sunday 22 November 2026 05:49 Updated: 05:49 Make us your Google favorite A furious Lewis Hamilton was handed a 10-second time penalty after an incident early in the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Saturday night. The seven-time world champion was again involved in a bitter fight with Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc in the early stages of the race, but it was a skirmish with Lando Norris which saw him fall foul of the stewards. Hamilton overtook the 2025 world champion for P7 on Lap 12 as the pair battled with Leclerc, and then was forced to leave the track as he was squeezed for space. Article continues under video F1 HEADLINES: Oscar Piastri explains shock split as F1 team release statement on driver exit Hamilton hammered by stewards with 10-second penalty The incident was immediately noted by the stewards, who ruled a short time later. And unsurprisingly, it was bad news for Hamilton. The FIA announced that it was a 10-second time penalty for the 41-year-old British star, for leaving the track and gaining an advantage. Hamilton was predictably frustrated, as he said on team radio: “Ah, that’s ****. If I’d turned in, we would have crashed." Hamilton vs Leclerc battle rages on The battle between Hamilton and Leclerc continued after the incident, with both drivers vocal about the other on team radio. Leclerc fumed to race engineer Bryan Bozzi: “He needs to be careful with squeezing because it’s not gonna end well” Hamilton meanwhile was telling his race engineer Carlo Santi: “Charles is just. Can you tell him to back the f*** off? I’m trying to catch these guys ahead” Hamilton came in to take his penalty under Safety Car conditions after a Sergio Perez crash on Lap 19, and came back out in P14. His reaction - "That's unbelievable, absolutely incredible". records.excerpt: The entente cordiale at Ferrari lasted precisely one race as Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc clashed again with disastrous consequences at the F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix on Saturday night. Photo: © IMAGO Change your timezone: Las Vegas Grand Prix FIA announce Charles Leclerc penalty verdict for Lewis Hamilton clash at Las Vegas Grand Prix More disaster for the Scuderia Graham Shaw Consultant Editor Digital sports specialist running global brands for 30 years Sunday 22 November 2026 06:26 Updated: 06:26 Make us your Google favorite The entente cordiale at Ferrari lasted precisely one race as Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc clashed again with disastrous consequences at the F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix on Saturday night. Leclerc was handed a 10-second time penalty for spinning his team-mate around on Lap 38 of an acrimonious battle on the famous Strip. The two Maranello superstars have been at the centre of the biggest story on the grid in recent weeks after their high-profile skirmishes at the Italian and Mexican Grands Prix. Article continues under video The pair held crisis talks with team principal Fred Vasseur after Mexico, with the Frenchman stressing they needed to respect the iconic Ferrari brand. F1 HEADLINES: Oscar Piastri explains shock split as F1 team release statement on driver exit Hamilton vs Leclerc battle boils over again Well the uneasy peace did not last long, as they engaged in a furious battle all night long on the Strip on Saturday night, ending with almost inevitable contact. After starting P10 and P11 on the grid respectively, their fight was always going to be an intriguing subplot to the action up front, and so it proved. As the battle raged, before and Hamilton was handed a 10-second time penalty following a move on McLaren 's Lando Norris , both men raged about the other on team radio. Leclerc fumed to race engineer Bryan Bozzi: “He needs to be careful with squeezing because it’s not gonna end well” Hamilton meanwhile was telling his race engineer Carlo Santi: “Charles is just. Can you tell him to back the f*** off? I’m trying to catch these guys ahead.” After Hamilton made his way back up through the order after taking that penalty, he was again in a battle with Leclerc for P7 when disaster (almost inevitably) struck on Lap 38 of the 50-lap race. Leclerc dived down the inside of Hamilton in an attempt to take P7, and while Hamilton gave the Monegasque room, the pair collided exiting the corner. Hamilton was spun around by the incident and had fallen back to P10 by the time he was able to get going again. After investigating the incident, the FIA later announced that the stewards had given Leclerc a 10-second time penalty for causing a collision. records.excerpt: FIA announces grid penalty for Las Vegas Grand Prix collision Henry Valantine 22 Nov 2026 8:13 AM Sergio Perez retired from the Las Vegas Grand Prix after contact with Rafael Camara. The FIA stewards have decided upon a five-place grid penalty for Sergio Perez for causing a collision with Haas ’ Rafael Camara at the Las Vegas Grand Prix. The Cadillac driver attempted a move into Turn 14, but tagged the rear of the rookie’s car and sent him into a spin, bringing out the Safety Car. FIA stewards confirm Sergio Perez grid penalty Perez had been catching Camara along the Las Vegas Strip Straight, and moved to the inside ahead of the left-right-left sequence of Turns 14-16, but made contact with the Brazilian while doing so. While a 10-second time penalty would normally have been the punishment for such a moment, because Perez retired from the race as a result of the collision, that has been converted to a five-place grid penalty for the Qatar Grand Prix instead. “The Stewards noted that at no point during the manoeuvre was the front axle of Car 11 [Perez] at least alongside the mirror of Car 51 [Camara],” the verdict explained. “The two cars collided at the entry to Turn 14, resulting in Car 11 retiring from the Race. Applying the Driving Standards Guidelines, the Stewards determined that Car 11 had not earned the right to the corner and was wholly to blame for the collision.” Perez attributed some of the blame to the overtake mode capabilities placed on the 2026 cars, with the slipstream effect exaggerated to its fullest extent at the Las Vegas Grand Prix. With that, he did not think Camara would have seen him coming or been expecting a move, because of how far behind Perez was heading onto the Strip. More from the Las Vegas Grand Prix Max Verstappen survives Mercedes onslaught in spectacular Las Vegas Grand Prix thriller Max Verstappen pokes fun at George Russell in Las Vegas GP team radio “It’s this overtake mode, it’s so artificial that basically I exited Turn 12 a second away from Camara, so Camara thought he was completely safe, but then into Turn 14 I was alongside him,” the Cadillac driver explained. “But, when I saw that he was doing a normal line, I tried to avoid him, and it was just too late.” Camara admitted he thought his race was done as a result of being spun around, though he eventually recovered onto the road to take 16th place at the line. “I thought it was over there,” he said. “I don’t know how it didn’t damage anything because we came back and it was all right. We just had to change tyres and came back into it. “I think I was quite surprised with that, and after that we had some fun in the restart, and then after was just a bit more boring being alone.” Read next: Lewis Hamilton fumes at Las Vegas penalty as Charles Leclerc comparison emerges

records.excerpt: FIA explains Charles Leclerc punishment after Lewis Hamilton Las Vegas GP incident Jamie Woodhouse 22 Nov 2026 1:32 PM Charles Leclerc received a 10-second penalty after colliding with Lewis Hamilton The FIA stewards considered Charles Leclerc “wholly to blame” for a fresh clash with Ferrari teammate Lewis Hamilton at the Las Vegas Grand Prix. As a result, the stewards hit Leclerc with a 10-second time penalty. He was ultimately classified 10th. Charles Leclerc got 10-second penalty for Lewis Hamilton incident It was only at the prior round in Brazil that Hamilton and Leclerc squashed the beef stemming from their Mexican GP incident. The pair arrived in Sin City as a united front, Leclerc even suggesting that the media had overblown the situation. By Las Vegas Grand Prix Saturday, there were fresh fireworks between the Ferrari drivers. While Mexico City saw neither driver make Turn 4, opening the door for Max Verstappen, this time, there was a collision between the red cars. As Hamilton eyed-up the McLaren of Oscar Piastri, Leclerc mounted an attack of his own on the Brit into Turn 7. His front right clipped the rear left of the sister Ferrari, sending Hamilton spinning. He dropped to 10th. That triggered an investigation from the FIA stewards, the verdict a 10-second penalty for Leclerc, who was deemed to have caused the collision. Their explanation reads: “The stewards reviewed video and in-car video evidence. “Car 16 attempted to overtake Car 44 on the inside at Turn 7. The Stewards noted that Car 16 initiated the overtaking manoeuvre from a considerable distance behind Car 44, attempting to position his car on the inside. “In assessing the incident, the stewards also took into account the FIA Driving Standards Guidelines, in particular the criteria applicable to overtaking manoeuvres on the inside of a corner. “The stewards determined that the front axle of Car 16 was not at least alongside the mirror of Car 44 at the apex of the corner. “The stewards therefore determined that Car 16 had not earned the right to the corner at Turn 7 and was wholly to blame for the resulting collision. “Accordingly, the stewards imposed a 10-second time penalty.” Ferrari team boss Fred Vasseur had already reminded his drivers after Mexico that the team comes first, so was furious with the pair after this latest flashpoint. He called out a “lack of respect” shown by his drivers towards the team and its sponsors. Leclerc was quick to apologise for his role in the incident post-race. “The race didn’t finish well for us, and my mistake was part of that,” he said. “I accept the penalty and we will review what I could have done differently so it doesn’t happen again. “I’m sorry for the team, for everyone in Maranello and for the points we lost today.” More on Ferrari from PlanetF1.com Telemetry reveals full Ferrari impact of Hamilton, Leclerc clash in Las Vegas Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari ‘deserve better’ after latest Charles Leclerc clash Hamilton was ultimately classified P7. Ferrari failed to wrap-up second in the Constructors’ standings in Las Vegas, but with Red Bull 77 points behind, and a maximum of 86 still up for grabs, P2 is almost certain to go Ferrari’s way. records.excerpt: Liam Lawson vents FIA frustration after Las Vegas GP false start Henry Valantine 22 Nov 2026 6:01 PM From a fuel leak to starting a lap down, it was a difficult Saturday night for Liam Lawson. Liam Lawson shared his frustration at both starting the Las Vegas Grand Prix a lap down, and not receiving the chance to claw that lap back sooner under Safety Car conditions. Lawson suffered a pre-race fuel leak which necessitated a pit-lane start in Las Vegas but, despite Racing Bulls having worked in double-quick time to get him into the action, he began a lap behind the rest of the pack. Liam Lawson bemoans ‘so frustrating’ Las Vegas GP unlapping delay The chance for the New Zealander to rejoin the back of the field came after a collision between Sergio Perez and Rafael Camara brought out the Safety Car, and was likely extended by Lawson’s teammate, Arvid Lindblad, pitching his car into an unexpected spin in yellow flag conditions. Having received the instruction to overtake the Safety Car and catch up, however, he passed the whole field and, by the time racing got going again, Lawson still faced a significant deficit to the rest of the field. This ultimately left him unable to make any headway in the race, crossing the line in 15th place, but would later be promoted one place after a 10-second penalty for Isack Hadjar was applied. The 24-year-old thanked his team for having been able to fix his car, but did not hide his frustration at not being able to make his way back up the pack – with Race Control having opted to take four laps before allowing him to unlap himself. “That’s really the big question I think we need to answer, is what we can do in the future to figure it out earlier,” Lawson said of his fuel leak after the race. “We’ve actually had a similar thing happen in Monaco this year, and both times, the guys and girls have done a really, really good job to put the car together and maximise. “For us to go out on track today, have absolutely no issues, and have a really, really fast race car is massively impressive from everybody – I just feel for them that I couldn’t deliver a result because we lost a lap. “The thing is, I got it back, and we actually probably could have still had a really good race, but I don’t know why they they took four laps to release me. How the Las Vegas Grand Prix unfolded Las Vegas Grand Prix 2026 – F1 race results (Las Vegas Strip circuit) Telemetry reveals full Ferrari impact of Hamilton, Leclerc clash in Las Vegas “I get that when there’s marshals on track and there’s safety around it, I can understand that – but it’s still a double yellow. I can still slow down for the double yellow zone and follow a delta. “I’m not going to blow through that zone at high speeds, but it just means I can do the whole lap and catch back up. And unfortunately, they went to four laps and then they gave me half a lap to catch back up, and I restarted more than 25 seconds behind the field. “It’s so frustrating, I was watching the screens the whole race, and I could see how close it was bunched up. At the end of the race, we were very, very quick today. “It’s really frustrating to not have the chance to fight there, obviously, and then to lose more points to Alpine.” Read next: Charles Leclerc apologises after ’embarrassing’ Hamilton Las Vegas clash Racing Bulls Liam Lawson

records.excerpt: FIA confirms Isack Hadjar punishment after ‘deliberate’ Las Vegas GP incident Jamie Woodhouse 22 Nov 2026 10:24 AM Isack Hadjar received a 10-second penalty after the Las Vegas GP Isack Hadjar has received a 10-second time penalty for what the stewards called a “deliberate” and “tactical” act at the Las Vegas Grand Prix. The incident in question occurred under Safety Car conditions, as the stewards determined the Red Bull driver deliberately slowed, under instruction from the team, to create a double stack pit-stop opportunity. FIA stewards explain Isack Hadjar 10-second penalty The Safety Car was deployed on Lap 19 as Cadillac’s Sergio Perez tangled with Rafael Camara in the Haas. Perez tried to pass the Brazilian up the inside into Turn 14, but Camara turned in and a collision followed for which the Cadillac driver was penalised . A flurry of pit-lane activity commenced, and Hadjar had backed up the field so that teammate and race leader Max Verstappen could complete his stop before he arrived at the Red Bull pit box. The stewards took a dim view of the Frenchman’s actions and handed out a post-race 10-second penalty. Added to his race time, it drops him to 15th in the final classification. The verdict reads: “The stewards heard from the driver of Car 6 (Isack Hadjar) and his team representative as well as the team representative of Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 team and reviewed positioning/marshalling system data, video, timing, telemetry, team radio and in-car video evidence. “While driving on the straight between Turns 13 and 14 under Safety Car conditions, the driver of Car 6 received repeated instructions from his team stating “five seconds, five seconds, five seconds”. “Following these instructions, Car 6 significantly reduced its speed, at one point travelling approximately 100 km/h slower than Car 3, which was ahead of it. “The stewards determined that this significant reduction in speed was deliberate and intended to create a gap to the car ahead and was not made for safety reasons, thereby allowing the team to perform a double-stack pit stop without Car 6 losing time waiting behind its teammate in the pit lane. “Furthermore, this manoeuvre directly impacted the cars following Car 6, which were forced to reduce their speed accordingly and could not overtake Car 6 due to the restrictions applicable under Safety Car conditions. “The stewards considered that Car 6 was driving unnecessarily slowly for tactical reasons and that such conduct constituted a breach of the applicable regulations. “In reaching their decision, the stewards also took into account the precedent involving Car 4 (Norris) at the 2023 Canadian Grand Prix, where a penalty was imposed for similar conduct. “The stewards imposed a 10-seconds time penalty which is consistent with the 2026 F1 Penalty Guidelines.” Latest Las Vegas GP talking points on PlanetF1.com Max Verstappen slams George Russell with brutal ‘far below my level’ remark Ferrari blasts ‘unacceptable’ Hamilton, Leclerc clash in Las Vegas Hadjar suffered a broken front wing not long after the race restart, forcing him to box his sparking Red Bull for a new one. He came back out in 19th. He had worked his way back up to 14th by the finish, but drops one spot with the penalty applied. records.excerpt: Lewis Hamilton breaks silence on Ferrari number one driver debate Lewis Hamilton makes feelings clear on Ferrari No.1 driver debate Jamie Woodhouse 23 Nov 2026 11:25 AM Lewis Hamilton has "never asked" to be Ferrari number one driver Lewis Hamilton insists that he has “never asked” to be recognised as the Ferrari number one driver. He did, however, claim that with “support” earlier in the year, he could have beaten Kimi Antonelli at certain points when he was the Mercedes driver’s closest title challenger. The likes of Damon Hill and Ralf Schumacher have weighed in with strong opinions on Hamilton’s status within Ferrari. Lewis Hamilton ‘never asked’ for Ferrari No.1 status It was following a clash between the red cars in Mexico City, one which left Charles Leclerc with a penalty and that opened the door for a Max Verstappen victory, that Damon Hill, the 1996 world champion, suggested the solution was to make Hamilton the clear lead driver. “Here is where I stand on the Lewis v Charles debate: make Lewis #1 Ferrari driver,” he posted on social media. “Sort it out. Make it clear. Ends all debate. “Lewis will deliver for Ferrari. If they back him 100%.” Hill later doubled down on his stance, though six-time grand prix winner Ralf Schumacher pushed back, insisting that Hamilton would need to consistently and soundly beat Leclerc to earn that status, but has not done so. Former Renault driver Jolyon Palmer also rejected Hill’s theory, and foresaw a scenario where Hamilton and Leclerc would once again go wheel-to-wheel to “prove their superiority”. Fresh wheel-to-wheel exchanges arrived in Las Vegas, the end result Hamilton being sent spinning by his teammate. Following the race, Hamilton was presented with Hill’s comments. “I’ve never asked to be number one. I genuinely haven’t ever asked,” he clarified. That being said, Hamilton went on to highlight where he could have benefitted from “support” at a time earlier in the year where he was shaping up as Antonelli’s biggest title threat. Hamilton’s calls in the moment fell on deaf ears, and after being shown the gravel by Leclerc at the Italian Grand Prix, confirmed post-race that it was now “far too late” for team orders. “There was a point in the season where I was 40-odd points ahead, and at that point, the fight was with me and Kimi,” Hamilton continued after the Las Vegas GP. “I was the closest one to him. I was second for a long time in the year, and at that point, needed backing to make sure we beat Kimi. “There were certain instances in the season where, with the support, I think we could have beaten Kimi, like Zandvoort, for example. “But no, that’s not what I’ve asked for. Just we shouldn’t have been able to come together [in Las Vegas]. That should just never happen. “But I’ve said everything I can on it, and the question should be for Ferrari now.” Latest Ferrari news on PlanetF1.com Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari ‘deserve better’ after latest Charles Leclerc clash Telemetry reveals full Ferrari impact of Hamilton, Leclerc clash in Las Vegas Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur was left enraged over the Las Vegas GP collision, pointing the finger at Leclerc. records.excerpt: Telemetry reveals full Ferrari impact of Hamilton, Leclerc clash in Las Vegas Uros Radovanovic 22 Nov 2026 9:22 AM Another clash between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc cost Ferrari dearly in Las Vegas. Just a few laps before their collision in Las Vegas, Lewis Hamilton was 2.5 seconds behind the race leader and Charles Leclerc 2.9 seconds adrift, with Ferrari the fastest car on track. Telemetry data reveals how much pace the team had in hand, and how a Lap 38 clash left them with just seven points from a race they could have turned into a double podium – and possibly more. How Far Could Ferrari Have Gone in Las Vegas? As discussed after qualifying , Las Vegas combines the worst possible circuit characteristics for the SF-26. The cold track surface amplifies tyre warm-up struggles, preventing Ferrari from matching its usual cornering competitiveness, while the long straights ruthlessly expose its power unit deficit and lower ERS efficiency. During qualifying, that lack of straight-line speed along the Strip wasn’t an issue, as Ferrari adjusted its deployment strategy to remain competitive there and avoid becoming sitting ducks in the race. However, it paid a heavy price for that compromise in the middle sector. Long runs in FP3 revealed that, while Ferrari trailed the leaders on race pace, roughly 70 percent of that deficit originated specifically in Sector 2. Going into Sunday with low expectations, the race nonetheless unfolded very differently. The Grand Prix was both unusual and thrilling to watch: after 10 laps, the top 10 runners sat within five seconds of the race leader—a rare sight in modern Formula 1. Ferrari remained firmly in that lead pack, with both drivers showing solid pace during the opening stint. Starting from P11, one spot behind Leclerc, Hamilton overtook his teammate on the opening lap and climbed as high as P6 at one stage, before settling into P7 and P8 around Lap 15 to battle Norris and Piastri for position. The graph below illustrates average lap times across the opening stint: Antonelli and Piastri set the pace on track, yet everyone else—aside from Norris, who dropped several places—remained closely matched. George Russell, Hamilton and Max Verstappen were on nearly the same race pace for the first 17 laps of the race. Laptimes scatterplot – Race First stint comparison A Lap 19 Safety Car effectively ended any strategic variation: everyone switched from softs to mediums or vice versa, locking in their compounds to the chequered flag. At the Lap 26 restart, Leclerc held seventh, while Hamilton dropped back to P13 after serving a 10-second time penalty and pitting a lap later than the bulk of the field. On the medium compound, however, Ferrari’s pace looked even stronger than in the first stint. Hamilton drove brilliantly, climbing from P13 to P8 in just six laps, while Leclerc gained a spot to sit in P6, with Piastri sandwiched between the two scarlet machines. That triggered the intra-team fight that ultimately ended in contact between Hamilton and Leclerc. Piastri moved ahead of both red cars, while Hamilton pulled off a crisp move around the outside of Turn 3 to repass his teammate. Crucially, a few laps before the collision, Hamilton trailed race leader Verstappen by only 2.5 seconds, with Leclerc just 2.9 seconds adrift; both drivers remained firmly in the fight and, with overtaking happening throughout the field, anything was possible. Then came Lap 38: Hamilton attempted a pass down the inside of Piastri on entry to Turn 5 but failed to complete it, slightly compromising his corner exit—an opening Leclerc immediately tried to exploit. On entry to Turn 7, Charles dived up the inside, resulting in contact that left Hamilton spun around facing the wrong way. Hamilton was ahead at the apex and owned the corner, a verdict confirmed by the stewards, who handed the Monegasque driver a 10-second penalty as his teammate plummeted down the order. Data underscores just how rapid Hamilton was during those opening laps of the second stint: he averaged the fastest pace of any front-running driver, as shown in the graph below – more than four tenths of a second per lap faster than Verstappen on average. Naturally, that delta would have narrowed by the finish, but the takeaway is clear: Ferrari possessed the raw pace to take the fight to McLaren, and possibly Verstappen. Laptimes scatterplot – Race Second stint comparison (from lap 27 to lap 38) More on Ferrari at the Las Vegas Grand Prix Lewis Hamilton fumes at Las Vegas penalty as Charles Leclerc comparison emerges Ferrari summons Charles Leclerc after ‘unacceptable’ Lewis Hamilton Las Vegas clash Had contact been avoided and Ferrari managed to beat McLaren—a thoroughly realistic prospect—we might now be talking about a remarkable Scuderia comeback and a double podium. That outcome would have been aided further by Russell hitting the wall late on and Antonelli losing battery deployment over the final two laps. Instead, we are once again analysing how Ferrari shot itself in the foot and left Las Vegas with just seven points—its second-lowest points haul of the season after scoring only six in Brazil. Whether the team will introduce stricter internal rules of engagement remains to be seen, but one thing is certain: the lack of clear team orders has only hurt it this season. records.excerpt: Ferrari declares Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc line-up 'unmanageable' Ferrari boss signals doubt over ‘unmanageable’ Lewis Hamilton-Leclerc line-up Taylor Powling 23 Nov 2026 8:56 AM There were more Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc fireworks in Las Vegas Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur has claimed that the collaboration between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc has become “unmanageable” after their latest clash in Las Vegas. The two Ferrari drivers came to blows on Lap 38 of the race when Leclerc’s attempted move down the inside of his teammate into Turn 7 ended in wheel-to-wheel contact that pitched Hamilton into a spin, an incident that capped off what had already been a tumultuous weekend for the Maranello-based squad at the Las Vegas Strip Circuit. Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton under scrutiny after latest clash The collision comes only two weeks after Vasseur held behind-closed-doors talks with both men to clear the air over the first-lap squabble that cost the team a win in Mexico. Vasseur, in particular, pointed the finger at Leclerc, whom he spoke with privately prior to conducting his post-race media duties , citing that the Monegasque had gone against a team order not to try and overtake his teammate at that stage in proceedings. “First of all, I must say that what happened is unacceptable,” Vasseur expressed to Sky Italy. “I’ll repeat the same message I gave in Mexico, because we need to think of the people working at Maranello, the team, all the shareholders and the sponsors. “We had told Charles not to overtake, because at that stage it was important to catch up with the cars ahead rather than get caught up in a battle. “Charles made a mistake that has really cost the team dearly: his behaviour was unacceptable. “To be honest, I’m more than just angry, because the message was clear after Mexico and we’d all had a chat together in Brazil. Today we gave an instruction with the team’s best interests in mind, yet they were racing against each other: the result is what we saw. And it’s extremely frustrating for all of us.” Unlike in Mexico City – where he emphasised that Ferrari had failed as a collective – Vasseur insisted that no blame can be apportioned to the team for this latest run-in. When it was put to him that there seems to be a persistent communication problem between the drivers and the team, including him, Vasseur retorted: “No, I don’t think that’s the case. I think the message from the pit wall was very clear. “At the end of the day, I’m not the one driving the car, and neither are the track engineers. We gave an order that was crystal clear. “It’s not a question of communication. We’d been very open and very clear after Mexico, and we were the same today.” More on the Ferrari collision in Las Vegas Telemetry reveals full Ferrari impact of Hamilton, Leclerc clash in Las Vegas Ferrari outlines action after ‘unacceptable’ Hamilton, Leclerc clash in Las Vegas Having divulged that the coming together would trigger another internal discussion in the coming week, Vasseur hasn’t ruled out action being taken against either driver. “We’ll discuss this tomorrow, but we’ll certainly have to take some measures and make some decisions,” he answered. “We don’t need to act tonight. We must keep calm and then take the necessary steps. “Of course, it’s unacceptable that the work of two thousand people who put in so much effort should be ruined in this way. Perhaps it’s also time to start thinking about next season.” Amid Max Verstappen’s claim that having two well-matched drivers in the same team isn’t conducive to success, Vasseur had insisted in Brazil that he continues to back his decision to pair Hamilton with Leclerc, arguing that the intense competition between the two has been integral to Ferrari sitting second in the Constructors’ Championship. But for the first time, Vasseur appears to have signalled doubts about the suitability of the Hamilton and Leclerc line-up, as he admitted the various on-track disputes that the two have been embroiled in this year have dented their working relationship. Pressed on whether he expected things to come to this when he made the decision to replace Carlos Sainz with seven-time champion Hamilton from 2025, the Frenchman responded: “Honestly, no. If I’d known, our approach would have been different. “The pressure is certainly mounting. It’s much worse now than it was 18 months ago. Lately, the situation between them has become unmanageable. But honestly, ultimately, it’s a human misunderstanding between them, not with the team.” Read next: Max Verstappen delivers brutal verdict on George Russell after Las Vegas showdown Ferrari Charles Leclerc Fred Vasseur Lewis Hamilton Related Articles Taylor Powling 24 Nov 2026 Lewis Hamilton reignites Charles Leclerc criticism after Las Vegas clash Lewis Hamilton appeared to take issue with Charles Leclerc again after their collision in Las Vegas. records.excerpt: Jonathan Wheatley is expected to join Aston Martin in early January, but the team has yet to confirm an agreement, start date or role. Jonathan Wheatley is expected to join Aston Martin in early January in a move that will see the former Audi team principal take a similar position at the Silverstone-based tea Aston Martin set to appoint Jonathan Wheatley in early January Exclusive Updated : 11:39, 23 Nov 6 Comments Ben Hunt Ben Hunt is an award-winning motorsport journalist with over two decades of experience in Formula 1 and international media. As a former editor-in-chief and bestselling author, he delivers in-depth analysis and strategic insight from the highest level of the sport. Jonathan Wheatley is expected to join Aston Martin in early January in a move that will see the former Audi team principal take a similar position at the Silverstone-based team. Wheatley left Audi in March, with the team announcing that he had departed with immediate effect for personal reasons. His exit quickly prompted speculation about a move to Aston Martin, where his experience in Formula 1 made him an obvious target. However, the switch was not without questions over when Wheatley could take up a new role immediately, with a spell of gardening leave likely to be served to offer a clear break with Audi's F1 operations. But GPBlog understands that after a period of nearly 10 months, the former Red Bull Sporting Director will be free to join Aston early next year. Read also Fernando Alonso blasts Las Vegas Grand Prix as a 'demo' amid more problems for Aston Wheatley’s Aston Martin link remains unconfirmed ADVERTISEMENT Wheatley’s name has been linked with Aston Martin since his departure from Audi. GPBlog previously reported t hat he was among the figures connected with the team’s leadership considerations, while cautioning that speculation did not amount to a completed deal. The attraction is understandable. Wheatley spent years in senior roles at Red Bull before joining Audi, building experience across the sporting and operational sides of Formula 1. That background could be valuable to a team seeking to strengthen its management structure, particularly as Aston Martin continues to pursue its ambitions at the front of the grid. It is not yet clear whether Wheatley would become team principal, take another senior role, or join under a different structure, as Adrian Newey remains in place as the defacto team boss. The team’s leadership arrangements have been a subject of scrutiny since Newey took on a prominent position at Aston Martin. GPBlog has previously outlined the uncertainty around a possible succession and the questions surrounding Wheatley’s potential appointment. Read also International media rave about Verstappen: ‘Mario Kart on LSD’ ADVERTISEMENT January could bring clarity to Aston Martin’s plans If Wheatley does arrive in early January, the timing could give Aston Martin a chance to settle its management plans ahead of the new season. That would not necessarily mean an immediate change in responsibilities: the team would still need to confirm his role and explain how it fits with the existing leadership structure. However, it is clear that after another turbulent season, with Fernando Alonso critical of the team's results , Aston need some changes if they are to make progress in their aspirations to challenge for wins. records.title: ステランティス、FIA世界選手権ワークス撤退を発表。プジョーはWEC即時撤退、シトロエンとオペルはGEN4初年度限り
records.excerpt: Courtesy Of Stellantis ステランティス、FIA世界選手権ワークス撤退を発表。プジョーはWEC即時撤退、シトロエンとオペルはGEN4初年度限り 公開： 2026/11/24 02:23 プジョーやシトロエン、オペルを傘下に持つ自動車グループのステランティスは11月23日（月）、国際自動車連盟（FIA）が管轄する世界選手権でのワークス活動を終了すると発表した。 プジョーのFIA世界耐久選手権（WEC）プログラムは即時終了となり、シトロエンとオペルも2026／27年シーズン限りでフォーミュラEから撤退する。オペルにとっては、初戦を迎える前に参戦初年度限りでの撤退が決まった格好だ。 GEN4初年度限りでフォーミュラE撤退 シトロエン・レーシング、2026年11月 フォーミュラEプレシーズンテスト（ハラマ・サーキット） Courtesy Of Stellantis ステランティスは、フォーミュラEが新世代マシン「GEN4」に切り替わる今季に向けて、新たなパワートレインを開発している。オペルは自社で運営するチームを立ち上げ、ジャガーで10年を過ごしたミッチ・エバンスと、2023年のFIA-F2王者テオ・プルシェールを起用する。 シトロエンは、同じグループ傘下のマセラティ名義で参戦していたモナコ・スポーツ・グループのチームを引き継ぎ、ステランティスがフランス・サトリーの拠点で直接運営する体制に移行した。ドライバーは2度のシリーズ王者ジャン＝エリック・ベルニュと、同ブランドの参戦2戦目で初勝利を挙げたニック・キャシディだ。 両ブランドが参戦するGEN4初年度は、2027年7月24日（土）と25日（日）の東京E-Prixで幕を閉じる予定だ。 復帰から4年、プジョーWEC活動は即時終了 （プジョー 93号車9X8）と（プジョー 94号車9X8）、2026年 FIA世界耐久選手権 モンツァ6時間レース 決勝（モンツァ・サーキット） Courtesy Of Stellantis プジョーはコスト面を理由に、2012年シーズン開幕前にル・マン24時間レースを含むWECから撤退し、10年後の2022年にハイパーカー「9X8」でWECに復帰した。今年7月には、チーム代表のエマニュエル・エノーが、2027年に向けて9X8を改良し、安定して上位を争うことを目指すと説明していた。 プジョーは来季のドライバーとして、元フェラーリ開発ドライバーのロバート・シュワルツマンと、リザーブから昇格するアレックス・クインの起用を発表済みだった。クインはその後、予定を前倒しして2026年の残り2戦に出場している。 巨額赤字と経営再建、ワークス撤退の背景に何が パブロ・サラザン（ランチア・コルセHF イプシロン・ラリー2HFインテグラーレ）とヤニック・ロシュ（ランチア・コルセHF）、2026年11月 ラリー・シックス・シティーズ・ノース・オブ・ポルトガル（ポルトガル北部） Courtesy Of Stellantis ステランティスは、商品計画の見直しなどに伴う一時費用が響き、2025年通期に223億ユーロ（約3兆8800億円／1ユーロ＝174.01円）の純損失を計上した。2026年1～9月は2億1700万ユーロ（約378億円）の純利益に転じたものの、7～9月期単独では4億5300万ユーロ（約788億円）の純損失を計上している。 経営計画「FaSTLAne 2030」では、2028年までに2025年比で年間60億ユーロ（約1兆400億円）のコスト削減を目指すとしており、今回のワークス活動終了については、「新製品の開発、品質向上、より幅広い市場への展開に同社の取り組みと経営資源を集中させる」同計画に沿った判断と位置付けている。 FIA世界選手権でのワークス活動終了に伴い発生する余剰リソースについては、カスタマーレーシングおよび高性能車両の開発に再集中するとしており、その一環として、複数のブランドを通じたカスタマー向けのラリー競技車両の販売事業を強化する。 なお、ランチアはPHスポーツと組み、2026年のWRC2でチームタイトルを獲得しているが、今回の発表では、今後の活動計画に関する説明はなかった。ダッジについても、2027年にNASCARカップ・シリーズへ復帰することが決まっており、現時点で活動計画に関する変更は発表されていない。 TAG： おすすめ FIAフォーミュラE世界選手権 FIA世界耐久選手権（WEC） その他レース等 records.title: ラファエル・カマラ、F1カタールGPとアブダビGPに参戦決定。FIA F2欠場が正式発表に
records.excerpt: プロ野球 MLB ゴルフ 日本代表 Jリーグ プロ野球（2軍） 大相撲 テニス 侍ジャパン フィギュア ラファエル・カマラ、F1カタールGPとアブダビGPに参戦決定。FIA F2欠場が正式発表に 11/23(月) 3:45 share シェア X Facebook LINE 閉じる ただ、ハースF1はカタールとアブダビでのカマラ起用を発表した。小松礼雄チーム代表は「ラファ（カマラの愛称）がドライバーを務めるかたちで今シーズンを締めくくれることを嬉しく思います」と、コメント。 「ブラジルとアメリカでの最初の2戦を経て、そこからさらに積み上げていけるはずです。ラファがコース上でのあらゆるセッションを学びの機会と捉え、チームにしっかりと溶け込んでくれたことを大変嬉しく思っています」 「こうしてシーズンを最後までともに戦えることは、比較的短いオフシーズンを控え、2027年に向けた準備が本格化するなかで、我々全員にとってプラスとなるでしょう」 カマラが2戦4レースを残してFIA F2を離れることになり、FIA F2のドライバーズタイトル争いは、現在ランキング2位のニコラ・ツォロフ（カンポス・レーシング／レッドブル育成）、ツォロフから11点差でランキング3位のアレクサンダー・ダン（ロダン・モータースポーツ／アルピーヌ育成）が争うことになる見込みだ。 また、カマラが離れるインビクタ・レーシングのシートに誰が座るのかは、本稿掲載時点では明らかにされていない。なお、インビクタ・レーシングは2027年にフレディ・スレイター（アウディ育成／今季FIA F3ランキング2位）とノア・ストロムステッド（今季FIA F3ランキング10位）をFIA F2で起用することを明らかにしている。 [オートスポーツweb 2026年11月23日] 記事に関するキーワード [科学・技術](https://www.vietnam.vn/ja/category/khoa-hoc-cong-nghe) # ベトナムは、FIA規格に準拠した初の国際ラリーレースを開催する。 （CLO）2026年チュオンソンラリーは、12月2日から6日にかけてクアンチ省で正式に開幕し、ベトナムのモータースポーツ界にとって歴史的な節目となる。 [![Image 3: Công Luận](https://vphoto.vietnam.vn/thumb/48x48/vietnam/resource/IMAGE/2025/1/21/c24dae1bd6ae41d99f0a721f4551aa76)Công Luận•22/11/2026](https://www.vietnam.vn/ja/authors/congluan-vn) * * * Vietnam.vn をフォローしてください G o o g l e Vietnam.vn を追加 G o o g l e 0 チュオンソンラリー（正式名称はペトロリメックスXCRスプリントカップベトナム2026）は、国際基準のスプリントラリーレースであり、 [日本](https://www.vietnam.vn/ja/tag/nhat-ban "日本")が設立・認可したXCRシリーズの一部で、国際自動車連盟（FIA）の安全基準に準拠しています。 従来の周回コースで行われるレースとは異なり、チュオンソンラリーでは、タイムトライアル形式のステージ（スペシャルステージ：SS）を通して、選手たちは難易度の高いオフロード地形を走破することが求められます。そこでは、スピード、ナビゲーションスキル、そしてメインドライバーとコ・ドライバー間の連携が非常に重要となります。 当該レーストラックは、国際自動車連盟（FIA）および日本自動車連盟（JAF）の厳格な安全基準および技術基準に従って調査され、承認された。 ![Image 4: anh-man-hinh-2026-11-22-luc-081229.png](https://vstatic.vietnam.vn/vietnam/resource/IMAGE/2026/11/22/1795317619125_anh-man-hinh-2026-11-22-luc-081229-png.avif) 2026年チュオンソンラリーには、数々の著名な国際レーサーが出場予定 - 写真：組織委員会 Khám phá thêm Tìm hiểu lịch sử Đọc Mẹo Du Lịch Khám phá ĐNA 主催者からの初期情報によると、レースは主に2つの競技カテゴリーに分けられるとのことです。 _ラリースプリントカテゴリー_ はタイムトライアル形式のレースです。各チームはメインドライバー1名とコ・ドライバー1名で構成され、2名が協力してステアリング操作を行います。4x4 SUV/ピックアップトラック向けに設計されたこのカテゴリーは、XC1（オープン）とXC2（プロダクション）の2つのサブクラスに分かれています。チームは、2026年12月5日～6日の2日間にわたって連続して行われる、総距離約60kmの9つのスペシャルステージ（SS）を3つのセクションに分けて走破します。 _モーターサイクル部門は_ ラリー・スプリント形式で行われ、ビッグ・アドベンチャー（排気量900cc以上のバイク）とミッド・アドベンチャー（排気量450cc～800ccのバイク）の2つのクラスに分かれ、各クラスの参加台数は最大25台に制限されている。 records.excerpt: Title: FIA Confirms Unanimous 2030 Power Unit Framework Agreement and Full-Time Stewards From 2027 URL Source: http://ministryofsport.com/fia-confirms-unanimous-2030-power-unit-framework-agreement-and-full-time-stewards-from-2027/ Final URL: https://ministryofsport.com/fia-confirms-unanimous-2030-power-unit-framework-agreement-and-full-time-stewards-from-2027/ Published Time: 2026-11-23T23:21:56+00:00 Markdown Content: [Home](https://ministryofsport.com/)>FIA Confirms Unanimous 2030 Power Unit Framework Agreement and Full-Time Stewards From 2027 2 min read Written by MOS Editorial Team Published on 24 November 2026 ![Image 1: image](https://ministryofsport.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/698efe7a-252b-4014-9cc2-012cbd2a67fc-2302584872.webp) ## FIA Announces Two Major Governance Decisions in November 2026 The FIA has confirmed unanimous agreement among key stakeholders on the 2030 power unit technical framework for Formula 1, while separately announcing that full-time stewards will be introduced from the **2027 season** onwards. Both decisions were announced in **November 2026**. The 2030 power unit framework secures a long-range technical direction for F1, with the FIA and participating teams having committed to its terms without reported opposition. The recruitment process for full-time stewards is now underway. ## 2030 Power Unit Framework The FIA confirmed that all key parties — including the FIA itself and F1 teams — reached unanimous agreement on the 2030 power unit technical framework. No dissenting positions from stakeholders were reported at the time of the announcement. The framework sets the technical specifications that will govern Formula 1 power units from 2030, providing manufacturers and teams with a defined long-term planning horizon. ## Full-Time Stewards From the 2027 Season Alongside the power unit announcement, the FIA confirmed it is **beginning recruitment of full-time stewards** ahead of the 2027 Formula 1 season. The stated purpose of the initiative is to bring greater levels of consistency to race management and officiating decisions across the championship. Under the current structure, stewards have operated on a rotating, part-time basis at individual race events. The move to full-time appointments represents a structural change to how the FIA administers on-track governance in F1. ## Scope of the Changes Taken together, the two announcements reflect a direction from the FIA toward greater standardization and long-term planning in Formula 1 governance. The 2030 power unit agreement addresses the sport’s technical regulations over a multi-year horizon, while the full-time steward programme targets procedural consistency within individual race weekends beginning in 2027. Recruitment for the full-time steward roles was confirmed as active as of November 2026. ### Latest News ![Image 2: logo](https://ministryofsport.com/wp-content/themes/ministryofsport/images/logo-icon.png) [![Image 3: Image](https://ministryofsport.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/5.png)](https://ministryofsport.com/membership-plans/) ## It's free to join the team! records.label: racingnews365.com
records.title: F1 set for another major change over 2030 V8 engine regulations
records.excerpt: Article To news overview © XPB Images F1 power unit manufacturers could be limited to supplying only one customer team from 2030, RacingNews365 understands. Last week, the FIA revealed that all power unit manufacturers had agreed to the new technical framework for the next era of regulations, set to commence in 2030. This will see F1 shift to a 2.1-litre turbocharged V8 engine, with less electrical influence and the use of sustainable fuels. A return to V8 engines was proposed by the FIA earlier this year, with president Mohammed Ben Sulayem stating after the agreement was reached that it would offer F1 a chance to “reconnect with the DNA” of the sport. But what was not outlined in the initial release is another element that could have significant sporting and political implications going forward. RacingNews365 understands that the power unit manufacturers will only be able to field engines at two entries, including their works teams. However, at this early stage of the situation, discussions are still ongoing on the details of the sport's new era from 2030, with nothing set in stone. Should it be decided that a power unit manufacturer can only supply one customer, the FIA could still step in and mandate an additional customer, raising the supply to three teams in total. Mercedes set for big impact If this rule becomes reality, it would bring significant changes across the grid, perhaps most notably at Mercedes. Out of the 11 teams currently on the grid, four currently run under Mercedes power: the Mercedes works team, McLaren, Williams and Alpine. While the works team is obviously in no danger of losing the supply, it raises doubt for the other three outfits. During the Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend, McLaren CEO Zak Brown stated that he saw his squad running Mercedes engines for a “long time” in the future. The pair have a historic partnership that dates back to the mid-1990s, and after brief stints with Honda and Renault in the 2010s, it returned to Mercedes power in 2021 before resurging towards title success. Williams has been buying Mercedes power units since the start of the turbo-hybrid era in 2014, while Alpine is its newest customer, having taken on the engines this year after selling its own in-house engine operation. Two of these teams will be impacted should the regulation be ratified, forcing them to find a new supplier. It is hoped that Audi and Honda, who currently supply just one team each, will take on a customer team. General Motors also remains an option as the American squad prepares to enter its own power unit in 2030. records.title: Formula 1 Plans Major 2030 Engine Change.
records.excerpt: Formula 1 is planning new V8 engine rules for 2030, with a proposed limit of two teams per manufacturer. Mercedes could lose two customer teams. Formula 1 Plans Major 2030 Engine Change. Formula 1 is planning new V8 engine rules for 2030, with a proposed limit of two teams per manufacturer. Mercedes could lose two customer teams. by Sportscape Editor | Nov 23, 2026 | 2 min Formula 1 to get new 2030 V8 engine regulations under discussion. · Credits: Via Wikipedia Global Formula 1 is preparing for a major change in its engine regulations from the 2030 season. The FIA six power unit manufacturers have reportedly agreed on a plan to introduce V8 engines. This will limit the manufacturers to supply only two teams including its own company. This could create a major challenge for the Mercedes F1 team. Mercedes is currently supplying to McLaren, Williams and Alpine. All these three teams might have to fight for their place to get the supplies from Mercedes in future. The main aim behind this change is to reduce cost, making engines simple, and creating a new direction for sports technical development. F1 Plans to Bring Back V8 Engines in 2030 The proposed F1 engine regulations will introduce 2.1-litre V8 engines with turbochargers. The new power units will also use sustainable fuels and have a maximum electric power output of 200 kilowatts. The changes are expected to make engines cheaper and less complicated. The proposal has received support from all six manufacturers, but final approval from the FIA World Motor Sport Council is still required. Mercedes Could Lose Two Customer Teams The biggest challenge could be for Mercedes F1. The manufacturer currently supplies engines to McLaren, Williams and Alpine, apart from its own factory team. Under the proposed rules, Mercedes can supply only one additional customer team. McLaren CEO Zak Brown has already made his position clear. Speaking in Las Vegas, he said: “We’re very happy with HPP. I think we’ve proven that we can win championships with them, so we don’t have any intention to have anything in the back of our car other than a Mercedes.” Williams is also interested in continuing its partnership with Mercedes. However, the final decision will depend on Mercedes’ plans. Ferrari and Red Bull Also Face Changes Now Ferrari supplies engines for the Haas team as well as its own team, and it is the same for Cadillac. But from 2030, Cadillac will be making its own powertrain. Under the proposed cap, Red Bull Powertrains will remain in place, providing both Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls with engines. The FIA has also introduced a ‘jumping in’ condition rule in case of a lack of engine partner for a team. So there may be plenty of changes for engine partners on the grid with the new F1 rules 2030. formula 1 2030 rules f1 engine regulations mercedes f1 v8 engines mclaren f1 fia f1 power units Written by Sportscape Editor

records.excerpt: The shrill roar of the V8 engines is set to return to the grid, with the FIA and F1 teams establishing the framework for a 2030 power-unit switch. The FIA began the Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend by announcing that all manufacturers have agreed to the framework to bring turbocharged V8 engines back to F1 and move away from the current V6 turbo.This move has long been expected, with hopes that it will make engine building easier and cheaper while bringing back the sound that motorsport fans deeply miss.The sound of the V8 engines was a rally cry for fans and has been sorely missed by audiences worldwide.The F1 engine manufacturers agreed to a rough-out overarching plan to move to a 2.1-liter turbocharged V8 from 2030 onwards, with a lower charge of electrical power reducing the hybrid output from 350kW to 200kW, a decrease of nearly 56 percent.The FIA announced that ‘The plan is to marry the V8 power unit to a chassis which will also be lighter, more agile and placing greater emphasis on driver skill and close racing.”With everyone in agreement, PU manufacturers will start to jockey between improving the new car entering a sophomore season of new regulations and game planning for the major change coming just three seasons down the line.It’s been 13 years since manufacturers last built a V8 engine for F1.“This agreement marks a significant milestone in shaping the future of Formula 1,” FIA President Mohammed Ben Sulayem said. “From the outset, I have been clear in my ambition to deliver a sport that is more competitive and more exciting for our fans, while remaining at the forefront of innovation and sustainability.“The return of V8 engines represents an opportunity to reconnect with the DNA of this Championship, bringing back the sound, emotion and pure racing that is loved worldwide. Our vision is clear, lighter, simpler and more affordable cars that put driver skill at the heart of the competition.”

records.excerpt: FIA, AAMC Extend GT World Cup Agreement to 2028 – Sportscar365 Connect with us FIA GT World Cup FIA, AAMC Extend GT World Cup Agreement to 2028 FIA GT World Cup to remain in Macau through for at least next two editions… by Sportscar365 Staff November 21, 2026 Photo: PMAP The FIA and its member club, the Automobile General Association Macau-China (AAMC) have extended their agreement for the promotion of the FIA GT World Cup through at least 2028. Announced on Sunday in Macau, ahead of this afternoon’s ninth edition of the FIA GT World Cup, the deal confirms that AAMC will continue as the promoter of the race for at least the next two editions and remain a key part of the Macau Grand Prix. Under the renewed agreement, the FIA will retain responsibility for the safety, sporting and technical regulatory framework of the competition, while the FIA and AAMC will continue working together to further develop the event’s international visibility, broadcast coverage, digital presence and promotion. “The extension of this agreement is yet another important milestone in a year where we have made vital deals to secure the future of global motor sport across many different categories,” said FIA President Mohammed Ben Sulayem. “The partnership between the FIA and the Automobile General Association Macao-China brings important stability for the continued development of the world’s most prestigious sprint race for GT3 cars. “I would like to thank our Member Club, the AAMC, for their continued collaboration and shared commitment to strengthening the international profile of this incredible competition, which is a showcase for top-level GT racing in Asia, each year attracting a range of manufacturers and a line-up of some of the best GT racers in the world.” AAMC chairman Chong Coc Veng added: “Macau welcomes the continued hosting of the GT World Cup at the Guia Circuit. This year, the event features numerous manufacturers and the world’s top GT drivers, making it a premier GT spectacle that commands global attention. “The AAMC will continue to collaborate with the FIA​ to promote the FIA GT World Cup and deliver thrilling racing action to motor sport fans.” The FIA GT World Cup forms part of a lineup of FIA competitions held as part of the Macau Grand Prix, alongside the FIA FR World Cup, FIA F4 World Cup and the traditional season finale of the Kumho FIA TCR World Tour. “Macau is a natural home for the FIA GT World Cup,” said FIA GT Commission President Lutz Leif Linden. “The Guia Circuit provides a unique challenge for the world’s best GT racers, while the importance of the Asian market to prestigious automotive brands makes it an equally important event for manufacturers. “There is a strong local connection to GT3 customer racing, with several teams from the region represented on the grid. “This year, we’re seeing a record eight manufacturers on the grid, so I am pleased that the profile of the FIA GT World Cup keeps growing and that it will continue here until at least 2028.” Related Topics featured fia gt world cup Sportscar365 Staff The latest news, photos and video features from the trusted Sportscar365 web staff. records.title: FIA explains Lewis Hamilton Las Vegas GP penalty after 'b******t' called
records.excerpt: FIA explains Lewis Hamilton penalty after Las Vegas GP fury Jamie Woodhouse 23 Nov 2026 7:11 AM Lewis Hamilton was furious over his 10-second penalty in Las Vegas Lewis Hamilton was left seething over his 10-second penalty at the Las Vegas Grand Prix. The FIA stewards have argued that he had lost the corner. The Ferrari driver received those 10 seconds for leaving the track and gaining an advantage in defence against the McLaren of Lando Norris. While the verdict left Hamilton furious, the corner was Norris’ in the view of the stewards. FIA stewards explain Lewis Hamilton penalty Hamilton had pounced to pass Norris into Turn 5, but the McLaren would fight back. Joined by Hamilton’s Ferrari teammate Charles Leclerc, the trio went three abreast into Turn 7, Norris now on the inside line. Hamilton secured the position, but did so with all four wheels off the track. That was noted by the FIA stewards and resulted in a 10-second penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage. The fact that Norris lost out to Leclerc, Oscar Piastri and Franco Colapinto after Hamilton came through, complicated the situation. Informed of his sanction, the seven-time world champion was far from pleased. “That’s b******t! If I’d turned in, we’d have crashed,” he said over the radio, before adding: “Isn’t that interesting? One race where someone is given mitigating circumstances, they give them five seconds and then they give me 10 seconds for avoiding an incident.” While unconfirmed, Hamilton was potentially referring to teammate Leclerc’s five-second punishment in Mexico City for the same transgression, after fireworks between the Ferraris at Turn 4. Leclerc later quipped, after picking up a penalty for his Brazilian GP clash with Liam Lawson, that this was “probably the five seconds that I didn’t get in Mexico.” Amid Hamilton’s frustration, the stewards have shed further light on their decision to dish out the standard 10 seconds for leaving the track and gaining an advantage. “The stewards reviewed video, timing and in-car video evidence,” the explanation begins. “Car 1 (NOR) attempted to overtake Car 44 (HAM) on the left-hand side approaching Turn 7. records.title: Stellantis exit leaves Formula E facing a grid crisis
records.excerpt: Stellantis is winding down its European motorsport programmes, with Opel and Citroen leaving Formula E after the 2027 season and the grid shrinking to 20 cars. News Stellantis exit leaves Formula E facing a grid crisis Stellantis is winding down its European motorsport programmes, with Opel and Citroen leaving Formula E after the 2027 season and the grid shrinking to 20 cars. by Simone Scanu · Nov 23, 2026, 1:42 PM UTC · Updated Nov 23, 2026, 2:24 PM UTC © Opel Stellantis is pulling back from its European motorsport programmes, and Formula E is the series facing the sharpest consequences. Opel and Citroen will both depart at the end of the 2027 season , shortly after the Gen4 era begins, and the grid will drop from 24 cars to 20. Opel's entry is short-lived while Citroen's future hangs in the balance Opel's situation is the most dramatic. It had only just become Formula E's 11th team, signing Mitch Evans and Theo Pourchaire, and had completed pre-season running at Jarama with its Gen4 car the week before. That entry will now run its course through 2027 before being wound down. © FIA Formula E via Getty Images Citroen is in a slightly better position. Its programme is run through the independent Monaco Sports Group rather than as a direct factory operation, which leaves room for MSG Racing to find a new powertrain partner or commercial backer once Stellantis support ends. Citroen joined for Season 12, taking over Maserati's MSG effort, and has already tasted a win, a pole and a podium. Losing its backing piles pressure on the series to attract a Chinese brand, and the team's recent driver line-up news shows how much the operation was building toward the new era. The money behind the withdrawal According to Reuters, the cuts form part of chief executive Antonio Filosa's Value Creation Program, which targets six billion euros in group-wide savings by 2028. The context is hard numbers: Stellantis posted a 311 million euro operating loss in Europe in the third quarter of 2026. Executives pointed to pricing pressure on the continent and intensifying competition from Chinese manufacturers as the driving forces. © FIA Formula E Stellantis frames the exit as a focus on customers and cost Stellantis says the decision fits its FastLane 2030 strategy, which concentrates resources on customer racing, production vehicles and cost reduction. The closure of Peugeot's 9X8 Hypercar project in the WEC takes effect immediately, while customer programmes such as Lancia's WRC2 operation and Opel's electric rally cars will continue. The company plans to retain and redeploy staff from its Formula E and WEC programmes, although it has not said how many people will be affected. Finishing the current season, rather than withdrawing straight away, is understood to protect independent operators and give them time to secure new commercial partners and powertrain suppliers. The shutdown does not extend to North America, where Dodge's planned NASCAR Cup Series entry is reportedly unaffected. The unanswered question is whether MSG Racing can secure an alternative powertrain in time to keep Jean-Eric Vergne and Nick Cassidy on the grid beyond 2027. Until that is settled, the future of one of the series' most established operations remains uncertain.

records.title: Cadillac and Audi join Hot Wheels' expanding F1 collection
records.excerpt: Hot Wheels will complete its 2026 F1 grid in 1:64 scale for the first time, with Cadillac and Audi joining the collection Extra Cadillac and Audi join Hot Wheels' expanding F1 collection Fleur Mealing 23 Nov 2026 — 2 min read Hot Wheels will bring all 11 Formula 1 teams to its 1:64-scale collection for the first time in 2027, with Cadillac and Audi joining the range. Mattel, the owner of the Hot Wheels brand, has announced new premium die-cast models of the two newest additions to the F1 grid. The announcement marks the first time Cadillac and Audi F1 teams have been included in the Hot Wheels F1 collection, with both brands set to feature cars carrying their respective 2026 liveries. Cadillac's first model will feature Sergio Perez's #11 car, arriving in February 2027, with Valtteri Bottas's #77 machine following later in the year. Audi's initial release will feature Gabriel Bortoleto's #5 car, also scheduled for February 2027, followed later in the year by Nico Hulkenberg's #27. The models feature metal bodies and chassis, 'Real Riders' tyres, display plinths and specialist collector packaging. Each will be priced at £11.99 in the UK and available through mass retailers and Mattel Creations. The remaining nine teams will also receive updated 2026-liveried models throughout 2027, completing a 22-car collection featuring both drivers from every team. Alongside the premium die-cast releases, Hot Wheels is expanding its wider F1 offering with new track sets and a Tooned collection. The Hot Wheels Racing F1 Elimination Race track set is scheduled to launch in spring 2027, bringing head-to-head racing to the range. The wider track set collection will be priced between £29.99 and £149.99. A new Silver Series Tooned F1 collection will also arrive throughout 2027, featuring all 11 teams in an exaggerated Hot Wheels design. The 1:64-scale models will include authentic team logos, sponsorship details, front and rear wing decoration, and driver-specific helmet colours. Each will retail for £4.49. The expansion builds on the ongoing commercial partnership between F1 and Mattel, which has increasingly sought to connect the championship with younger audiences and collectors through toys, merchandise and interactive fan experiences at grands prix. Alex Ries, Mattel's vice president and global head of Hot Wheels, said: "Our relationship with F1 continues to grow, creating new opportunities for Hot Wheels to bring the excitement of the sport to fans and collectors around the world." Ries added: "Hot Wheels wants as many F1 fans as possible to be able to celebrate the teams and drivers they love, and completing the 2026 grid with the addition of Cadillac and Audi brings us closer to that goal." The night kicked off with Cassidy Towriss , Chief Brand Advisor of the Cadillac Formula 1 Team, and Savannah James , founder of Reframe , welcoming guests with the team car at the entrance and with the Sphere illuminated by the team’s logo. Guests such as Alix Earle , Olivia Jade , Jake Shane , Bryce Alakai , and Jordan Chiles filed into the venue, designed as a casino-inspired Driver’s Lounge, featuring card games, intimate cigar rooms, and whiskey tastings. Displays of race suits and driver helmets spanning this Formula 1 season paid homage to Cadillac's debut in Formula 1 racing, championing the evolution of the team’s identity throughout its inaugural year. With beats from DJ Millie and Tay James electrifying the dancefloor, alongside beauty stations from the cosmetic brand Reframe, the night sought to both celebrate the Grand Prix’s beginning and to honor the contributors and personalities that have made Cadillac's first Formula 1 season so memorable—a season that jumped off the starting line so ambitiously, that it couldn’t help but throw a grand Las Vegas party worth attending. records.excerpt: ナイキ、キャデラックF1と提携交渉か ウォルフ代表はメルセデスを去ったスポンサーに皮肉 11/24(火) 0:04 配信 2026年F1サンパウロGP、キャデラック(C)Cadillac F1（TopNews） ■ロードン前代表の在任中に交渉が加速か F1との提携を正式発表したナイキが、キャデラックとも契約を結ぶ可能性がある。一方、メルセデスF1のトト・ウォルフ代表は、ルイス・ハミルトンの移籍を機にチームを離れたスポンサーに皮肉を向けた。 ●【F1ライブ結果速報】F1ラスベガスGPも全セッションライブでお届け ドイツ紙『Bild（ビルト）』によると、ナイキとキャデラックは以前から提携に向けて協議を続けている。交渉が加速したのは、グレアム・ロードンがチーム代表を務めていた時期だという。 同紙によると、アメリカのスポーツ用品大手ナイキはマイアミGPでキャデラックの首脳陣に特製シューズも提供し、双方は今も契約に関心を示しているという。キャデラックは現在、トミー・ヒルフィガーのウェアを使用している。 ■ハミルトン移籍でメルセデスへの関心後退 『Bild（ビルト）』によると、ナイキはかつて、ハミルトンの世界的な知名度を主な理由としてメルセデスとの提携も検討した。だが、7度のF1王者ハミルトンが2025年にフェラーリへ移籍すると、関心は薄れたとされる。 メルセデスはプーマとの長年の提携を終え、2025年からアディダスと契約している。 ■ウォルフ代表、ハミルトン移籍で離れたスポンサーを振り返る ウォルフ代表はラスベガスでドイツのテレビ局『RTL』と同国の放送局『Sky Sport』の共同インタビューに応じ、ハミルトンの後任にアンドレア・キミ・アントネッリを起用した当時を振り返った。ハミルトンが去ったことを理由に、一部のスポンサーもチームを離れたという。 「スポンサーから『キミ・アントネッリとは誰なのか』と聞かれ、ルイス・ハミルトンがいなくなったから私たちと一緒に歩んでいくつもりはないと言われたことを、はっきり覚えています。彼らの判断が間違っていたのは明らかですから、その点ではいくらか満足しています。」 アントネッリが2026年のF1王者となった今、ウォルフ代表はこう付け加えた。 「彼らは今、ほかのチームと組んでいます。そこでの成績に満足すればいいでしょう。」 ■2027年からF1公式パートナー ナイキは2027年からF1の公式パートナーとなり、世界各地のF1イベントでスタッフが着用する公式ユニフォームを供給する。提携にはファン向けの商品展開も含まれる。また、ナイキは女性ドライバーの育成を目的とするF1アカデミーの公式パートナーにも就任する。 【関連リンク】 ●【画像】キャデラックF1、車体の内部が透けて見える特別リバリーを公開／ラスベガスGP ●ボッタス、2027年もキャデラックF1残留が決定 ペレスとのコンビ継続へ ●【F1｜決勝ダイジェスト】フェルスタッペン連覇 首位争いは「電気の使い方」が鍵に チームメイト対決も相次ぐ／ラスベガスGP ●メルセデスF1、残り3戦をマシンの検証に活用へ ウォルフ代表「9月の改良を入れたマシンをまだ理解できていません」 ●【F1】2030年の2.1リッターV8ターボ案で全会一致 FIAが発表、12月に最終案提出

records.excerpt: 【F1ラスベガスGP｜決勝結果】目が離せぬ大激戦！フェルスタッペンが優勝！フェラーリ同士が接触、最終周に波乱 11/22(日) 15:23 配信 2026年F1ラスベガスGP、マックス・フェルスタッペン（レッドブル・フォード）(C)Red Bull Content Pool（TopNews） 11月21日(土)、2026年F1第21戦ラスベガスGP（ラスベガス・ストリップ・サーキット）の3日目、決勝レース(50周)が開催された。 ●【F1ライブ結果速報】F1ラスベガスGPも全セッションライブでお届け 1位はマックス・フェルスタッペン（レッドブル／フォード）、2位はランド・ノリス（マクラーレン／メルセデス）、3位はオスカー・ピアストリ（マクラーレン／メルセデス）だった。 ■アストンマーティン・ホンダ ホンダのパワーユニットを搭載するアストンマーティン・アラムコF1チームは、フェルナンド・アロンソが19位、ランス・ストロールは17位だった。 ■トピックス ・気温12℃、路面温度14℃、湿度32％のドライコンディション。 ・アルボンはグリッドへ向かう途中にブレーキが過熱し、損傷を修復できず出走しなかった。ローソンは燃料漏れを修復した後、ピットレーンから遅れて出走した。 ・フェルスタッペンが首位を守るも、ラッセルがストレートで抜き、最終コーナーでフェルスタッペンが抜き返す激しい攻防。 ・ハジャーもノリスを抜き、ラッセルと2番手を争う。さらにフェルスタッペンにも迫り、チームからタイムを失わないよう指示。 ・ガスリーも好調で、リンドブラッドやハジャーをオーバーテイク。序盤から上位勢の順位が激しく入れ替わる。 ・ハミルトンにはコース外走行でアドバンテージを得たとして10秒ペナルティ。 ・19周目、ペレスとカマラが接触し、ペレスがクラッシュ。セーフティカー（SC）が導入され、各車が一斉にタイヤ交換へ。 ・ペレスはカマラとの接触で10秒ペナルティを科されたが、リタイアで消化できず、次に出走するレースで5グリッド降格となった。 ・レッドブルとメルセデスはダブルピットストップ。ハミルトンも10秒ペナルティを消化。リンドブラッドはスピンしてリタイア。 ・26周目にレース再開。ハジャー、フロントウィングが突然破損して火花が散った。 ・フェルスタッペン、ラッセル、ノリスが電気エネルギーの使い方を巡って激しい首位争いを展開。 ・フェラーリ勢はハミルトンとルクレールが接触。ルクレールには10秒ペナルティ。 ・上位勢で唯一ソフトタイヤを履くアントネッリもフェルスタッペンと首位を争う。 ・最終周、アントネッリが突然減速。抜いたラッセルは曲がりきれずウォールに接触するも走行を続ける。 ・アロンソは終盤に白煙を上げてコースアウトし、ピットレーンで停止。 ・フェルスタッペンは「こんなレース見たことないよ！来年はスポッターを用意するよ」と驚きを語った。 ■【暫定結果】決勝レース：F1ラスベガスGP 1
