records.title: 首位交代35回。「F1史上最もカオス」な一戦をフェルスタッペンが0.639秒差で制す / F1ラスベガスGP 2026《決勝》結果と詳報
records.excerpt: Courtesy Of Red Bull Content Pool 首位交代35回。「F1史上最もカオス」な一戦をフェルスタッペンが0.639秒差で制す / F1ラスベガスGP 2026《決勝》結果と詳報 公開： 2026/11/22 15:39 更新： 2026/11/24 02:33 2026年FIA-F1世界選手権第21戦ラスベガスGPの決勝が現地時間11月21日（土）に行われ、マックス・フェルスタッペン（レッドブル）がF1史上類を見ないレースをポール・トゥ・ウインで飾り、9戦連続となる表彰台に上がった。 0.639秒差の2位にランド・ノリス、1.529秒差の3位にオスカー・ピアストリが続き、マクラーレンが今シーズン初のダブル表彰台を獲得した。17番グリッドから追い上げたピアストリにとっても今季初の表彰台となった。 オーバーテイク数は352回、首位が入れ替わったのは実に35回。電気エネルギーを使う場所やオーバーテイクモードを使えるかどうかの違いに加え、強烈なトウの効果が、フィールド全体で抜きつ抜かれつの展開を生んだ。12周を終えても上位10台が9秒以内にひしめき、最終的にも6位までが7.955秒以内に収まった。 ノリスは「F1史上最もカオスなレースだったと思う。最高のレースができたとして、それで優勝を争えるのか、最下位で終わるのか、全く分からなかった」と振り返った。後続車が得るアドバンテージが大きく、前に出た途端に今度は自分が狙われる。批判の的となってきた新世代マシンの難点が、F1自らが主催する唯一のグランプリでこれほど露わになったのは皮肉に映った。 ランド・ノリス（マクラーレン）とマックス・フェルスタッペン（レッドブル）とオスカー・ピアストリ（マクラーレン）、2026年11月21日（土） F1ラスベガスGP 決勝（ラスベガス市街地コース） Courtesy Of McLaren 2026年11月21日（土） F1ラスベガスGP 決勝（ラスベガス市街地コース） Courtesy Of Pirelli & C. S.p.A. 勝敗を左右した電力配分の駆け引き 好スタートを切ったフェルスタッペンは首位でリードを広げたが、2周目のバックストレートで早くもジョージ・ラッセル（メルセデス）に抜かれた。ただ、同じ周の最終コーナーで抜き返すと、4周目にはアイザック・ハジャーがラッセルをかわし、レッドブルが1-2体制を築いた。 その後もフェルスタッペンは首位を奪い返し続けたが、終盤にはメルセデス勢がスタート・フィニッシュラインまで先頭を保てるエネルギーの使い方を見つけた。ファイナルラップで同じことが起きれば、ターン1で抜き返しても間に合わない。フェルスタッペンは無線で、最終周のライン上で首位に立つためのバッテリーの使い方を検討するようチームに求めた。 「序盤は電気エネルギーの使い方という点で上手くいっていた。でも、みんな僕らのやり方を見て学んでいくし、スタート・フィニッシュラインまでに首位を取り返せなくなった。だから無線で聞いたんだ」とフェルスタッペンは説明した。 「僕らのエネルギーマネジメントは良かったと思う。それでも、トウの効果があまりに大きくて引き離せなかった。こんなに多くのマシンがついてくるなんて、本当にクレイジーだった。F1でこんな光景は見たことがない」 残り3周、表彰台を争っていたラッセルはターン5への進入でタイヤをロックさせ、バリアに接触して9番手に後退。そのまま9位でレースを終えた。 6番グリッドからミディアムでスタートしたチームメイトのアンドレア・キミ・アントネッリは、終盤にフェルスタッペンと首位を争ったものの、 アクセル操作を誤った結果としてエネルギー制御システムが狂って失速 。マクラーレン勢に先行を許して4位に終わった。表彰台にメルセデスの姿はなかった。 オスカー・ピアストリ（マクラーレン MCL40）とランド・ノリス（マクラーレン MCL40）とフランコ・コラピント（アルピーヌ A526）、2026年11月21日（土） F1ラスベガスGP 決勝（ラスベガス市街地コース） Courtesy Of McLaren 波乱続出、ハジャーはウイング脱落で後退 波乱はスタート前から始まっていた。7番グリッドに着くはずだったリアム・ローソン（レーシング・ブルズ）は燃料漏れに見舞われ、ガレージでの修復作業がピットレーンの閉鎖に間に合わず、1周遅れでコースに入った。 14番グリッドからスタート予定だったアレックス・アルボン（ウィリアムズ）はブレーキのオーバーヒートにより車体を損傷。出走すらできなかった。スタートタイヤは、アントネッリ、ローソン、最後尾のオリバー・ベアマン（ハース）がミディアムを選び、他はソフトを選択した。 19周目にセルジオ・ペレス（キャデラック）とラファエル・カマラ（ハース）が衝突し、ペレスがリタイヤ。セーフティカー（SC）が導入されると、走行を続けていた各車がタイヤ交換に動いた。ローソンは周回遅れの解消を許されて首位と同一周回に戻り、最終周に1分35秒591のファステストラップを記録して15位でフィニッシュした。 一方、6番手を争っていたアーヴィッド・リンブラッド（レーシング・ブルズ）は、SC先導中にタイヤを温めようとマシンを左右に振った際にスピン。壁との接触は避けたものの、再始動できずにリタイヤした。 26周目のリスタート直後にはハジャーのフロントウイングが突如コース上に脱落。予定外のピットストップで表彰台争いから最後尾に転落し、14位に終わった。だが、 チームの指示を受けSC導入中に「不必要に低速で走行」したことでレース後に10秒ペナルティを受け 、15位に降格した。 アルピーヌ2台で18点得点、フェラーリまたも同士討ち ピエール・ガスリー（アルピーヌ）は序盤から表彰台を争ったが、ミディアムに履き替えてからは失速。それでも最終盤に持ち直して5位でフィニッシュした。チームメイトのフランコ・コラピントが6位に続き、アルピーヌは2台で18ポイントを獲得した。 フェラーリは2台ともが10秒ペナルティを受けた。序盤、ルイス・ハミルトンはターン9でノリスを抜いた際にコース外を走行し、アドバンテージを得たと判定された。38周目には、6番手を走るハミルトンにシャルル・ルクレールがアウト側から仕掛け、両者が接触。ハミルトンはスピンして10番手まで後退し、ルクレールに10秒ペナルティが科された。 最終順位はハミルトンが7位、ルクレールが10位だった。 チーム代表フレデリック・バスールがレース後に激怒 したのも無理はない。 カルロス・サインツ（ウィリアムズ）は20番グリッドから1周目だけで9つ順位を上げて11番手に浮上し、8位でフィニッシュした。カマラは対照的に、1周目に全ドライバーで最多となる3つのポジションを失い、18番手に後退。ペレスとの接触後も走行を続け、16位でレースを終えた。 アロンソ最終周にリタイヤ、アストン無得点 アストンマーティン・ホンダ勢は1周目に揃って順位を上げ、フェルナンド・アロンソが17番手、ランス・ストロールが19番手に浮上した。だがそれ以上の前進はなく、ストロールは17位でフィニッシュ。 アロンソはエンジンの異常を訴え 、最終周にピットへ戻ってリタイヤし、49周を走って19位扱いとなった。 スタート前に出走を断念したアルボンと、レース中にリタイヤしたペレス、リンブラッド、アロンソの計4人がチェッカーフラッグを受けられなかった。 2026年11月21日（土） F1ラスベガスGP 決勝（ラスベガス市街地コース） Courtesy Of McLaren 2026年F1第21戦 ラスベガスGP 決勝リザルト Pos No Driver Team Laps Time PTS 1 3 マックス・ records.title: El nuevo Ferrari F8 Tributo no impedirá que el modelo híbrido llegue al mercado
records.excerpt: Ferrari acaba de desvelar en Ginebra al nuevo F8 Tributo pero, aún así, ese misterioso híbrido seguirá en desarrollo hasta ocupar su correspondiente lugar. Ferrari Supersportive Il nuovo Ferrari F8 Tributo non impedirà che il modello ibrido arrivi sul mercato Javier López @jlopezbryan96 7 March 2019 3 min. Ferrari ha appena svelato a Ginevra la nuova F8 Tributo, ma, nonostante ciò, quel misterioso ibrido continuerà in sviluppo fino a occupare il posto che gli spetta. Negli ultimi mesi siamo stati testimoni di come un prototipo di collaudo con l’aspetto di una Ferrari 488 GTB circolasse per le strade in assoluto silenzio, un chiaro indizio del fatto che si trattasse di un veicolo ibrido . Tutte le nostre aspettative erano concentrate sul fatto che la casa del Cavallino Rampante approfittasse di questa edizione del Salone di Ginevra per presentare il tanto atteso modello, ma invece abbiamo conosciuto la F8 Tributo e il suo motore a combustione. Tuttavia, i prototipi di collaudo di questo modello continuano a circolare, il che ci spinge a pensare che presto condividerà la linea di produzione con l’ultima novità di Ferrari . È vero che Ferrari ha mantenuto invariati diversi componenti della 488 GTB per concepire la F8 Tributo, ma è possibile che gli ingegneri ricorrano maggiormente a quest’ultimo modello per completare la definizione di quella presunta Dino ibrida . Con questa premessa, possiamo prevedere che questo misterioso modello sarà basato sulla nuova F8 o che si presenterà come una sua variante, un evento che permetterà per la prima volta ai clienti di Ferrari di scegliere tra un’auto mossa interamente da un propulsore a combustione o da un motore ibrido . Grazie ai vari video che circolano sulle diverse reti sociali, possiamo vedere come la casa italiana vada avanti con lo sviluppo di questo modello . Così Ferrari intende non solo ampliare la sua gamma di modelli, ma anche avvicinare i suoi clienti a un mondo in cui efficienza, impegno e sportività vanno di pari passo per dimostrare che un motore ad alte prestazioni non è incompatibile con il rispetto per l’ambiente . Per il momento i prototipi di collaudo continuano a presentare caratteristiche più vicine a quelle della 488 GTB che a quelle della F8 Tributo, ma considerando che questo modello, già denominato Dino, si trova ancora in fase di sviluppo, possiamo aspettarci diverse modifiche al suo stile . In questo modo, possiamo attenderci che Ferrari adotti diversi canoni per completare la forma della sua supersportiva ibrida o, al contrario, la mantenga all’interno del suo ultimo linguaggio di design . La meccanica impiegata per animare questo modello è uno degli interrogativi che suscitano maggiore attesa, poiché si mormora la possibilità che sia un V6 a darle vita al posto del consueto V8 . Comunque sia, ci troveremo di fronte a un sistema ibrido che non solo permetterà di guidare in modalità 100% elettrica, come anticipano già i prototipi, ma anche di erogare ancora più potenza, potendo superare persino i 720 CV dichiarati dalla recentemente presentata F8 Tributo . https://youtu.be/7saAdK0uPAw Sarà molto presto quando Ferrari metterà la parola fine ai test di questa nuova creazione per dare vita alla variante di produzione . Questo evento segnerà un prima e un dopo all’interno della casa italiana, poiché tracerà la strada che seguiranno i modelli futuri, i quali potranno ricorrere anche all’ibridazione e persino a motori 100% elettrici . records.title: Nike e Formula 1: partnership globale e debutto a Las Vegas
records.excerpt: Nike e Formula 1: partnership globale e debutto a Las Vegas Vai al contenuto Newsletter Connettersi Nike e Formula 1 siglano partnership pluriennale per portare la velocità oltre il circuito Aggiornato il : 22 Novembre 2026 | Di : Davide Caruso X Facebook WhatsApp Share Nike e Formula 1 hanno svelato una collaborazione globale che promette di mescolare sport, moda e innovazione. L’intesa prevede abbigliamento, design e nuove esperienze durante i weekend di gara, con un debutto pubblico già programmato a Las Vegas. È l’inizio di un progetto che punta a coinvolgere tifosi, squadre e le nuove generazioni delle corse. Un accordo globale: cosa prevede la partnership Le due realtà hanno siglato un’intesa pluriennale. Dal 2027 Nike sarà partner ufficiale della Formula 1 e agirà come fornitore ufficiale di uniformi per lo staff presente agli eventi in tutto il mondo. L’accordo abbraccia più ambiti. Progettazione e produzione di capi tecnici e lifestyle. Innovazione sui materiali e design per le esigenze delle corse. Sviluppo di esperienze dedicate ai weekend di gara. I dettagli operativi saranno resi noti progressivamente durante la partnership. Capsule collection: l’anteprima a Las Vegas Prima del via ufficiale del 2027, la collaborazione offre al pubblico una preview. Durante il Gran Premio di Las Vegas Nike propone una capsule in edizione limitata . La linea è disponibile presso il Nike Store del Caesars Palace e allo F1 Hub del Venetian. La capsule Nike in edizione limitata esposta durante il Gran Premio di Las Vegas. Si tratta di un primo assaggio pensato per i fan. La capsule è sia un esercizio di stile sia un test sul mercato in vista di collezioni future . Uniformi e abbigliamento: il nuovo look dello staff Uno degli aspetti concreti dell’accordo riguarda i vestiti dello staff F1. Nike si occuperà delle uniformi ufficiali e di altri capi funzionali. Bozza di design e tessuti pensati per le uniformi dello staff F1. Progettazione ergonomica per chi lavora in gara. Materiali performanti ideati per le condizioni dei box e delle paddock. Estetica coordinata per gli eventi globali. L’obiettivo è coniugare performance e identità estetica su scala mondiale. F1 Academy: supporto alle nuove pilota e innovazione di prodotto Collaborazione dedicata alle donne nel motorsport La partnership include il sostegno alla F1 Academy , il campionato femminile pensato per formare le future protagoniste delle corse. Nike sarà Official Sporting Apparel Partner della serie. Il coinvolgimento non è solo commerciale. Le atlete parteciperanno allo sviluppo di capi pensati per le loro esigenze. Questo approccio punta a trasformare il feedback diretto in tecnologie e soluzioni di design. Le parole dei vertici: visione e motivazioni I dirigenti di Nike e della Formula 1 hanno sottolineato affinità culturali e ambizioni condivise. La partnership viene descritta come un incontro tra due marchi capaci di influenzare sport e cultura. Per Nike è un modo di portare il proprio know-how nello sport automobilistico. Per la Formula 1 è un passo verso nuove forme di coinvolgimento del pubblico. Secondo i protagonisti, la collaborazione dovrebbe imprimere energia e nuove idee allo spettacolo delle corse. Cosa possono aspettarsi i tifosi e i mercati Al momento certe sono alcune tappe iniziali: il ruolo ufficiale di Nike dal 2027, la capsule di Las Vegas e la presenza nella F1 Academy. Molte delle iniziative rimangono però aperte. Lancio delle uniformi ufficiali per lo staff a partire dal 2027. Disponibilità della capsule esclusiva durante il Gran Premio di Las Vegas. Sviluppo congiunto di prodotti performance per atlete della F1 Academy. Nuove collezioni, eventi speciali e format esperienziali verranno annunciati in seguito, man mano che il progetto prenderà forma. records.excerpt: Commercial Space Transportation | Federal Aviation Administration Skip to main content USA Banner An official website of the United States government Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. Secure .gov websites use HTTPS A lock ( ) or https:// means you’ve safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. United States Department of Transportation Commercial Space Transportation Countdown to launch. The FAA has reached a historic milestone with successful launch and reentry operations. See Stats Here FAA Reaches 1,000 Licensed Space Operations August 14, 2025 marked the FAA’s 1,000th operation of a commercial space vehicle that the agency licensed or permitted. The United States is a leader in space exploration, and this milestone highlights more than 35 years of the FAA successfully fulfilling its mission to protect safety and advance the future of our skies. The commercial space transportation industry emerged in the 1990s and was primarily used to launch commercial satellites and transport cargo to the International Space Station (ISS). In just the last few years, growing interest in commercial space is realizing new possibilities for the industry including providing transportation to the ISS laboratories for research and space tourism. This rapidly growing industry is inspiring scientists, engineers, teachers, and a whole generation, to imagine entirely new possibilities for the future of space. Safety Safety is our North Star. Compliance, Enforcement & Mishap Legislation & Policies Operations We protect the public, property, and U.S. national security interests. Airspace Integration Commercial Space Data Licensing We license all U.S. commercial launches and reentries here and abroad. Environmental Licenses, Permits and Approvals Stakeholder Engagement Vehicle Operator Licenses Industry Outreach We work collaboratively with industry to promote safety. Aerospace Rulemaking Committees: (SpARCs) COMSTAC Standards Development International We work with our international partners to promote safety. International Affairs Spaceports U.S. Spaceports are critical infrastructure for the industry. Office of Spaceports Spaceports by State Commercial Space By The Numbers Spaceports Map Find a U.S. spaceport near you. Map to commercial, government, and active private spaceports around the country. Learn about U.S. Spaceports Jobs What do we do? What careers are in commercial space? Commercial Space Transportation ensures that rocket launches and reentries are safe. We do this by applying a broad range of skillsets to manage licensing and regulatory work, as well as many programs and initiatives. Some examples of the jobs we do include inspecting reusable and expendable launch vehicles, assessing aerospace vehicle systems, developing public safety standards and requirements, assuring engineering quality, and assessing environmental impacts. Why does it matter? Our efforts help facilitate both the U.S. and global commercial space transportation industry’s health and growth. We value the talents, ideas, and insights that will enable us to continue our mission of ensuring and promoting the safest commercial space transportation in the world. records.title: SpaceX Dragon CRS-35 Splashdown Completes ISS Solar Upgrade, Returns Canadarm2 Robotic Arm Joint
records.excerpt: SpaceX Dragon CRS-35 splashdown on November 21, 2026 closed out the ISS Roll-Out Solar Array program, with Dragon C211 returning the eighth and final pair of Redwire-designed flexible iROSA solar... SpaceX's Cargo Dragon capsule splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the California coast on Friday, November 21, 2026, at 2:03 p.m. PST, closing out the CRS-35 resupply mission to the International Space Station. The recovery marked the successful end of a cargo run that quietly accomplished two of the most consequential hardware milestones in the station's recent operational history.Dragon Delivers and DepartsDragon C211 — on its fourth flight — launched October 13, 2026, at 6:33 a.m. EDT from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral on a Oct. 13 Falcon 9 launch of Booster B1096, making its eighth flight. Dragon docked to the Harmony module's forward port two days later and remained berthed for more than five weeks before undocking on November 20. The three-day weather delay caused by sustained high winds over the Pacific recovery zone pushed the original November 18 splashdown target to Friday.SpaceX recovery teams aboard the GO Navigator vessel retrieved the capsule and its cargo shortly after splashdown.The Final Pair of Solar ArraysThe headline cargo on the outbound leg of CRS-35 was a pair of ISS Roll-Out Solar Arrays — the seventh and eighth iROSAs in the station's power upgrade program, and the last the station will ever receive. Each iROSA is a roll-out solar wing designed by Redwire Space: a flexible photovoltaic blanket that unfurls from a compact stowage cylinder like a roll of carpet and deploys to full span without any hinged rigid panels. The design allows the arrays to be packed tightly enough to fit inside Dragon's unpressurized trunk and still cover a surface area large enough to meaningfully supplement the station's aging original solar arrays.The installation program spread across four Dragon missions — CRS-22, CRS-26, CRS-28, and CRS-35 — beginning in June 2021 and concluding with the final pair installed on the station's 2A and 3B power channels in late October and early November. The completed eight-array suite delivers more than 160 kW supplemental power across all eight arrays, enough to cover the growing electricity demands of research facilities added to the station over the past decade while also providing margin for future expansion. With all eight iROSAs in place, Boeing's solar power system for the station is now operating at its fully upgraded configuration.Canadarm2 Wrist Joint Returns to EarthThe second major hardware story of CRS-35 traveled in the opposite direction: the failed wrist joint from the 17.6-meter robotic arm built by MDA for the Canadian Space Agency, which has been in continuous service since its launch aboard Space Shuttle Atlantis during mission STS-100 in April 2001. The arm is equipped with seven joints and can lift payloads of up to 116,000 kilograms — a capability that makes it indispensable for berthing Dragon capsules, repositioning large station components, and supporting spacewalking astronauts.On May 27, 2026, engineers monitoring the arm's performance telemetry detected that the wrist joint was drawing elevated motor current, a classic indicator of mechanical binding or bearing wear. Ground teams temporarily restricted the joint's range of motion while they developed a repair plan. The arm itself remained functional for essential operations, but the fault limited its full articulation and introduced risk into time-sensitive berthing and assembly tasks.On June 30, 2026, NASA astronauts Chris Williams and Jessica Meir conducted U.S. Spacewalk 95 — lasting 7 hours and 20 minutes — to remove the failed wrist joint assembly and install a spare that had been stored aboard the station. The procedure restored the arm to full articulation, and Canadarm2 returned to unrestricted operations the same day. The repaired arm was used to assist with subsequent payload handling, including support for the iROSA installation spacewalks in October and November.The failed joint, returned to Earth inside Dragon's pressurized cargo bay, will now be examined by MDA engineers. Physical analysis of flight hardware can reveal failure mechanisms that telemetry alone cannot — information that may inform maintenance schedules for Canadarm2's remaining joints, which have no planned replacement on the books as the station targets operations through the 2030s. ISS extension scenarios assume the arm continues to operate without a successor system.Science Cargo Returning to EarthDragon's pressurized cargo hold carried more than 6,300 pounds (2,858 kilograms) of return cargo, the largest portion of which was scientific samples and experiment hardware accumulated during the Expedition 75 crew rotation.Among the science cargo were bioprinted blood vessel constructs developed using the reduced-gravity environment of microgravity, which allows cells to self-organize in three dimensions without the structural support scaffolding that Earth-based printing requires. The samples will be analyzed to assess whether microgravity-printed vascular structures exhibit geometry and mechanical properties comparable to native tissue — a capability that could have implications for pharmaceutical testing and, ultimately, for the bioprinting of transplantable grafts.Also returning: antibiotic-resistant bacterial cultures cultivated during the mission, protein crystal samples grown for a JAXA pharmaceutical structure-determination study, and blood and urine samples from the Expedition 75 crew for long-duration spaceflight health monitoring.Dragon C211's RecordDragon C211 has now completed four cargo missions: CRS-26, CRS-29, CRS-33, and CRS-35. SpaceX's reusable Dragon capsules are refurbished between flights and can carry both pressurized and unpressurized cargo in their trunk section. The trunk — which is not recovered and reenters the atmosphere after splashdown — carried the iROSA hardware on the outbound leg of CRS-35 and was jettisoned before reentry on the return.Frequently Asked QuestionsWhat did SpaceX Dragon CRS-35 deliver to the ISS?CRS-35 delivered the seventh and eighth ISS Roll-Out Solar Arrays — the final pair of Redwire-designed flexible solar wings to be installed on the station — along with science experiments, crew provisions, and hardware. The solar arrays were installed on the 2A and 3B power channels in October and November 2026, completing the station's iROSA upgrade program.Why was the CRS-35 Dragon splashdown delayed?The original splashdown target of November 18, 2026 was pushed back three days due to high winds over the Pacific recovery zone. NASA and SpaceX stood down from the November 18 attempt and rescheduled after weather conditions improved. Dragon ultimately splashed down on November 21 at 2:03 p.m. PST.What is Canadarm2 and why was its wrist joint repaired?Canadarm2 is a 17.6-meter robotic arm built by MDA for the Canadian Space Agency, in service on the ISS since April 2001. It is used to berth visiting spacecraft, move large components, and support spacewalking astronauts. In May 2026, its wrist joint began drawing elevated motor current, indicating mechanical wear. NASA astronauts Chris Williams and Jessica Meir replaced the faulty joint during U.S. Spacewalk 95 on June 30, 2026, restoring the arm to full operation. The failed joint returned to Earth aboard CRS-35 for engineering analysis.How many iROSA solar arrays does the ISS now have?Eight. The ISS Roll-Out Solar Array program installed arrays across four SpaceX Dragon cargo missions — CRS-22 (June 2021), CRS-26 (November 2022), CRS-28 (June 2023), and CRS-35 (October–November 2026). Each array sits atop one of the station's existing solar wing masts and supplements its power output. All eight are now installed and operational.

records.title: SpaceX Makes History With Starship Catch as Falcon 9 Launches New US Spy Satellites
records.excerpt: STARBASE, Texas, - SpaceX has reached a major milestone in reusable rocket technology while maintaining a busy launch schedule, highlighting the company's. US News SpaceX Makes History With Starship Catch as Falcon 9 Launches New US Spy Satellites By: Daniel Brooks | Editor: Matthew Reed | Contributor: Sophia Collins November 23, 2026 at 3:27 PM WITA · 5 min read SpaceX's Starship spacecraft returns to the launch tower at Starbase, Texas, on November 14, 2026, marking the first successful tower catch of a Starship upper stage following an orbital mission. Josh Dinner/Space.com STARBASE, Texas, Aktualita.co - SpaceX has reached a major milestone in reusable rocket technology while maintaining a busy launch schedule, highlighting the company's expanding role in commercial spaceflight, US national security and NASA's efforts to return astronauts to the Moon. The aerospace company, founded by Elon Musk, successfully brought its Starship spacecraft back from orbit on November 14, 2026, completing the first capture of a Starship upper stage by the giant mechanical arms of its launch tower in South Texas. The achievement followed a nearly 22.5-hour mission in which the spacecraft completed 14 orbits around Earth and deployed 26 next-generation Starlink satellites. Just over a week later, SpaceX launched another Falcon 9 rocket carrying classified satellites for the US National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) on November 22. Together, the missions demonstrate two sides of SpaceX's operations: its established satellite-launch business and its ambitious effort to develop a fully reusable rocket capable of supporting future missions to the Moon and Mars. SpaceX Starship Completes Historic Return From Orbit Starship Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX's Starbase facility in Texas on November 13, beginning one of the most ambitious demonstrations in the company's rocket development program. The mission involved the Super Heavy booster and the Starship upper stage, collectively forming the largest operational rocket system currently under development. After separating from its booster, Starship entered low Earth orbit and began a mission lasting nearly a full day. During the flight, the spacecraft released 26 Starlink satellites before preparing for a carefully controlled return through Earth's atmosphere. On November 14, Starship descended toward Starbase after enduring the extreme temperatures associated with atmospheric reentry. Its engines reignited during the final descent, allowing the spacecraft to rotate into a vertical position before being caught by the launch tower's mechanical arms, commonly known as "chopsticks." The maneuver marked an important achievement for SpaceX's long-term goal of recovering both stages of its Starship launch system. "That was the missing link, the holy grail of spaceflight," said SpaceX mission commentator Dan Huot following the successful spacecraft recovery. The recovery also provided engineers with an opportunity to examine the spacecraft's structure, thermal protection system and engines after an extended orbital mission. Super Heavy Booster Recovery Remains a Challenge Despite the successful Starship landing, Flight 15 did not accomplish every objective. SpaceX originally intended to recover both the Super Heavy booster and the Starship spacecraft at the launch site. However, the booster experienced a problem during its return shortly after launch, preventing the planned tower catch. The vehicle instead diverted toward the Gulf of Mexico and was subsequently destroyed. During SpaceX's mission coverage, company representative Kate Tice explained that preliminary information indicated a fuel-related warning during the booster's return maneuver. "The team is still investigating the root cause on that," SpaceX representative Kate Tice said during the Flight 15 webcast. The setback means SpaceX has not yet demonstrated the recovery of both Starship stages during a single orbital mission. Another major engineering challenge involves developing a heat shield that can withstand repeated atmospheric reentries without requiring extensive repairs. Although Starship survived its latest return, engineers must determine how much refurbishment will be necessary before recovered spacecraft can fly again. Falcon 9 Launches US Intelligence Satellites While Starship development continues, SpaceX's Falcon 9 rocket remains central to its commercial and government launch operations. On November 22, a Falcon 9 lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California at approximately 4:23 a.m. Pacific Standard Time. The mission, designated NROL-136, carried classified satellites for the National Reconnaissance Office. The spacecraft are part of the agency's expanding satellite architecture, designed to improve the collection and delivery of intelligence from low Earth orbit. Specific details about the payloads have not been publicly disclosed. Following liftoff, the Falcon 9 first-stage booster successfully returned to Landing Zone 4 at Vandenberg. The booster, identified as B1097, completed its 14th flight, demonstrating the operational maturity of SpaceX's reusable Falcon system. The mission also reflected the company's increasingly rapid launch operations, with another Falcon 9 mission having departed the same California facility less than two days earlier. Unlike Starship, Falcon 9 currently recovers its first stage while its upper stage is generally expended after delivering spacecraft into orbit. SpaceX hopes Starship will eventually eliminate that limitation. Why Starship Matters for NASA's Moon Missions Beyond satellite launches, Starship is expected to play an important role in NASA's Artemis program. NASA has selected SpaceX and Blue Origin to develop human landing systems intended to transport astronauts between lunar orbit and the Moon's surface. In an October 23, 2026, announcement, NASA outlined changes to its lunar landing architecture as the agency works toward crewed Moon landings in 2028. Under the revised approach, SpaceX's Starship Human Landing System would rendezvous with NASA's Orion spacecraft in Earth orbit before traveling toward the Moon. The planned architecture also requires SpaceX to demonstrate the transfer of cryogenic propellants between spacecraft in orbit. This capability is particularly important because Starship's lunar missions are expected to require multiple tanker launches to supply the necessary fuel. records.title: SpaceX Sets 32 Hour Falcon 9 Launch Turnaround Record
records.excerpt: SpaceX launched two Falcon 9 rockets from the same California pad 32 hours apart, setting a new turnaround record while advancing classified satellite missions. Rapid launch operations at California's Vandenberg Space Force Base reached a new milestone on November 22, 2026, when SpaceX sent another Falcon 9 rocket into orbit for the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office (NRO). The mission, designated NROL-136, followed another launch from the same pad just 32 hours earlier, establishing a new turnaround record.The rocket departed Launch Complex-4E at 4:23 a.m. local time, carrying classified satellites toward low Earth orbit. According to Space.com, the interval between the two launches was precisely 32 hours, 3 minutes and 21 seconds.SpaceX's previous record for consecutive launches from a single pad was 45 hours, achieved at Pad 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. The latest achievement brings the company closer to its stated goal of reducing launch preparation time to 24 hours.Kiko Dontchev, SpaceX's vice president of launch, credited the company's West Coast team for the accomplishment in a November 22 post on X."Massive high five to the @SpaceX west coast team for a world record launch to launch turn from Pad 4e last night! 32 hr, 3 min, 21 sec! This smashed the previous record of 45 hrs from Pad 40. Team got there with several hours of margin.Next goal… the 24 hr turn!" Dontchev said.The NROL-136 mission also continued the intelligence agency's expansion of its proliferated satellite network. According to the NRO, the architecture is intended to strengthen global surveillance coverage and improve the resilience of U.S. intelligence operations in space.NROL-136 represented the network's 15th dedicated deployment mission and the NRO's sixth launch of 2026. SpaceX and Northrop Grumman developed the satellite architecture in partnership with the agency, which began deploying the constellation in May 2024 through the NROL-146 mission.The NRO has not disclosed how many satellites NROL-136 carried or provided details about their onboard equipment. All six of its launches during 2026 have used Falcon 9 rockets to deliver classified payloads into low Earth orbit, according to Space.com.The rocket's first-stage booster separated approximately two minutes after liftoff before returning to Vandenberg. It landed at Landing Zone 4 around seven and a half minutes after launch, completing another recovery operation.The booster, identified as B1097, completed its 14th flight. Its previous assignments included NASA's Sentinel-6B ocean-monitoring satellite, NROL-172, USSF-259 and eight Starlink missions.Separately, SpaceX is pursuing another major development in reusable launch technology through its Starship program. Ship 42, the first Starship upper stage successfully caught by the launch tower's mechanical arms, will not return to flight despite being considered technically capable of flying again.Speaking at the TomorrowX Summit on November 18, SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk explained that the company intends to preserve the vehicle because of its historical significance."In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said.Ship 42 completed Starship's 15th test flight, launched November 13, and returned to the company's Starbase facility in South Texas the following day. Musk said the vehicle had performed well enough that it could potentially fly again after several weeks of refurbishment.The recovery marked a significant step toward SpaceX's ambition of developing a fully reusable orbital transportation system. Before that mission, the company had successfully caught its Super Heavy first-stage booster three times and reflown a booster twice, but had never caught a Starship upper stage."Everyone knew, within SpaceX, at least, how important this milestone was, and that it was really something fundamental and profound — that Starship will be the first-ever fully reusable orbital space system," Musk said.SpaceX also plans to use Starship to deploy much larger satellite networks. The next-generation Starlink constellation is planned to contain approximately 100,000 satellites, while the proposed Starmind AI data-center constellation is expected to be 10 times larger.The company has already begun deploying next-generation Starlink hardware. Ship carried 26 of the new internet satellites during Flight 14, launched September 28, and repeated the deployment during Flight 15.

records.title: Musk Signals Interest in Hiring Jensen Huang at SpaceX
records.excerpt: Elon Musk expressed interest in hiring Jensen Huang as SpaceX expands its AI supercomputing and semiconductor ambitions. Space Exploration Technologies (NasdaqGS: SPCX) attracted investor attention on November 20, 2026, after Elon Musk publicly expressed interest in hiring Jensen Huang. The potential recruitment has drawn attention to SpaceX's growing artificial intelligence and semiconductor ambitions amid regulatory scrutiny facing Huang.Investors connected Musk's remarks to SpaceX's plans for AI supercomputing campuses and advanced semiconductor design projects. Huang's potential involvement could bring additional expertise to a business increasingly focused on computing infrastructure and chip development.SpaceX operates a satellite-based broadband network serving the United States and key international markets. Greater expertise in AI and semiconductor engineering could support the efficiency of its data transmission systems and the expansion of its digital infrastructure.The company's investment strategy already emphasizes growing demand for global AI computing capacity. According to Simply Wall St's analysis, large-scale capital expenditure on Colossus-scale infrastructure represents a central growth driver, although project execution remains a significant risk.The analysis also identifies concerns surrounding substantial spending, a limited cash runway, and the potential returns from the company's planned US$74 billion supercomputing investment.Musk's interest in Huang highlights the increasing importance of AI computing and chip design within SpaceX's broader business ambitions. However, the potential recruitment alone does not resolve questions about the financial sustainability or expected returns of the infrastructure expansion.Attention is now turning to SpaceX's anticipated December merger update, when the company could provide additional information about its AI infrastructure projects.Investors are particularly watching for details about the expected installed computing capacity, measured in gigawatts, across the company's Texas and Arizona campuses. Further disclosure could also identify the senior executives responsible for overseeing those developments.

records.title: AnthropicとSpaceX、IPO主幹事に競合他社との取引禁止を要求…ウォール街で「横暴」論争
records.excerpt: Anthropicが813億ドル（約12.9兆円）規模のIPOを推進するにあたり、主幹事証券会社の核心人材に対し、上場後6カ月間OpenAIなど競合他社の業務を禁じる条件を要求していたことが明らかになった。人員を4人に制限し、午前2時の緊急書類承認を求め、グリーンシュー（追加割当）手数料を未払いとするなどの条件も併せて課した。SpaceXも同様の一方的な条件を提示しており、ウォール街では大型発行体と投資銀行の間の力関係が変わったとの分析が出ている。 米国の人工知能（AI）企業Anthropicが史上最大規模の新規株式公開（IPO）を推進するなか、主幹事証券会社に前例のない水準の制約条件を課していた事実が明らかになった。競合他社との業務を一定期間禁じる条項から、人員投入の制限、未明の時間帯における緊急書類承認の要求まで含まれており、ウォール街の内外で反発が起きている。 22日（現地時間）の外信報道によると、Anthropicは19日のナスダック上場を控え、IPOを担当した投資銀行（IB）チームの核心人材に対し、上場後6カ月間、OpenAI、Cursor、DeepSeek、Hugging Faceなど競合企業に関連する業務を担当しないとする内容の法的文書への署名を求めた。一部の銀行の高位役員がこれへの署名を拒否したとの話も伝わっている。 金融機関は通常、顧客の機密保護と利益相反管理のための内部規程を設けているが、個々の職員に対し特定の競合他社との業務を6カ月間全面禁止する条件を求めるのは極めて異例だ。あるIB関係者は、AI関連の大型上場が相次ぐと予想される状況で、6カ月間競合他社に関与しないと約束する人材を確保するのは容易ではなかったと語った。 人員構成にも制限が付いた。Anthropicは22の引受金融機関のうち一部について、案件に投入する人数を4人以内に減らし、必ず高位職でなければならないとする条件を提示した。会社情報の流出を防ぐための措置と解釈されるが、一部の銀行は業務過程で人員制限を迂回する形で対応したとされる。 情報アクセスの統制も強化された。Anthropicは通常のPDFファイルではなく、文書の閲覧履歴がすべて記録され、複製保存が不可能な「NetRoadshow」プラットフォームを通じて大半の証券会社と情報を共有した。文書には担当銀行員の個人名が透かしとして刻まれた。 切迫した日程も混乱を助長した。10日の販売活動開始を前に、証券会社には誤った公募価格帯と株式数が記載された書類が先に送付され、訂正されたS-1A書類はニューヨーク時間の午前2時ごろにようやく届いた。銀行は米国証券取引委員会（SEC）への提出期限に間に合わせるため、わずか数時間で検討と承認を終えなければならなかった。 先に6月に上場を果たしたSpaceXの条件はさらに一方的だったとの評価もある。ゴールドマン・サックスやMorgan Stanleyなど主幹事に対し、手数料の規模すら知らせないまま契約書への署名を求め、銀行ごとに確保すべき投資家の類型と注文規模を指定して通知した。AnthropicとSpaceXはいずれも、追加割当オプション（グリーンシュー）で販売される追加株式については引受手数料を一切支払わない方針としたと伝えられている。 項目 Anthropic SpaceX 上場時期 2026年11月19日 2026年6月 調達規模 813億ドル（約12.9兆円） 史上最大記録更新前の基準 主幹事数 22社 複数 引受手数料 約5.5億ドル（約870億円） 非公開 競合他社業務の制限 6カ月、核心人材対象 別段の制限は確認されず グリーンシュー手数料 未払い 未払い 注：調達規模と手数料はAnthropic基準 Anthropicの今回の上場は813億ドル（約12.9兆円）を調達し、6月にSpaceXが打ち立てた最大IPO記録を上回った。22の引受金融機関が受け取る引受手数料は約5.5億ドル（約870億円）に達する。巨額の手数料にもかかわらず、一部の銀行関係者はAnthropicが上場過程の全体を過度に統制したと指摘する。 市場では技術企業とウォール街の間の力関係が変わったとの分析が出ている。フロリダ大学のJay Ritter名誉教授は、これらの企業が市場支配力を背景に、引受団に対して通常とは異なる条件を要求できる交渉力を確保したと評価した。ただ株価の動きは厳しい。SpaceXは6月16日に201.8ドル（約3.2万円）の高値をつけた後、7月中旬には135ドル（約2.1万円）の公募価格を下回った。Anthropicは上場初日に17%急騰したものの、その後AI関連株の調整に見舞われ、直近では8.5%下落して取引を終えた。 今回の件は、今後のAI企業の上場ラッシュにおいて、主幹事の選定や手数料交渉の慣行に影響を与え得るとの見方を生んでいる。大型発行体が有利な条件を貫徹する事例が繰り返されれば、引受団の収益性や人員配置戦略にも変化が避けられないとの指摘だ。Anthropicと主幹事のゴールドマン・サックス、Morgan Stanleyはコメント要請に応じず、SpaceXも回答しなかった。

records.title: SpaceX Fell Below Its IPO Price. Gene Munster Says It Trades at “10 Times Revenue” Growing 270%
records.excerpt: Title: SpaceX Fell Below Its IPO Price. Gene Munster Says It Trades at “10 Times Revenue” Growing 270% URL Source: http://www.tikr.com/ja/blog/spacex-fell-below-its-ipo-price-gene-munster-says-it-trades-at-10-times-revenue-growing-270 Final URL: https://www.tikr.com/ja/blog/spacex-fell-below-its-ipo-price-gene-munster-says-it-trades-at-10-times-revenue-growing-270 Published Time: 2026-11-23T13:38:00 Markdown Content: ## 主なポイント * SpaceXは金曜日に$135のIPO価格を下回り、これはAnthropicが上場した週のことだった。 * Gene Munsterは、SpaceXが売上高10倍で270%成長していることから、Anthropicよりも優れた買い物だと主張しており、TIKRの数字も彼の計算をほぼ裏付けている。 * SpaceXの成長の多くは、最大の賃借人が90日前通知でキャンセル可能なAIコンピュートの賃貸収入であり、CoreWeaveはそのような収入が利益を保証するものではないことを示している。 * SpaceXの方がより良い価値に見えるが、2027年第1四半期の売上高は、$330億から$370億という業績見通しの上限近くに到達する必要がある。 **SpaceX ([SPCX](https://app.tikr.com/stock/about?cid=7702894&tid=321424200))**は金曜日に$135のIPO価格を下回った。これは**Anthropic ([ANT](https://app.tikr.com/stock/about?cid=716923717&tid=2030909033))**が$1,073億を調達して自社のIPOを行ったのと同じ週のことだ。 他のAIコンピュート株も苦戦している：**CoreWeave ([CRWV](https://app.tikr.com/stock/about?cid=605989324&tid=1933861078))**は過去1年で43%下落した。 しかし、Deepwater Asset Managementのマネージング・パートナーであるGene Munsterは、投資家がこの取引を逆に捉えているかもしれないと考えている。木曜日の[CNBCのFast Money](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/anthropic-jumps-in-massive-debut-but-broad-markets-sell-off/id215529509?i=1000803020984)のエピソードで、彼は「売上高14倍で130%成長のAnthropic」を所有するのと、「売上高10倍で270%成長のSpaceXのようなもの」を所有するのと、どちらがより理にかなっているかと問いかけた。 NYU Sternの教授であるScott Gallowayはこれに同意しない。今週のPivotポッドキャストで、彼はAnthropicを「売上高20倍または25倍」、SpaceXを「120倍」と評価した。 ## Munsterの数字は正しい 270%という数字は、ウォールストリートの予想から直接来ており、SpaceXの売上高が来年ほぼ4倍になると見込まれている： ![Image 1: TIKRによるSpaceXの売上高（実績とコンセンサス予想）、$10億単位、2026-2028会計年度。](https://res.cloudinary.com/tikr/images/w_3024,h_2016,c_scale/f_webp,q_auto/v1795204605/images/2026-11-20_if02e9e25ea_SPCX_revenue_estimates_2023-2028/2026-11-20_if02e9e25ea_SPCX_revenue_estimates_2023-2028.png?_i=AA) SpaceX (SPCX): 売上高、実績とコンセンサス予想、$10億単位、2026-2028会計年度 (**TIKR**) アナリストは2027年に$1,800億の売上高を見込んでおり、今年の$488億と比較して約3.7倍、つまり約269%の成長となる。 TIKRの売上高倍率も彼の10倍に近い。SpaceXは11月19日時点でフォワード売上高13倍で取引されていた： ![Image 2: TIKRによるSpaceXのフォワード（NTM）株価売上高倍率の推移（上場以来）。](https://res.cloudinary.com/tikr/images/w_3024,h_2016,c_scale/f_webp,q_auto/v1795204603/images/2026-11-20_if02e9e25ea_SPCX_ntm_ps_1yr/2026-11-20_if02e9e25ea_SPCX_ntm_ps_1yr.png?_i=AA) SpaceX (SPCX): フォワード（NTM）株価売上高倍率、上場以来 (**TIKR**) これは11月5日の11倍という安値に近く、6月の上場以来の平均27倍の半分以下だ。Gallowayの120倍という数字はチャートのどこにも見当たらない。IPO直後のピーク時でさえ、SpaceXは62倍で取引されていた。 **TIKRはSpaceXについて40人のアナリストを追跡している。「買い」と言っているのは何人か？** SpaceXの買い、保有、売りのレーティングの完全な内訳と、ウォールストリートの売上高・利益予想をすべて一箇所で確認できる。50万人以上の投資家がTIKRを利用してこのような銘柄を調査している。[SpaceXのアナリスト・レーティングを見る](https://www.tikr.com/analyst-ratings) ## ギャップは来年の売上高にある 私の推測では、GallowayはSpaceXをすでに計上済みの売上高で評価しているのだろう。それは9月30日までの12ヶ月間で$320億であり、ウォールストリートは2027年にその5倍以上を見込んでいる。 SpaceX自身の業績見通しはまだ$1,800億には達していない。経営陣は2027年第1四半期の売上高を$330億から$370億と見通しており、そのペースで4四半期続くと$1,320億から$1,480億となる。したがって、予想に到達するには年間を通じて売上高が上昇し続ける必要がある。 ## 成長の半分は賃貸収入 これまでの成長は本物だ。SpaceXの売上高は第2四半期から第3四半期にかけてほぼ倍増した： ![Image 3: TIKRによるSpaceXの総売上高、$10億単位、過去6四半期（2026年9月30日まで）。](https://res.cloudinary.com/tikr/images/w_3024,h_2016,c_scale/f_webp,q_auto/v1795204601/images/2026-11-20_if02e9e25ea_SPCX_revenue_8q/2026-11-20_if02e9e25ea_SPCX_revenue_8q.png?_i=AA) SpaceX (SPCX): 総売上高、$10億単位、過去6四半期（2026年9月30日まで） (**TIKR**) 第3四半期の売上高は$146億に達し、第2四半期の$78.1億、1年前の$55.8億から増加した。そのうちAIセグメントが$75.6億をもたらし、単独の顧客が会社全体の34.5%を占めた。Anthropicは[SpaceXの最大のコンピュート賃借人](https://www.tikr.com/blog/bernstein-sees-95-upside-in-spacex-and-the-reason-has-nothing-to-do-with-data-centers-in-space)であり、契約の最初の3ヶ月後は、いずれかの側が90日前通知で契約を終了できる。 ## CoreWeaveが示す賃貸コンピュートの収益性 CoreWeaveの第3四半期売上高は168%増の$36.6億に跳ね上がった。しかし、$8.46億の正味支払利息が$2.07億の営業利益を圧倒し、$7.09億のGAAP純損失を計上した。アナリストは2027年まで調整後損失が続くと見込んでいる。 一方、SpaceXのAIセグメントは、第3四半期にCursor買収に伴う$12.2億の株式報酬を差し引いた後、$4.31億の営業利益を稼いだ。 ## より安価で、Starlinkが基盤にある Munsterの主張の方が優れている：投資家はすでに2027年に対する多くの疑念を織り込んでいる。そしてSpaceXにはAnthropicにはない利益エンジンがある：Starlinkのコネクティビティセグメントは、SpaceXの第3四半期営業利益$27.9億のうち$23.7億を稼いだ。 この価格では、AnthropicよりもSpaceXを所有したいと思うが、完全な270%成長には賭けないだろう。 最初の試練は2027年初頭の第4四半期決算で訪れる：12月の売上高は$83億に達し、SpaceXの$1,000億という年間化目標を達成する必要がある。その後、第1四半期の売上高が$330億から$370億の範囲の上限近くに達すれば、$1,800億が視野に入り続けるが、$330億を下回る結果であれば予想が下方修正され、Munsterの270%も同様に引き下げられるだろう。 ## では、SpaceXの株価の実際の価値は？ TIKRを使えば、あらゆる銘柄の将来価格を1分以内に予測できる。TIKRのバリュエーションモデルにいくつかの仮定を入力するだけで、SpaceXがどの程度の価値になる可能性があるかがわかる。ウォールストリートのコンセンサス予想から始めることも、ビジネスに対する独自の見解を反映するために入力を調整することもできる。無料で利用可能だ。 [SpaceXを無料で評価する](https://www.tikr.com/stock-valuation) ### **免責事項：** _TIKRの記事は、TIKRまたは当社のコンテンツチームによる投資または財務上のアドバイスとして、またいかなる株式の売買の推奨としても意図されていないことにご注意ください。当社のコンテンツは、TIKR Terminalの投資データとアナリストの予想に基づいて作成されています。当社の分析には、最近の企業ニュースや重要なアップデートが含まれていない場合があります。TIKRは、言及されたいかなる銘柄にもポジションを保有していません。お読みいただきありがとうございます。幸運な投資を！_

records.title: 2 Reasons Anthropic’s IPO Is a Bigger Risk to the Stock Market Than SpaceX’s
records.excerpt: Free Article Explore Premium Services 2 Reasons Anthropic’s IPO Is a Bigger Risk to the Stock Market Than SpaceX’s Anthropic’s IPO is a market-disrupting event, but it could also create opportunities in the long run. By Daniel Foelber – Nov 23, 2026 at 11:15AM EST Key Points SpaceX was added to the communications sector, which doesn’t attract as much ETF capital as the tech sector. Anthropic could make the tech sector’s weight in the major indexes even more dominant. Anthropic's appetite for compute capacity is a key catalyst behind hyperscaler data center spending. 10 stocks we like better than Anthropic › Anthropic ( ANT -1.43% ) jumped 17.1% on Nov. 19 -- surpassing Space Exploration Technologies ( SPCX +4.35% ) as the largest initial public offering (IPO) in history after raising roughly $81.3 billion. However, SpaceX remains far more valuable, with a market cap of $1.88 trillion compared to $1.27 trillion for Anthropic. Here's why Anthropic could have an even larger impact on the broader stock market than SpaceX and how the IPO is impacting investors even if they don't plan to buy Anthropic directly. Dario Amodei. Image source: Getty Images. 1. Anthropic could make the tech sector even more dominant The Nasdaq-100 is the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange by market cap. SpaceX joined the Nasdaq-100 less than one month after going public thanks to the index's new fast-tracked rules that allow mega-cap companies to be added to the Nasdaq-100 after their 15th trading day. However, the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC +4.73% ) still requires companies to be public for at least a year before they can be added. Anthropic is likely to be added to the Nasdaq-100 in early December, which will impact index-linked products like the Invesco QQQ Trust ( QQQ +7.00% ) . Several passively managed, high-profile exchange-traded funds (ETFs), including nine Vanguard ETFs , began buying SpaceX within weeks of its IPO. And I would expect the same for Anthropic. However, Anthropic's impact on the major indexes could be even larger than SpaceX's if it's classified as a tech stock . The tech sector makes up a staggering 64.4% of the Nasdaq-100 -- as measured by the Invesco QQQ Trust -- and 37.4% of the S&P 500. Despite it being a tech-focused company, Vanguard classified SpaceX in the communications sector alongside Alphabet ( GOOG +5.88% ) ( GOOGL +6.34% ) and Meta Platforms ( META +6.55% ) . Similarly, Amazon ( AMZN +3.47% ) and Tesla ( TSLA +11.46% ) are in the consumer discretionary sector despite being tech-focused companies. If Anthropic is classified as a technology stock, it will make the Nasdaq-100 (and eventually the S&P 500) even more concentrated in the tech sector. It would also have far-reaching effects on market-cap-weighted tech sector ETFs -- which are larger than other sector ETFs. For example, the Vanguard Communications Services ETF ( VOX +4.11% ) , which has added to its SpaceX holdings every month since it went public , has $5.4 billion in net assets, whereas the Vanguard Information Technology ETF ( VGT +8.98% ) has a staggering $145.1 billion in net assets. And that's just one investment management company's ETFs. SPCX - Space Exploration Technologies $133.35 +$5.56 (+4.35%) NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26 Key data points Market cap Market cap calculated using publicly traded shares outstanding only. Does not include unlisted, private, or dual-class non-traded shares. Implied market cap may vary. $1.81T Day's range $133.10 - $141.87 52wk range $104.83 - $225.64 Volume 96.2M Avg volume 95.8M 2. Many companies indirectly benefit from Anthropic's growth Anthropic plays a far more important role in the artificial intelligence (AI) value chain than SpaceX. SpaceX owns xAI and has plans to build constellations of orbital data centers . But for now, most of its revenue comes from its Starlink network of broadband and mobile satellites. Anthropic arguably makes the most important family of large language models -- Claude. Anthropic is driving massive demand for compute capacity. It is a big reason why hyperscalers are aggressively investing in AI data centers , with ripple effects for chip companies and data center pick-and-shovel plays such as specialty machinery companies, industrials, utilities, and energy . In addition to Anthropic’s own demand for compute, many third-party AI agents and AI tools rely on foundational models like Claude, thereby amplifying the full impact on data center demand. Anthropic is much more important to the market than its individual weighting will be in the major indexes. It's a similar dynamic to what we've seen play out with Nvidia ( NVDA +31.48% ) . Jensen Huang's sudden resignation sparked a massive sell-off in companies that depend on or do business with Nvidia. And beyond that, Huang has been a major proponent of AI innovation and dealmaking , impacting financial markets far beyond Nvidia's own deals. So just as Nvidia is arguably the most important company in the AI infrastructure layer of the value chain, Anthropic is probably the most vital company in the foundational model layer. Moving forward after Anthropic’s IPO With the market in a steep sell-off, some investors may view the Anthropic IPO as yet another factor that could add to volatility. And while the Anthropic IPO is arguably an even bigger risk to the market than the SpaceX IPO, it also has the potential to be an incredible opportunity. If Anthropic can continue delivering excellent revenue growth, it could be a catalyst for the broader tech sector and indexes. Especially if that growth coincides with more demand for even better AI chips, which would benefit the broader semiconductor industry . Investors interested in gaining exposure to Anthropic without buying the stock directly may want to consider a low-cost tech sector ETF like the Vanguard Information Technology ETF or the Vanguard Growth ETF ( VUG +6.82% ) , which invests in growth stocks from all stock market sectors . These ETFs will likely gradually accumulate a larger stake in Anthropic as more shares are unlocked and sold by insiders and early investors on the Nasdaq. On the other hand, investors looking to avoid Anthropic altogether may want to stick with high-conviction individual stocks or value and non-tech sector ETFs . records.title: Starlink Debuts Gigabit Plan At $4,650 Per Month For Cargo Ships
records.excerpt:
Starlink is asking early adopters to apply for the upcoming 'Global Business Merchant' plan, which is slated to arrive next year.

Starlink is preparing to offer gigabit speeds through an expensive new satellite internet plan meant for large commercial shipping vessels.

The official Starlink.com has updated its “Maritime” plans to introduce the “Global Business Merchant” tier, which will officially launch next year at a rather staggering $4,650 per month —more than double the Global Priority 2 TB plan at $2,150 per month.

“This plan is designed for merchant vessels that need unlimited priority connectivity in port, coastal areas, and on international waters,” SpaceX says. The plan includes unlimited data for global ocean coverage and up to two Starlink kits, although the dish models weren’t identified.

You May Also Like

The plan arrives as SpaceX has started to launch and operate new V3 satellites, which have been designed to offer gigabit speeds and drastically expand Starlink’s network capacity. Back in September, the company indicated it’d start offering gigabit speeds over the $1,999 Performance Gen 3 kit by the end of this year for eligible maritime users. When gigabit speeds will come to consumer subscribers has been left unclear.

For now, SpaceX only has 52 V3 satellites in orbit, not enough to offer global consistent coverage. Still, the number is expected to grow as SpaceX conducts more Starship launches. “I think we’ll need a few hundred V3 satellites for people to really feel the impact,” the company’s President Gwynne Shotwell said in an earnings call last month. “So, a few hundred satellites, and I think we can achieve that by mid next year.”

records.excerpt: Reliance Plans Satellite Network to Offset Starlink Reach in India - Inside Towers Media Kit Login Facebook Twitter Instagram Linkedin Subscribe Reliance Plans Satellite Network to Offset Starlink Reach in India November 23, 2026 5:55 am SHARE THIS ARTICLE Mumbai, India-based Reliance Industries is seeking manufacturing partners for 1,600 planned low-Earth orbit broadband satellites, accelerating its domestic challenge to SpaceX’s Starlink, Economic Times reported. It is negotiating deals with Indian satellite manufacturers, technology startups and industrial groups, offering infrastructure funding to boost production. Reliance also is discussing purchases with two unnamed U.S. firms and weighing European, but not Chinese, suppliers, according to Bloomberg . To offset India’s limited production capacity, it plans domestic manufacturing plus imports, including at least 400 U.S.-made satellites. India produces fewer than 15 satellites annually versus roughly 200 needed for the constellation, sources told Bloomberg . The LEO network would support growth of Reliance’s newly listed telecoms unit, Jio Platforms, which owns Reliance Jio, India’s largest mobile network operator, according to Inside Towers Intelligence . Primarily aimed at expanding connectivity across India, especially remote areas, the constellation could also support India’s strategic communications, according to Economic Times . Plans call for a September 2027 test mission and deployment from early 2028 through 2035. Completion moved five years from the original 2030 target due to manufacturing and launch constraints and delayed regulatory approvals, Bloomberg reported. records.title: Musk Says Tesla Hopes to Offer Built-In Starlink Beyond Cybercab by Late 2027
records.excerpt: Tesla hopes to offer Starlink satellite internet built into models other than the Cybercab toward the end of 2027, Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk said, giving the first timeframe for bringing the connection to the wider lineup. Musk Says Tesla Hopes to Offer Built-In Starlink Beyond Cybercab by Late 2027 Credit: Joe Tegtmeyer By Cláudio Afonso Nov. 23, 2026, 6:13 AM ET 4 min read Tesla hopes to offer Starlink satellite internet built into models other than the Cybercab toward the end of 2027, Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk said, giving the first timeframe for bringing the connection to the wider lineup. “Hopefully available towards the end of next year,” Musk wrote on X on Sunday. “This will be important for unsupervised FSD, so passengers have high bandwidth everywhere for work and entertainment.” Musk was replying to David Marcus, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer of payments company Lightspark and a former President of PayPal, who wrote that he could not wait for Tesla “to offer an embedded Starlink option in all models (beyond the Cybercab).” Musk did not say which models would get the hardware, what it would cost, whether it would be standard or optional, or whether cars already on the road could be retrofitted. In a separate reply on Sunday, Musk said the feature would not come to Tesla’s cars in China. “Except in China, as Starlink is illegal there,” he wrote. He was responding to investor Sawyer Merritt, who had summarized Musk’s comments and noted that the Cybercabs now carrying riders in Dallas already have the hardware, “although it doesn’t seem like riders can connect to it yet.” From One Model to All Musk has been pointing to a wider rollout since July. “Starlink will be integrated into all our car vehicles, at least for markets that Starlink is active,” he said on Tesla’s second-quarter earnings call on July 22. “For a Robotaxi situation, you need to have coverage everywhere,” Musk said on the call, including in places “where the cellular coverage is terrible or sometimes non-existent.” “We can’t have Robotaxis getting stuck in these Bermuda Triangles of lack of cellular connectivity,” he said. “With Starlink, you can watch 4K live sports in the car,” he added. Two days earlier, Tesla announced that the Cybercab would be the first vehicle in its lineup with a Starlink V5 terminal built in. “Watch 4K streaming video while Cybercab takes you anywhere you want,” Musk wrote on X that day. On August 9, Musk wrote that “all cars will have Starlink in the future.” Sunday’s reply is the first time he has put a date on that. What the Link Is For Tesla’s own AI lead has played down Starlink’s role in driving. “It is still not required for safe operation of the vehicle,” Ashok Elluswamy, Tesla’s Vice President of AI Software, wrote on X after the July announcement. “Connectivity is primarily meant for navigation, customer service and, in general, fleet management,” he wrote. Musk’s Sunday post framed the link around passengers, saying it would give riders “high bandwidth everywhere for work and entertainment” once FSD no longer needs supervision. Tesla currently sells its driver-assistance software as FSD (Supervised), which requires an attentive driver. A Dish “Not Intended for In-Motion Use” The Cybercab’s terminal is based on the Starlink V5, which SpaceX introduced in July as a home broadband dish. “Starlink V5 is not intended for in-motion use,” Starlink’s support page says. The V5 delivers download speeds of 375 Mbps or higher, with average power draw of 35 to 50 watts, about half that of its predecessor, according to Starlink. Tesla has not said whether the version fitted to the Cybercab has been adapted to work while the car is moving, or whether the terminal planned for other models will be the same unit. Hardware Without a Connection Cybercabs began coming off the Giga Texas line with the terminal fitted in September, drone footage of the plant showed at the time. At the Cybercab’s launch event in Austin on September 3, Tesla described the cabin as “soon to be equipped with V5 Starlink hardware.” David Moss, who rode for about an hour at the event, reported that “there was no available Starlink connection during any of my rides.” The cars Tesla began offering for public rides in Dallas on November 19 carry the rectangular panel on the rear hatch that marks the terminal. Tesla has not said when riders will be able to connect. Starlink and Tesla The two companies are increasingly intertwined. SpaceX, which runs Starlink, went public in June and trades on the Nasdaq. Musk, who leads both, has declined to rule out a merger between Tesla and SpaceX. On the July call, LightShed Partners analyst Walter Piecyk asked whether Cybercabs could become remote hotspots for Starlink’s mobile service. Musk said Tesla could “use the Starlink terminals that are in the Tesla cars as cell towers.” The Starlink timeline comes as Tesla begins rolling out its FSD V15 software , which Musk said would go to wide release next month . Musk also said on Sunday that Tesla’s cars would stay on the AI4 chip as the next-generation AI5 goes to the Optimus humanoid robot. records.title: 4 EU countries plan joint investigation into Starlink arson attacks, media reports
records.excerpt: Poland, Germany, Lithuania, and Bulgaria plan to establish a joint investigative team to probe arson attacks targeting Starlink satellite communications infrastructure. War 4 EU countries plan joint investigation into Starlink arson attacks, media reports November 23, 2026 3:34 pm • 2 min read Prefer on Google by Léopold Rannou Two men, arrested on suspicion of carrying out an arson attack in September in Poland on a ground station belonging to the Starlink satellite network, are being escorted to their car by police and court officials as they leave the magistrate's court in Nürtingen, Germany, on Oct. 13, 2026 (Jan-Philipp Strobel/picture alliance/Getty Images) Poland, Germany, Lithuania, and Bulgaria plan to establish a joint investigative team to probe arson attacks targeting Starlink satellite communications infrastructure in Bulgaria, Lithuania and Poland, Polish radio RMF24 reported on Nov. 23. Starshield, the militarized version of SpaceX' Starlink satellite internet system, has become a critical communication tool for Ukrainian forces, supporting battlefield coordination and drone operations, making attacks on its infrastructure in Europe a potential threat to networks carrying internet traffic to Ukraine. Prosecutors from the four countries are expected to meet in early December to set up the joint investigative team, RMF24 reported . The team should establish whether the attacks were coordinated by a single group, who carried them out, and who ordered them. On Sept. 23, two masked individuals allegedly set fire to a Starlink ground station in Wola Krobowska , Poland. Polish prosecutors suspect the act was carried out on orders from Russian intelligence to disrupt satellite internet traffic across Central and Eastern Europe. Polish Deputy Prime Minister and Digital Affairs Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski said on Sept. 24 that the Wola Krobowska station, operated by state-owned telecommunications company Exatel, served as an internet hub carrying traffic through Poland, including to Ukraine. Polish authorities charged two Turkish citizens living in Germany with acting on behalf of a foreign intelligence service and committing an act of sabotage. The two suspects had been arrested in Germany on behalf of Polish services on Oct. 10, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said in a post on X . He called the attack "another act of hybrid warfare." Tomasz Siemoniak, the minister coordinating Polish special services, made Russia responsible for the attack, reported AP . "We have no doubt that Russian intelligence services are behind this act of sabotage," he said, according to AP. On Oct. 9, an arson attack was carried out against SpaceX Starlink antennas at the Plana Teleport Facility, south of Bulgaria's capital city, Sofia. records.title: Northrop Grumman Contracts Another Falcon 9 for Cygnus
records.excerpt: Northrop Grumman has signed for another Falcon 9 to fly a Cygnus ISS mission, confirming Antares 330 remains far from flight-ready. Here's what it means. SpaceX Northrop Grumman Contracts Another Falcon 9 for Cygnus — Antares Still Not Ready BASENOR Editorial Desk Nov 23, 2026 Updated November 23, 2026 3 min read Share Northrop Grumman has now contracted a sixth SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket to carry its Cygnus resupply spacecraft to the International Space Station, NASASpaceflight.com reported on November 23, 2026. The move further extends the company's dependence on SpaceX while its own next-generation Antares 330 rocket remains unavailable — with no firm launch date in sight. Source: @SciGuySpace — November 23, 2026 Source: @NASASpaceflight — November 23, 2026 How Falcon 9 Became Cygnus's Default Ride The backstory here starts with the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine. Antares 230+, the rocket Northrop Grumman had used for years to launch Cygnus, relied on Russian-built RD-181 engines and a Ukrainian-built first stage — a supply chain that collapsed overnight when the war began. With no viable path to fly Antares 230+, Northrop Grumman turned to SpaceX. The NG-20 mission marked the first time a Cygnus spacecraft ever launched on a Falcon 9. Since then, the partnership has become routine. NG-21 lifted off on August 4, 2024, delivering more than 8,200 pounds of cargo to the ISS aboard booster B1080 on its tenth flight. NG-23 followed on September 14, 2025, debuting the larger Cygnus XL configuration with 5,000 kilograms of payload. CRS-24 launched on April 11, 2026 — the fourth consecutive Northrop Grumman ISS mission to ride a Falcon 9. The sixth contracted Falcon 9 will extend that streak further still. Antares 330: The Rocket That Keeps Slipping Northrop Grumman has been developing Antares 330 as a clean-sheet replacement for the grounded Antares 230+, designed around domestic engines to eliminate the geopolitical vulnerability that sidelined its predecessor. The program was originally projected to be flight-ready by 2025. That date slipped to 2027, according to reporting from spacepolicyonline.com, and the sixth Falcon 9 contract signals the 2027 target is itself uncertain. The disclosure, attributed to Northrop Grumman's Dave Schiller during a NASA teleconference on November 23, is the clearest public acknowledgment yet that Antares 330 will not be available in time to cover the next Cygnus mission slot. The phrasing matters: contracting a rocket takes months of coordination, and Northrop Grumman would not be spending that money if there were a realistic near-term alternative. What This Means for the ISS Supply Chain For NASA, the practical impact is continuity. Cygnus missions carry pressurized cargo — science experiments, crew supplies, hardware — that the ISS depends on. Keeping that pipeline flowing on Falcon 9 is a known, proven arrangement at this point, and the reliability record Falcon 9 has built over hundreds of consecutive successful missions makes it a low-risk choice for a cargo customer in Northrop Grumman's position. The broader picture, though, is one of growing concentration. SpaceX is now the launch vehicle for both NASA's Commercial Crew program (Crew Dragon) and an expanding share of Commercial Resupply Services missions — roles originally designed to spread work across multiple providers. That was always a structural tension in the CRS framework, and the Antares delays are making it more pronounced. Whether Antares 330 eventually reclaims Cygnus missions or Northrop Grumman continues rolling over Falcon 9 contracts indefinitely will depend on how the development program proceeds from here. For now, the answer is unambiguous: a sixth Falcon 9 is under contract, and there is no firm timeline for anything else. records.excerpt: Mesa Council debates Falcon Field contract before OK | News | themesatribune.com Skip to main content You have permission to edit this article. (YouTube) Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Save Top Story Mesa Council debates Falcon Field contract before OK By CECILIA CHAN, Tribune Managing Editor Nov 23, 2026 23 hrs ago Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Save Council last week awarded a $792,000 contract to a construction company to rehab a vehicle service road at Falcon Field Airport despite one councilwoman’s strong reservations. Councilwoman Dorean Taylor at the Nov. 12 study session asked if the city could delay the project and find another company because she wasn’t happy with Granite Construction’s job performance. “I’m very familiar with Granite,” Taylor said. “They’re doing Southern and Val Vista and it’s been atrocious. It’s probably been one of the worst managed projects I’ve ever seen. They’re gone. They leave the project, they come back, they sub out, they’re very slow. Councilwoman Dorean Taylor raised concerns at the Nov. 12 study session with Granite Construction, which was awarded a contract last week to do work at Falcon Field Airport. (YouTube) “My residents and I both notice there’s barely anybody there. They’ve pushed the project out two months now. “In my opinion completely untrustworthy and I would hate to see us give them essentially an award for a bid. If we can avoid that, that would be fantastic.” Handing the job to Granite Construction, the sole bidder for the project, highlighted the state of the industry. Arizona's construction industry needs 40,000-plus more workers, according to the Arizona Chapter of the Associated General Contractors of America. The skilled labor shortage in the state’s construction industry is driving up project costs, extending timelines and creating severe staffing challenges, the trade association said. Marc Ahlstrom, assistant city engineer, said delaying the project was difficult as federal funding was attached to the project. The project is funded largely by grants from the federal Aviation Administration and the Arizona Department of Transportation. “A delay or a rebid would potentially jeopardize the funding,” Ahlstrom said. Taylor pressed the issue, asking if the city still had time to see if anyone else would be willing to bid on it. Airport Projects and Operations Manager Mark Gibbs detailed the challenge in rebidding the project. “We would have to coordinate with those two granting agencies for permission,” Gibbs said. “They may find some exception if we can’t find a valid reason why Granite Construction is non-performing in terms of its bid on this specific project. I don’t know if other projects that the city has may be a reason for them not to award this particular bidder.” City Manager Scot Butler said the market for contractors was “very competitive.” “This is a challenge not just in Mesa but throughout the region,” he said. “There’s a lot of construction activity going on as you’re all aware around semiconductor infrastructure and other things. “I’ve heard this from other cities as well that it’s a very tough market right now on getting a lot of competitive bids for some of these projects.” Ahlstrom said that especially with projects where the limit is $4 million – the average job order contract across the Valley – there are generally fewer bids. “That’s been the case for the last six or seven years,” Ahlstrom said. “In fact, we’ve had cases where we’ve had no bids on a couple of them.” Taylor said, “I’ve experienced how bad the project has run in my district. “I want it to be very publicly, vocally known that they are causing a lot of strain on the city’s resources, on the district’s residents, and I would hate to see that happen at Falcon Field as well.” Councilwoman Alicia Goforth, whose northeast district encompasses Falcon Field, asked if the city engineer agreed with Taylor’s assessment. “We’re well aware of the issues that Granite has had on the Val Vista Southern project,” Ahlstrom said. “And we are going to have discussions with our legal staff and internally and look at best practices and see if there’s ways to qualify contractors. “But in the past as we’ve looked at that it’s very hard to do with the rules that we are governed by.” He said that Granite has not done any other work at Falcon. The firm also bid to build a new taxiway at Falcon but lost out Nov. 16 to low bidder Sunland Asphalt Construction Co. Butler said if Granite rebid and was the lowest bidder, the city would still need to award it the contract as federal funds are involved. Falcon Field Airport Director Corinne Nystrom pointed out that if the city rebid the project and the bids come in higher, “the FAA and the state will not pay any more than what they’ve already agreed to pay.” Ahlstrom said staff recommended the city proceed with the contract. “My recollection is they have done airport work in other jurisdictions and that they could perform this work,” she said. Mayor Mark Freeman said he also supported moving forward because “if we rebid it and it’s higher then we have to pay the difference. We don’t know what that difference might be but it could be hundreds of thousands of dollars.” The city anticipates the project to take no more than three months to complete. “What does that look like if we have the same experience there as we’re having at Val Vista and Southern?” Taylor asked. Nystrom said it might be a bit of an inconvenience but that another access road could be used. Butler noted that the quality of contractors used for city projects is part of an ongoing dialog. “When we are able to use other construction methods, it gives us more flexibility to partner with firms that have a track record of being able to deliver on time and on budget projects for the city,” Butler said. “Unfortunately, there will be instances where the low bid is mandated by state law or federal law in this case. And so our hands are somewhat tied on this one.” Freeman asked if a contractor doesn’t perform well on a city contract and then bids on another, can Mesa say, “Maybe you’re not the best contractor for future projects?” “Can that be put on our books?” he asked. Ahlstrom said that debarring someone from bidding is hard to do. “In my time at the city, we’ve never debarred anybody from bidding,” Ahlstrom said. “And so we would be working with our city attorney and his staff to see what our options are there.” Butler noted hurdles in that process. “One of the challenges is there is a very high bar in state law and state statute for a contractor to rise to that level that we would be allowed to do that,” Butler said. “The industry has worked very well to delineate a very high standard within state statute that prohibits us from a lot of the flexibility that we’d like to have on projects like this.” Vice Mayor Scott Somers said, “If we debar somebody who’s the only one bidder on certain projects, now we have nobody bidding on projects. “But it does raise the issue, did everybody know that this project was available to be bid on? And so I think what we ought to be looking at is pushing these projects out better.” He said that the city instead should “incentivize better performance.” Butler said he was in total agreement. “Finding ways to incentivize work to be done quicker ahead of schedule, those are all things that we’re looking into,” Butler said. That target sits about 64% above where the stock closed on November 20, 2026, at $127.79. What Jefferies is betting on Managing Director Sheila Kahyaoglu initiated coverage on November 22, 2026. Her thesis rests on two pillars: SpaceX’s engineering strength and its lead in mass-to-orbit launches. Put simply, SpaceX moves more stuff into space than anyone else. Jefferies argues that advantage feeds growth across the company’s space and connectivity businesses, with what the firm expects to be exponential growth in its artificial intelligence efforts on top. The numbers in the note are large. Jefferies projects that SpaceX’s Space segment will generate $9 billion in revenue and $4 billion in EBITDA by 2029. That forecast assumes approximately 315 Starship flights annually, approaching one launch per day. Starship is the company’s next-generation rocket, and Jefferies expects it to increase annual payload capacity by more than 10 times by 2029. However, the firm assumes only around 20% of launches will serve external customers. It expects much of the economic value from increased launch capacity to flow into SpaceX’s downstream businesses rather than launch services alone. The bigger prize, according to Jefferies, is Connectivity, driven primarily by Starlink, the company’s satellite internet service. A rough ride since the IPO SpaceX completed its IPO on June 12, 2026. The offering raised approximately $75 billion to $85.7 billion at a valuation of around $1.77 trillion. The stock trades on Nasdaq under the ticker SPCX. It peaked near $211 to $225 in June 2026, shortly after listing. Then gravity, appropriately, took over. By November 20, shares had slid to $127.79. Notably, the Jefferies target of $210 lands right around the bottom of that June peak range. SpaceX reports results in three segments. Space covers launches, Connectivity covers Starlink, and Super Intelligence covers AI and xAI-related activities. Jefferies is not alone Other Wall Street firms have also turned constructive on the name. Morgan Stanley has a high target of $300 on the stock. Bernstein rates SpaceX Outperform with a $268 price target. Against those, Jefferies’ $210 looks almost conservative. Analysts have also pointed to concrete projects as reasons for confidence. These include the expansion of Starbase, the company’s Texas launch and manufacturing site, as well as planned data-center investments. The data-center plans tie back to the Super Intelligence segment. What this means for investors The Jefferies case depends on execution at enormous scale. An estimated 315 Starship flights annually by 2029 is an ambitious operational target, and any delays to the rocket program would ripple through both launch and Starlink forecasts. The Connectivity projections carry similar weight. A 70% growth rate sustained over several years, with margins above 60%, leaves little room for stumbles in subscriber growth, pricing, or competition. Valuation is the other factor to watch. At a roughly $1.77 trillion IPO valuation, SpaceX started public life already priced like a mature tech giant. Key items to track include Starship flight cadence, Starlink revenue growth, progress at Starbase, and details on data-center spending. Each one maps directly onto a line in the Jefferies model, which makes the coming quarters a running scorecard for this buy call. Disclosure: This article was edited by Vivian Nguyen. Forget Anthropic and SpaceX shares! I’d rather buy this boring UK income stock for its stunning 6.7% yield Image source: Getty Images Harvey Jones Mon, 23 November 2026 at 2:37 am GMT-5 3 min read ANT SPCX MNG.L As investors fixate on the Anthropic IPO, why am I banging on about the delights of this old-school FTSE 100 income stock? I decided to sit out the Anthropic excitement, and I'm glad I did. Its shares behaved much as SpaceX did, soaring on the initial hype before becoming volatile as underlying worries about AI swept back with a vengeance. By contrast to Anthropic and SpaceX, this UK blue-chip hasn't flown to the stars and back and that's a key reason why I like it. Another's that it's been giving me a fantastic rate of income, with share price growth on top. I love my M&G shares I had high hopes when I added wealth manager M&G ( LSE: MNG ) to my Self-Invested Personal Pension (SIPP) in spring 2023, and it's exceeded all of them. The stock was actually yielding 10%. A sky-high yield like that can be a warning sign, but I felt the shares had been overlooked and the company was good for its dividends. Somebody who invested £10,000 lump into this stock five years ago would now have £20,992. The shares grew 63% but reinvested dividends lifted the total return to 110%. M&G had its own IPO in October 2019, when it was spun off from FTSE 100 insurer Prudential . Its early years were also bumpy, as investor uncertainty and concerns about its prospects hit the share price and drove up that yield. Lately, it's had a much better run, albeit with volatility along the way. Buying opportunity? The shares have dipped 12% in the last three months, but are still up 17% over one year. I think this may be creating a buying opportunity. Sadly, the dividend isn't in double digits any more, but it's still 6.7%, one of the highest on the FTSE 100. The board's targeting annual dividend growth of 2%. Unfortunately, that's now below inflation, currently 3.6% and expected to rise further. That's a blow, as it means the dividend will shrink slightly in real terms. But given its high starting point, that's not the end of the world. And with luck, inflation will fall at some point. We'll see. The shares have also become more expensive after their strong run, but the forward price-to-earnings ratio's a modest 10.4. A dividend machine There are risks to every stock, including this one. If we get a wider AI or stock market crash , that could hit the value of assets under management, reduce customer inflows, increase outflows and cut commission-based fee income. M&G also operates in a fiercely competitive market, facing pressure from cheaper passive investment providers and rivals chasing the same institutional and private-market clients. Yet with that valuation and high yield, I think it's worth considering for the long term. It's the type of stock to buy and hold for years, hoping its dividends compound steadily and the shares enjoy the odd growth spurt. The income should come in handy in retirement. I'll be looking to take advantage if the shares dip further, locking in an even higher yield.
